26	# Adversarial review findings
27	
28	One thing not to relitigate: keeping Codex `memories=true` is correct because disabling it kills chronicle; ADR 0007 lines 22 and 34 align with the stated constraint.
29	
30	## CRITICAL
31	
32	### C1 — Cache golden rule is violated by “core re-render at SessionStart + compaction”
33	
34	**Failure scenario:**
35	A same-cwd Pi/Claude/Codex session starts after a previous session caused harvest/consolidation. The harness re-renders its cached core from `~/.agents/memory`, which now contains new harvested/native/canonical facts. The cached prefix changes byte-for-byte even though the cwd is the same. That re-bills the whole prefix. “Deterministically rendered” does not save this; deterministic rendering of changing inputs still changes bytes.
36	
37	The design makes this likely in three places: harvest happens on SessionStart/Stop, canonical memory mutates, then the core is re-rendered at SessionStart or compaction. If any canonical data, tombstone state, provenance, qmd result, dedup decision, or native self-injected digest affects core rendering, the cached prefix becomes per-session variable.
38	
39	**Attacks:**
40	ADR 0008 lines 16, 21, 38–39; spec lines 42, 46, 48, 50; ADR 0007 lines 22, 24.
41	
42	**Concrete fix:**
43	Split “core” into a **versioned, explicitly promoted cache-base snapshot**, not a live render of canonical memory. The cached prefix renderer must read only `core-snapshots/<harness>/<cwd-or-scope>/<base_epoch>.md`, with a stable manifest and byte-for-byte snapshot tests. Harvest, qmd, dedup, tombstones, consolidation, and native-memory changes may affect only appended recall until an explicit cache-base epoch bump is accepted. Add a test that starts two same-cwd sessions while canonical memory changes between them and asserts identical `system + tools[]` bytes.
44	
45	---
46	
47	### C2 — The spec risks reviving dream-memory as a Pi model-facing injector, contradicting the 2026-06-10 decision
48	
49	**Failure scenario:**
50	The implementation follows the spec diagram and lets `extensions/dream-memory` perform “inject: core @ SessionStart+compaction / recall @ turn” for all harnesses, including Pi. That puts dream-memory back into Pi’s model-facing injection path. If it touches Pi’s cached base, it directly violates the prior decision. Even if it only injects tail recall, `memory-architecture.md` explicitly required a single-owner injection guard before dream-memory re-adds model-facing recall.
51	
52	The ADR text says each harness keeps its own injector, but the implementation spec diagram centralizes “inject” under the bridge. That ambiguity is dangerous because the owner extension is listed as `dream-memory` plus `pi-memory`, and P5 says the bridge gains compaction subscriptions.
53	
54	**Attacks:**
55	`memory-architecture.md` lines 35–41; ADR 0007 lines 18, 36; ADR 0008 line 25; spec lines 5, 15, 30–33, 50.
56	
57	**Concrete fix:**
58	State this as a hard interface rule: for Pi, `dream-memory` may compute recall candidates but **must not inject** into Pi’s cached base or transcript. `pi-memory` remains the sole Pi model-facing injector for both core and recall tail. Add a single-owner injection guard that scans final Pi `system`, tool definitions, SessionStart messages, and recall custom messages for duplicate/dream-owned memory blocks before every release.
59	
60	---
61	
62	### C3 — “Single writer” is false at the semantic level; the design keeps multiple model-facing memory authorities alive
63	
64	**Failure scenario:**
65	Claude Code native memory records “use yarn for repo X.” The bridge harvests it into canonical. Later Pi corrects the canonical fact to “use pnpm for repo X.” Claude Code still self-injects the stale native “yarn” memory because the bridge never writes back. The bridge then injects canonical recall. The model sees both facts. Worse, the embedding “minus self” backstop may suppress the canonical correction because it is similar to the self-injected stale fact. Claude then re-learns or re-writes the stale fact from its own prompt, and the bridge harvests it again.
66	
67	That is the old multi-writer anti-pattern through the back door: native stores still write, native injectors still speak, the canonical store writes, and the bridge recall also speaks. Calling the bridge the “single writer of canonical consolidated record” is too narrow to prevent semantic drift.
68	
69	There is also a direct textual contradiction: the architecture diagram says “Pi writes canonical directly,” while the ADR says the dream bridge is the single writer of the canonical consolidated record.
70	
71	**Attacks:**
72	ADR 0007 lines 18, 22, 24; spec lines 20–33, especially lines 21–25 and 46–48; `memory-architecture.md` lines 39–41.
73	
74	**Concrete fix:**
75	Define three separate write classes:
76	
77	1. **Raw capture writers** may write only append-only events into `inbox/raw/<origin>/`.
78	2. **Canonical consolidated writer** is one bridge process under a global lock.
79	3. **Model-facing injectors** are single-owner per harness.
80	
81	Pi must not “write canonical directly” unless “canonical” means append-only inbox. Native self-injected memories must be treated as untrusted external input. Do not suppress canonical corrections by embedding similarity. If canonical contradicts self-injected native memory, inject an explicit appended correction/override until the native source stops surfacing the stale fact.
82	
83	---
84	
85	### C4 — “Global minus self” can leak byte-unstable per-session state into cached core
86	
87	**Failure scenario:**
88	The bridge computes “canonical minus what X already self-injects.” But “what X already self-injects” is not stable. Claude Code and Codex native memories can change between sessions. Pi’s profile snapshot can change after consolidation. If this subtraction is used anywhere in the core render path, the cached prefix changes based on native memory state, qmd index state, similarity scores, ordering, or SessionStart harvest results.
89	
90	The spec says “Dedup-on-inject + per-harness scope” without limiting it to volatile recall. The diagram also places core and recall under a single “inject” block. That is enough ambiguity for an implementer to run global-minus-self before rendering both core and recall.
91	
92	**Attacks:**
93	ADR 0007 line 24; ADR 0008 lines 16–23; spec lines 30–33, 46, 48, 50; `recall-routing.ts` lines 16–21.
94	
95	**Concrete fix:**
96	Make this rule explicit: **global-minus-self is tail-recall only. It must never influence cached core bytes.** Core dedup must be manifest-based and snapshot-based, not qmd/embedding/native-self based. For recall, “minus self” should use exact source IDs or exact normalized text hashes first. Embedding similarity may rank candidates, but must not delete/suppress corrections or scoped distinctions.
97	
98	---
99	
100	### C5 — Migration can silently corrupt or lose data; union-count reconciliation is not a data-loss gate
101	
102	**Failure scenario:**
103	The migration pushes disjoint stores plus a 267 KB Codex `MEMORY.md` and 438 KB `raw_memories.md` through an LLM patch engine. The LLM false-merges distinct facts, rewrites scoped facts into global facts, drops weakly worded facts, or converts a correction into an update without preserving the contradicted source. The output still has roughly the expected file count, so “union-count reconciliation” passes while semantic data is lost.
104	
105	Examples of false merges:
106	
107	* “Use pnpm in repo A” and “Use yarn in legacy repo B” become “prefer pnpm.”
108	* “Nadya is the user’s girlfriend” and “Nadya is involved in project planning” become one vague personal note.
109	* “Do not expose client secrets in Claude” and “Codex captured a client token” become a generic security preference, losing the incident provenance.
110	* Two files with different filenames but same topic are treated as duplicates despite different scope or recency.
111	
112	A partial apply is also under-specified. If the patch engine crashes halfway through apply, the canonical store may contain half-migrated records and a qmd index built over inconsistent data. A rerun may generate different patches, so “idempotent re-run is a no-op” is an aspiration, not a mechanism.
113	
114	**Attacks:**
115	ADR 0007 lines 8, 43; spec lines 42–44, 56–58.
116	
117	**Concrete fix:**
118	Do not use file-count reconciliation. Build a **claim-level migration ledger**:
119	
120	* Extract atomic claims with source store, path, line/offset span, content hash, timestamp if available, and scope.
121	* Every source claim must map to one canonical record, one conflict group, or one explicit quarantine/reject decision.
122	* Canonical IDs must be content-addressed or ledger-assigned, not LLM-invented.
123	* Apply must be transactional: write to a temp tree, validate, atomically swap, retain rollback snapshot, then rebuild qmd.
124	* Reruns must use the ledger and source hashes, not fresh LLM judgment.
125	* Huge files must be chunked with source spans preserved; the LLM may propose merges, but it must not be the authority for deletion.
126	
127	---
128	
129	### C6 — PII/secrets can cross harness boundaries through `shared/`
130	
131	**Failure scenario:**
132	Codex captures an API key, local credential path, client name, private commercial detail, or screen-memory snippet via chronicle. The bridge harvests it, classifies it as `shared/`, indexes it, and later injects it into Claude Code or Pi. Now a secret captured in one harness becomes context in another harness, possibly with different tools, different logs, different model provider exposure, and different retention behavior.
133	
134	The proposed namespaces are functional, not security boundaries. There is no redaction layer, no default-private policy, no secret scanner, no per-harness ACL, no client/project isolation rule, and no injection allowlist.
135	
136	**Attacks:**
137	ADR 0007 lines 16, 22, 24, 43; spec lines 20–36, 44, 46, 48, 63.
138	
139	**Concrete fix:**
140	Default all harvested native memories to `inbox/quarantine/<origin>/`, not `shared/`. Promotion to `shared/` must require classification. Add secret scanning before indexing and before injection: API keys, tokens, private keys, env vars, credentials, client identifiers, payment/legal/medical content, screen captures, and local paths. Add memory ACL metadata: `visibility: private | harness:<x> | project:<slug> | shared`, plus `sensitivity`. The recall layer must enforce ACLs before qmd ranking and again before final injection.
141	
142	---
143	
144	## HIGH
145	
146	### H1 — Native self-injection plus embedding dedup can suppress the exact correction the model needs
147	
148	**Failure scenario:**
149	Codex self-injects “the database is Postgres.” Canonical memory says “correction: production moved to MySQL.” The embedding backstop sees these as similar database facts and subtracts the canonical correction as “already self-injected.” The model keeps acting on stale native memory.
150	
151	This is especially dangerous because corrections, negations, dates, numbers, and scope changes are often embedding-near the stale fact they replace.
152	
153	**Attacks:**
154	ADR 0007 line 24; spec line 48.
155	
156	**Concrete fix:**
157	Embedding similarity must never be a deletion/suppression authority. It can only mark “possible duplicate.” Suppression requires exact canonical source ID, exact normalized text hash, or an entailment check that proves the self-injected fact entails the canonical fact. If the candidate contains negation, correction language, dates, numbers, repo names, tool names, or project scope, default to injecting it.
158	
159	---
160	
161	### H2 — “Compaction bounds the staleness window” is false
162	
163	**Failure scenario:**
164	A stale core fact says “it is acceptable to edit production data directly.” The user corrects it mid-session. The stale line remains in the cached prefix. Recall appends “correction: never edit production directly.” The model now sees a contradiction between a high-priority stable prefix and a later volatile correction. Depending on placement and model behavior, it may follow the stale instruction, oscillate, or waste turns resolving the conflict.
165	
166	For Codex, ADR 0008 already admits compaction likely does not exist and degrades to SessionStart-only refresh. For Pi, the compaction hook is unverified. For any harness, compaction is non-deterministic and may not occur before the harmful action. Therefore compaction does not bound staleness in any reliable engineering sense.
167	
168	**Attacks:**
169	ADR 0008 lines 16, 34, 38–39; spec lines 50, 65.
170	
171	**Concrete fix:**
172	Do not put high-risk mutable facts in cached core. Core should contain only durable, low-volatility preferences and identity facts. Corrections, removals, security rules, project state, tool choices, credentials, and “do not do X” facts belong in tail recall or an emergency revocation block. Add a “critical revocation” mechanism that appends a high-priority tail block every turn and optionally forces a new session/base epoch for affected harnesses.
173	
174	---
175	
176	### H3 — The qmd re-point plan can break existing Pi recall because `recall-routing.ts` still encodes the old world
177	
178	**Failure scenario:**
179	P1 re-points qmd to canonical collections, but active recall still defaults to `pi-memory`, `scars`, and `changes`. It explicitly excludes `dream-memory-profile` and `dream-memory-project` because those were “already injected deterministically every session.” After cutover, that assumption may no longer hold, or it may hold differently per harness. Result: Pi recall silently misses canonical memories, double-injects old/new duplicates during dual-read, or continues querying stale `~/.pi/agent/memory` while the canonical corpus is the intended source of truth.
180	
181	The source-of-truth router has no concept of `shared/`, `harness/{claude,codex,pi}/`, `episodic/`, migration dual-read, or per-harness scope.
182	
183	**Attacks:**
184	`recall-routing.ts` lines 16–27, 92–103, 133–160; spec lines 42, 48, 54.
185	
186	**Concrete fix:**
187	Update routing before qmd cutover. Add explicit collection names and aliases for canonical memory, old pi-memory, old dream-memory, scars, changes, workspace, and project-docs. During dual-read, return both old and new with source IDs and duplicate suppression in the tail only. Add regression tests for: existing Pi recall, migrated canonical recall, no duplicate profile/project recall, and per-harness scoping.
188	
189	---
190	
191	### H4 — Cross-harness concurrent writes are not designed
192	
193	**Failure scenario:**
194	A Pi write-path repoint, a Claude SessionStop harvest watcher, and a Codex SessionStart harvest watcher all run close together. They each diff source dirs, produce patches, and mutate `~/.agents/memory`. One process writes a file while another reads it for qmd indexing. A tombstone and an update race. The final canonical tree contains partial frontmatter, lost updates, duplicated records, or an index built over a half-written state.
195	
196	The old Pi architecture had a per-scope lock. The new canonical design names no lock, no transaction log, no atomic write protocol, and no index rebuild ordering.
197	
198	**Attacks:**
199	`memory-architecture.md` lines 90–98; ADR 0007 lines 18, 22, 43; spec lines 23–25, 44, 46, 50.
200	
201	**Concrete fix:**
202	Add a global canonical-store write lock plus scope locks. All mutations go through a write-ahead log. File writes must be temp-file + fsync + atomic rename. qmd indexing must consume committed snapshots only. Harvesters should enqueue work; one consolidator applies patches. Add crash-recovery tests that kill the process during apply and verify clean rollback or clean resume.
203	
204	---
205	
206	### H5 — The build-vs-buy decision is not supported by the proposed evidence
207	
208	**Failure scenario:**
209	The team rejects Mem0/Letta because the in-house bridge already has the desired components. Then P6 runs offline snapshot-replay against the canonical corpus shaped by the in-house system and records overlap@5/rank-correlation. The result “proves” the own stack is better because the benchmark measures retrieval overlap on a corpus, schema, and memory taxonomy already optimized for the own stack. It does not test live extraction quality, correction handling, privacy filtering, stale suppression, cache churn, operational complexity, latency under real traffic, or whether an external system with an adapter could satisfy the cache contract.
210	
211	**Attacks:**

# Adversarial review findings

One thing not to relitigate: keeping Codex `memories=true` is correct because disabling it kills chronicle; ADR 0007 lines 22 and 34 align with the stated constraint.

## CRITICAL

### C1 — Cache golden rule is violated by “core re-render at SessionStart + compaction”

**Failure scenario:**
A same-cwd Pi/Claude/Codex session starts after a previous session caused harvest/consolidation. The harness re-renders its cached core from `~/.agents/memory`, which now contains new harvested/native/canonical facts. The cached prefix changes byte-for-byte even though the cwd is the same. That re-bills the whole prefix. “Deterministically rendered” does not save this; deterministic rendering of changing inputs still changes bytes.

The design makes this likely in three places: harvest happens on SessionStart/Stop, canonical memory mutates, then the core is re-rendered at SessionStart or compaction. If any canonical data, tombstone state, provenance, qmd result, dedup decision, or native self-injected digest affects core rendering, the cached prefix becomes per-session variable.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0008 lines 16, 21, 38–39; spec lines 42, 46, 48, 50; ADR 0007 lines 22, 24.

**Concrete fix:**
Split “core” into a **versioned, explicitly promoted cache-base snapshot**, not a live render of canonical memory. The cached prefix renderer must read only `core-snapshots/<harness>/<cwd-or-scope>/<base_epoch>.md`, with a stable manifest and byte-for-byte snapshot tests. Harvest, qmd, dedup, tombstones, consolidation, and native-memory changes may affect only appended recall until an explicit cache-base epoch bump is accepted. Add a test that starts two same-cwd sessions while canonical memory changes between them and asserts identical `system + tools[]` bytes.

---

### C2 — The spec risks reviving dream-memory as a Pi model-facing injector, contradicting the 2026-06-10 decision

**Failure scenario:**
The implementation follows the spec diagram and lets `extensions/dream-memory` perform “inject: core @ SessionStart+compaction / recall @ turn” for all harnesses, including Pi. That puts dream-memory back into Pi’s model-facing injection path. If it touches Pi’s cached base, it directly violates the prior decision. Even if it only injects tail recall, `memory-architecture.md` explicitly required a single-owner injection guard before dream-memory re-adds model-facing recall.

The ADR text says each harness keeps its own injector, but the implementation spec diagram centralizes “inject” under the bridge. That ambiguity is dangerous because the owner extension is listed as `dream-memory` plus `pi-memory`, and P5 says the bridge gains compaction subscriptions.

**Attacks:**
`memory-architecture.md` lines 35–41; ADR 0007 lines 18, 36; ADR 0008 line 25; spec lines 5, 15, 30–33, 50.

**Concrete fix:**
State this as a hard interface rule: for Pi, `dream-memory` may compute recall candidates but **must not inject** into Pi’s cached base or transcript. `pi-memory` remains the sole Pi model-facing injector for both core and recall tail. Add a single-owner injection guard that scans final Pi `system`, tool definitions, SessionStart messages, and recall custom messages for duplicate/dream-owned memory blocks before every release.

---

### C3 — “Single writer” is false at the semantic level; the design keeps multiple model-facing memory authorities alive

**Failure scenario:**
Claude Code native memory records “use yarn for repo X.” The bridge harvests it into canonical. Later Pi corrects the canonical fact to “use pnpm for repo X.” Claude Code still self-injects the stale native “yarn” memory because the bridge never writes back. The bridge then injects canonical recall. The model sees both facts. Worse, the embedding “minus self” backstop may suppress the canonical correction because it is similar to the self-injected stale fact. Claude then re-learns or re-writes the stale fact from its own prompt, and the bridge harvests it again.

That is the old multi-writer anti-pattern through the back door: native stores still write, native injectors still speak, the canonical store writes, and the bridge recall also speaks. Calling the bridge the “single writer of canonical consolidated record” is too narrow to prevent semantic drift.

There is also a direct textual contradiction: the architecture diagram says “Pi writes canonical directly,” while the ADR says the dream bridge is the single writer of the canonical consolidated record.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 18, 22, 24; spec lines 20–33, especially lines 21–25 and 46–48; `memory-architecture.md` lines 39–41.

**Concrete fix:**
Define three separate write classes:

1. **Raw capture writers** may write only append-only events into `inbox/raw/<origin>/`.
2. **Canonical consolidated writer** is one bridge process under a global lock.
3. **Model-facing injectors** are single-owner per harness.

Pi must not “write canonical directly” unless “canonical” means append-only inbox. Native self-injected memories must be treated as untrusted external input. Do not suppress canonical corrections by embedding similarity. If canonical contradicts self-injected native memory, inject an explicit appended correction/override until the native source stops surfacing the stale fact.

---

### C4 — “Global minus self” can leak byte-unstable per-session state into cached core

**Failure scenario:**
The bridge computes “canonical minus what X already self-injects.” But “what X already self-injects” is not stable. Claude Code and Codex native memories can change between sessions. Pi’s profile snapshot can change after consolidation. If this subtraction is used anywhere in the core render path, the cached prefix changes based on native memory state, qmd index state, similarity scores, ordering, or SessionStart harvest results.

The spec says “Dedup-on-inject + per-harness scope” without limiting it to volatile recall. The diagram also places core and recall under a single “inject” block. That is enough ambiguity for an implementer to run global-minus-self before rendering both core and recall.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 line 24; ADR 0008 lines 16–23; spec lines 30–33, 46, 48, 50; `recall-routing.ts` lines 16–21.

**Concrete fix:**
Make this rule explicit: **global-minus-self is tail-recall only. It must never influence cached core bytes.** Core dedup must be manifest-based and snapshot-based, not qmd/embedding/native-self based. For recall, “minus self” should use exact source IDs or exact normalized text hashes first. Embedding similarity may rank candidates, but must not delete/suppress corrections or scoped distinctions.

---

### C5 — Migration can silently corrupt or lose data; union-count reconciliation is not a data-loss gate

**Failure scenario:**
The migration pushes disjoint stores plus a 267 KB Codex `MEMORY.md` and 438 KB `raw_memories.md` through an LLM patch engine. The LLM false-merges distinct facts, rewrites scoped facts into global facts, drops weakly worded facts, or converts a correction into an update without preserving the contradicted source. The output still has roughly the expected file count, so “union-count reconciliation” passes while semantic data is lost.

Examples of false merges:

* “Use pnpm in repo A” and “Use yarn in legacy repo B” become “prefer pnpm.”
* “Nadya is the user’s girlfriend” and “Nadya is involved in project planning” become one vague personal note.
* “Do not expose client secrets in Claude” and “Codex captured a client token” become a generic security preference, losing the incident provenance.
* Two files with different filenames but same topic are treated as duplicates despite different scope or recency.

A partial apply is also under-specified. If the patch engine crashes halfway through apply, the canonical store may contain half-migrated records and a qmd index built over inconsistent data. A rerun may generate different patches, so “idempotent re-run is a no-op” is an aspiration, not a mechanism.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 8, 43; spec lines 42–44, 56–58.

**Concrete fix:**
Do not use file-count reconciliation. Build a **claim-level migration ledger**:

* Extract atomic claims with source store, path, line/offset span, content hash, timestamp if available, and scope.
* Every source claim must map to one canonical record, one conflict group, or one explicit quarantine/reject decision.
* Canonical IDs must be content-addressed or ledger-assigned, not LLM-invented.
* Apply must be transactional: write to a temp tree, validate, atomically swap, retain rollback snapshot, then rebuild qmd.
* Reruns must use the ledger and source hashes, not fresh LLM judgment.
* Huge files must be chunked with source spans preserved; the LLM may propose merges, but it must not be the authority for deletion.

---

### C6 — PII/secrets can cross harness boundaries through `shared/`

**Failure scenario:**
Codex captures an API key, local credential path, client name, private commercial detail, or screen-memory snippet via chronicle. The bridge harvests it, classifies it as `shared/`, indexes it, and later injects it into Claude Code or Pi. Now a secret captured in one harness becomes context in another harness, possibly with different tools, different logs, different model provider exposure, and different retention behavior.

The proposed namespaces are functional, not security boundaries. There is no redaction layer, no default-private policy, no secret scanner, no per-harness ACL, no client/project isolation rule, and no injection allowlist.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 16, 22, 24, 43; spec lines 20–36, 44, 46, 48, 63.

**Concrete fix:**
Default all harvested native memories to `inbox/quarantine/<origin>/`, not `shared/`. Promotion to `shared/` must require classification. Add secret scanning before indexing and before injection: API keys, tokens, private keys, env vars, credentials, client identifiers, payment/legal/medical content, screen captures, and local paths. Add memory ACL metadata: `visibility: private | harness:<x> | project:<slug> | shared`, plus `sensitivity`. The recall layer must enforce ACLs before qmd ranking and again before final injection.

---

## HIGH

### H1 — Native self-injection plus embedding dedup can suppress the exact correction the model needs

**Failure scenario:**
Codex self-injects “the database is Postgres.” Canonical memory says “correction: production moved to MySQL.” The embedding backstop sees these as similar database facts and subtracts the canonical correction as “already self-injected.” The model keeps acting on stale native memory.

This is especially dangerous because corrections, negations, dates, numbers, and scope changes are often embedding-near the stale fact they replace.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 line 24; spec line 48.

**Concrete fix:**
Embedding similarity must never be a deletion/suppression authority. It can only mark “possible duplicate.” Suppression requires exact canonical source ID, exact normalized text hash, or an entailment check that proves the self-injected fact entails the canonical fact. If the candidate contains negation, correction language, dates, numbers, repo names, tool names, or project scope, default to injecting it.

---

### H2 — “Compaction bounds the staleness window” is false

**Failure scenario:**
A stale core fact says “it is acceptable to edit production data directly.” The user corrects it mid-session. The stale line remains in the cached prefix. Recall appends “correction: never edit production directly.” The model now sees a contradiction between a high-priority stable prefix and a later volatile correction. Depending on placement and model behavior, it may follow the stale instruction, oscillate, or waste turns resolving the conflict.

For Codex, ADR 0008 already admits compaction likely does not exist and degrades to SessionStart-only refresh. For Pi, the compaction hook is unverified. For any harness, compaction is non-deterministic and may not occur before the harmful action. Therefore compaction does not bound staleness in any reliable engineering sense.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0008 lines 16, 34, 38–39; spec lines 50, 65.

**Concrete fix:**
Do not put high-risk mutable facts in cached core. Core should contain only durable, low-volatility preferences and identity facts. Corrections, removals, security rules, project state, tool choices, credentials, and “do not do X” facts belong in tail recall or an emergency revocation block. Add a “critical revocation” mechanism that appends a high-priority tail block every turn and optionally forces a new session/base epoch for affected harnesses.

---

### H3 — The qmd re-point plan can break existing Pi recall because `recall-routing.ts` still encodes the old world

**Failure scenario:**
P1 re-points qmd to canonical collections, but active recall still defaults to `pi-memory`, `scars`, and `changes`. It explicitly excludes `dream-memory-profile` and `dream-memory-project` because those were “already injected deterministically every session.” After cutover, that assumption may no longer hold, or it may hold differently per harness. Result: Pi recall silently misses canonical memories, double-injects old/new duplicates during dual-read, or continues querying stale `~/.pi/agent/memory` while the canonical corpus is the intended source of truth.

The source-of-truth router has no concept of `shared/`, `harness/{claude,codex,pi}/`, `episodic/`, migration dual-read, or per-harness scope.

**Attacks:**
`recall-routing.ts` lines 16–27, 92–103, 133–160; spec lines 42, 48, 54.

**Concrete fix:**
Update routing before qmd cutover. Add explicit collection names and aliases for canonical memory, old pi-memory, old dream-memory, scars, changes, workspace, and project-docs. During dual-read, return both old and new with source IDs and duplicate suppression in the tail only. Add regression tests for: existing Pi recall, migrated canonical recall, no duplicate profile/project recall, and per-harness scoping.

---

### H4 — Cross-harness concurrent writes are not designed

**Failure scenario:**
A Pi write-path repoint, a Claude SessionStop harvest watcher, and a Codex SessionStart harvest watcher all run close together. They each diff source dirs, produce patches, and mutate `~/.agents/memory`. One process writes a file while another reads it for qmd indexing. A tombstone and an update race. The final canonical tree contains partial frontmatter, lost updates, duplicated records, or an index built over a half-written state.

The old Pi architecture had a per-scope lock. The new canonical design names no lock, no transaction log, no atomic write protocol, and no index rebuild ordering.

**Attacks:**
`memory-architecture.md` lines 90–98; ADR 0007 lines 18, 22, 43; spec lines 23–25, 44, 46, 50.

**Concrete fix:**
Add a global canonical-store write lock plus scope locks. All mutations go through a write-ahead log. File writes must be temp-file + fsync + atomic rename. qmd indexing must consume committed snapshots only. Harvesters should enqueue work; one consolidator applies patches. Add crash-recovery tests that kill the process during apply and verify clean rollback or clean resume.

---

### H5 — The build-vs-buy decision is not supported by the proposed evidence

**Failure scenario:**
The team rejects Mem0/Letta because the in-house bridge already has the desired components. Then P6 runs offline snapshot-replay against the canonical corpus shaped by the in-house system and records overlap@5/rank-correlation. The result “proves” the own stack is better because the benchmark measures retrieval overlap on a corpus, schema, and memory taxonomy already optimized for the own stack. It does not test live extraction quality, correction handling, privacy filtering, stale suppression, cache churn, operational complexity, latency under real traffic, or whether an external system with an adapter could satisfy the cache contract.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 20, 26, 32–33, 42; spec lines 52, 56–58.

**Concrete fix:**
Define falsification criteria. Example: run Mem0/Letta as non-injecting live shadows over the same raw event stream, with the same privacy filters and no access to canonical labels. Compare against blinded human judgments on recall usefulness, correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, wrong-action prevention, write precision, latency, cost, and cache-base churn. Offline snapshot-replay may remain a smoke test, but it is not sufficient evidence for “do not adopt.”

---

### H6 — Namespacing semantics are contradictory: “global minus self” is not the same as `shared ∪ harness/X`

**Failure scenario:**
A Codex session learns a generally useful build fact. It lands under `harness/codex` because its origin is Codex. Pi never recalls it because Pi’s scope is `shared ∪ harness/pi`. Alternatively, the system promotes too much into `shared/` to make cross-harness recall work, and Pi starts receiving Claude/Codex-specific tool noise.

The design lacks a promotion policy from origin-specific to shared semantic memory. “Origin harness” is provenance; it is not the same thing as “visibility scope.”

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 16, 22, 24; spec lines 36, 48, 63.

**Concrete fix:**
Separate metadata fields:

* `origin`: where it was captured.
* `visibility`: where it may be injected.
* `scope`: profile/project/tool/harness/client.
* `confidence`: extracted/consolidated/confirmed.
* `sensitivity`: public/private/secret.

Do not infer visibility from origin. New harvested facts default to origin-private until promoted by rules or review.

---

### H7 — The ADR relies on retired/dead dream-memory code as if it were production-ready

**Failure scenario:**
ADR 0007 says the dream bridge already normalizes hook payloads and owns extract → consolidate → index → recall. But `memory-architecture.md` says dream-memory is retired, in no profile manifest, and `harness-cli.ts` is dead code. The implementation then builds a critical canonical memory system on code paths that are not currently live, not soak-tested, and may not obey the newer cache constraints.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 line 12; `memory-architecture.md` lines 23–31, 35–41.

**Concrete fix:**
Add a requalification phase before migration. Treat dream-memory as legacy code until proven otherwise. Required gates: live harness hook normalization tests for Pi/Claude/Codex, patch-applier idempotency tests, qmd index tests, recall injection ownership tests, cache-byte stability tests, and dead-code removal or explicit reactivation under feature flags.

---

### H8 — Open questions are not peripheral; they are core architecture decisions

**Failure scenario:**
The spec is accepted while leaving unresolved whether Pi exposes compaction, whether a fork hook is required, and whether `pi-memory` becomes a thin shim or full write-path repoint. These are not implementation details. They determine cache safety, injection ownership, and whether the single-writer claim is true.

**Attacks:**
Spec lines 60–66; ADR 0008 lines 38–39; ADR 0007 lines 18, 22.

**Concrete fix:**
Demote the ADRs from “Accepted” to “Proposed” or add blocking preconditions. Resolve Pi compaction availability, Pi write-path ownership, and injection ownership before P1/P2. Do not start migration until these are nailed down.

---

## MEDIUM

### M1 — Tombstones and qmd indexing are under-specified

**Failure scenario:**
A memory is soft-invalidated with a tombstone. The physical file remains until consolidation. qmd indexes the stale file or continues returning an old embedding. Recall appends the deleted fact because the retrieval layer is not tombstone-aware. The cached prefix may stay stable, but model behavior remains stale.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0008 lines 21–23, 39; spec line 50.

**Concrete fix:**
Tombstones must be first-class in the retrieval layer. qmd indexing must either exclude tombstoned records or include tombstone metadata and filter before ranking. Add tests: deleted memory must not appear in recall, even before physical prune; correction memory must outrank the tombstoned predecessor.

---

### M2 — Provenance is too weak for migration, dedup, audit, and rollback

**Failure scenario:**
Two stores contain `MEMORY.md`, multiple project dirs use similar slugs, and paths are normalized differently across machines. “Origin harness + capture path” collides or becomes unstable after move/rename. The system cannot prove which source claim produced which canonical memory. Later, dedup or rollback deletes the wrong record.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 22, 24, 43; spec lines 36, 44.

**Concrete fix:**
Use structured provenance: `source_store`, `source_path`, `source_span`, `source_content_hash`, `source_record_id`, `migration_batch_id`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `origin_harness`, and `capture_mechanism`. Keep provenance out of cached core rendering unless explicitly stripped and normalized.

---

### M3 — Chronicle-to-episodic ingestion lacks a safety and promotion policy

**Failure scenario:**
Chronicle screen summaries are ingested into `episodic/`. They include transient screen state, secrets, client data, or misread UI context. Later a promotion process turns episodic data into durable semantic memory, or recall surfaces episodic details into another harness. The design only asks when a screen summary “earns durable memory”; it does not define what must never be promoted or injected.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 22, 43; spec lines 44, 63.

**Concrete fix:**
Chronicle ingestion must default to private, low-confidence, non-shared, non-core, non-promotable until classified. Add TTLs. Require explicit promotion rules for episodic → semantic. Secret/PII scanning must run before qmd indexing and before any injection.

---

### M4 — “Core frozen until compaction” creates contradiction windows that the model cannot reliably resolve

**Failure scenario:**
The core says “the user prefers concise answers.” The recall tail says “for this project, produce exhaustive reports.” This is mild. But the same pattern applies to safety, credentials, deployment rules, legal/client constraints, or financial data. The model receives two contradictory memory authorities in one prompt. The design assumes appended recall can correct stale core, but it cannot unsend or demote the stale prefix line.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0008 lines 16, 21, 34, 39.

**Concrete fix:**
Add memory mutability classes. Only low-risk stable facts may enter core. Anything likely to change or cause harm must stay in recall. Corrections should include explicit supersession metadata: `supersedes`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, `scope`, and `confidence`.

---

### M5 — P7’s “30-session soak or metric parity” is too late for the dangerous failures

**Failure scenario:**
The system migrates, starts harvesting, and only at cutover runs a soak. By then source stores may have been partially migrated, qmd repointed, native harvesters running, and canonical memory influencing recall. Data loss, cache churn, and cross-harness leakage may already have occurred.

**Attacks:**
Spec lines 38–54, 56–58.

**Concrete fix:**
Move hard gates earlier. Before P2 apply: claim-level migration verification and rollback test. Before P3: lock/crash test. Before P4: no false suppression tests. Before P5: byte-stability tests across same-cwd sessions. Before any cross-harness recall: secret/PII isolation tests.

---

## LOW

### L1 — The wording “CC native” vs `harness/claude` invites namespace mistakes

**Failure scenario:**
One part of the system writes `harness/cc`, another reads `harness/claude`, and a third labels it `claude-code`. Memories disappear from recall or are incorrectly promoted to `shared/`.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 16, 24; spec lines 21, 26, 36.

**Concrete fix:**
Define canonical harness IDs in one enum: `pi`, `claude-code`, `codex`. Use them in paths, provenance, qmd collection names, tests, and docs. Avoid informal aliases in implementation docs.

---

### L2 — Obsidian “read-only view” is underspecified enough to become an accidental writer later

**Failure scenario:**
Obsidian is demoted to read-only, but an on-demand render or push-sync job later writes back edited files, creating another source of truth and another migration/reconciliation problem.

**Attacks:**
ADR 0007 lines 16, 40, 43; spec lines 16, 64.

**Concrete fix:**
Define the read-only view contract now: generated from canonical, no edits accepted, no sync-back. If editable Obsidian memory is desired later, it must write only to an inbox/import queue with provenance and review.

---

# Ship-blocking fix order

1. Freeze cached core behind explicit versioned snapshots; prohibit live canonical/qmd/dedup/native state from affecting cached prefix bytes.
2. Resolve Pi injection ownership in code and docs; `pi-memory` must be the only Pi model-facing injector.
3. Redefine write ownership: append-only raw capture from harnesses, one locked canonical consolidator, transactional apply.
4. Replace migration count reconciliation with claim-level ledger, atomic apply, rollback, and idempotent rerun.
5. Add privacy/secret classification before anything enters `shared/`, qmd, or cross-harness recall.
6. Rewrite `recall-routing.ts` for canonical collections and dual-read before qmd repoint.
7. Remove embedding similarity as a suppression authority; use it only as a candidate signal.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/adr

# ADRs

## Objective

Keep a thin, durable decision log for each bounded context so future agents know why the codebase is shaped this way.

## Workflow

1. Verify the repo/context:
   - Work from the git root.
   - If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, use it to choose the bounded context.
   - Otherwise use root `docs/adr/`.
2. Read existing ADRs in the chosen context before proposing a decision change.
3. Offer or create an ADR only when all three are true:
   - **Hard to reverse** — changing course later has meaningful cost.
   - **Surprising without context** — a future reader will wonder why this path was chosen.
   - **Real trade-off** — genuine alternatives existed and one was chosen for specific reasons.
4. If any criterion is missing, skip the ADR:
   - Use a code comment for local implementation rationale.
   - Use a commit/PR note for historical change details.
   - Use no artifact for obvious or reversible choices.
5. Create one ADR per decision. Number it `NNNN-kebab-title.md`, incrementing from the highest existing ADR in that context.
6. Keep it short. Start with Matt Pocock's one-paragraph format; add sections only when they carry real decision memory.
7. Update `CONTEXT-MAP.md` only when adding a new bounded context or moving the ADR location.

## Placement

- Single-context repo → `docs/adr/` at repo root.
- Multi-context repo → root `docs/adr/` for system-wide decisions; `<context>/docs/adr/` for context-specific decisions.
- One stack of ADRs per bounded context.

## References

- For the ADR template and examples of what qualifies, read `references/format.md`.

1	# ADR 0007: Unified cross-harness memory store (`~/.agents/memory`)
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-22)
4	**Related:** `docs/memory-architecture.md`, `docs/memory-systems-comparison.md`, `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md`, ADR 0008, the 2026-06-10 A/B-deadline disposition in `memory-architecture.md`
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	Memory had diverged across five stores: `pi-memory` (`~/.pi/agent/memory/`), the dream bridge (`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`), Claude Code native auto-memory (`~/.claude/projects/<proj>/memory/`), Codex native memories + chronicle (`~/.codex/memories/`), and the `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` eval lanes. The two agent-facing stores were already disjoint (124 vs 81 profile files, different filenames; 25 vs 39 project dirs) — neither a superset of the other. Per-store consolidators on divergent corpora is the named industry anti-pattern (definition drift, irreconcilable conflicts).
9	
10	Two forcing functions converged. (1) The requirement that **CC/Codex learnings be *actively recalled* like Pi's**, not merely injected once at session start. (2) The 2026-06-10 disposition in `memory-architecture.md` set an A/B deadline (2026-06-30 / 30 sessions) to *choose the primary memory path*. This ADR resolves that deadline.
11	
12	The unification target is not greenfield: `extensions/dream-memory/src/lib/agents-path.ts` already defines `~/.agents/projects/<git-root>/memory/` as "the write target for agentic dream mode," `dream/agentic.ts` already writes there, and `claudeMemoryRoot()` already reads CC's native dir as a read-only source. The dream bridge already normalises pi/claude/codex hook payloads (`harness-cli.ts`) and already owns extract → consolidate (`dream/`, incl. `patch-applier.ts` ADD/UPDATE/DELETE) → index (qmd) → recall (`active-memory/`).
13	
14	## Decision
15	
16	1. **Canonical store = `~/.agents/memory`**, namespaced `shared/` + `harness/{claude,codex,pi}/` + `episodic/` + `inbox/`. Obsidian demotes to an optional **read-only view**, never load-bearing.
17	
18	2. **Single writer of the canonical consolidated record = the dream bridge's consolidation engine.** "Single writer" governs the canonical *store*, not injection. Each harness keeps its own **core injector** (CC native, Codex native, `pi-memory` `profile-base.ts`); the bridge owns the canonical store + cross-harness active recall + harvest. This preserves the 2026-06-10 rule that `pi-memory` — not dream-memory — owns Pi profile-core injection.
19	
20	3. **Build on the own stack; do not adopt Mem0/Letta as runtime.** Every component an external memory system sells already exists in the bridge, tuned to constraints they do not model (cache byte-stability per ADR 0008, human-gated dreaming, three-harness normalisation, structured patch edits). Borrow *algorithms* (the conflict-merge verbs are already mirrored in `dream/patch-schema.ts`), never the dependency. This is the primary-path choice the 2026-06-10 deadline asked for.
21	
22	4. **Fold natives by capture + harvest, not by disabling.** CC `autoMemory` and Codex `memories` (+ chronicle) stay **ON as capture surfaces**: they capture and self-inject their own subset; the bridge **harvests their dirs read-only** into the canonical store via the dream/patch pipeline, provenance-tagged. The bridge **never writes back into native dirs** (keeps single-writer intact). Keeping Codex `memories=true` preserves chronicle's screen-memory injection. `pi-memory`'s write/extraction repoints to the canonical store; its Pi-core injection role stays.
23	
24	5. **Recall = global minus self, namespaced.** The bridge's injected recall for harness X = canonical memory **minus what X already self-injects** — a cheap provenance-tag pass plus a qmd embedding-similarity backstop (catches dreamed/reworded duplicates). Per-harness uniqueness falls out of the same machinery: recall scope for X = `shared ∪ harness/X`, so a Claude-specific tool learning surfaces to CC and never noise-injects into Pi.
25	
26	6. **Shadows = offline-bench backends only.** `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` register nothing live and are evaluated by snapshot-replay (`scripts/bench/`), not live traffic. Move them out of the daily-driver profile; re-bench against the new canonical corpus post-migration as the build-vs-buy proof.
27	
28	## Alternatives Considered
29	
30	| Alternative | Rejected because |
31	|---|---|
32	| Per-harness stores + a reconciler pass | The named anti-pattern; divergent corpora already proved drift (disjoint 124/81 sets). |
33	| Adopt Mem0/Letta as the runtime | Regresses human-gated dreaming (ahead of the commercial pack), discards the bridge's tuned pipeline, and retrofits constraints they don't model. Kept only as offline benchmarks. |
34	| Disable CC + Codex native memory; bridge owns all capture | Simplest, but loses CC's extractor (whose memories Luke wants surfaced) and — because Codex's memory switch gates chronicle — kills chronicle's screen-memory injection. |
35	| Symlink native dirs at the canonical store | Format pollution (CC owns its file shape) + two writers on one dir; breaks single-writer. |
36	| Make the bridge the single *injector* too | Violates the 2026-06-10 cache-governance decision; `pi-memory`'s `profile-base` is the proven cache-safe Pi core renderer. |
37	
38	## Consequences
39	
40	- Implementation is a grouped program — see `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md` (canonical skeleton, one-off migration, harvest watchers, dedup-on-inject, qmd re-point, `pi-memory` write repoint, shadow relocation, cutover).
41	- The mutation/cache behaviour of the unified store is governed by **ADR 0008** (two-region contract).
42	- This **supersedes the 2026-06-30 A/B "choose primary path" deadline**: primary = own unified stack; shadows retained only as offline benchmarks with the existing metric set (cache-base churn, recall precision/usefulness, correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool overhead, prompt bytes).
43	- One-off migration must union pi + obsidian as full members and ingest CC/Codex (chronicle → episodic) as read-only sources, deduped in a single pass, via dry-run → quarantine review → apply.
44	- `memory-architecture.md` becomes the descriptive map of the unified system after cutover; this ADR is the decision of record.
45

1	# ADR 0008: Memory cache-stability contract (two regions, frozen-per-span)
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-22)
4	**Related:** ADR 0007, `docs/cache-strategy.md`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`, the cache golden rule in `pi-dev.md`
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	ADR 0007 makes one canonical store serve active recall across Pi, Claude Code, and Codex. Active recall "like Pi's" is a per-turn read, which collides directly with the cache golden rule: `params.system` and `tools[]` must stay byte-stable across same-cwd sessions, and dynamic data must live in appended messages, never in the cached prefix.
9	
10	The unresolved question was: when a memory is **modified or removed**, how does that propagate without busting each harness's prompt-prefix cache mid-session? The three harnesses already share the same physics — a stable core is read **once at session start** and injected into the cached prefix (CC `MEMORY.md`, Codex Developer Message, Pi's `profile-base` snapshot), while dynamic recall is **appended per turn** (Pi's `active-memory` tail). The contract below formalises that shape and makes the mutation policy explicit so future memory work cannot silently violate it.
11	
12	## Decision
13	
14	Two regions, enforced per harness:
15	
16	- **Core** — small, slow-changing, deterministically injected into the harness's cached prefix at **SessionStart**, then **frozen for the cached span**. It is re-rendered only at boundaries that *already* rebuild the prefix: **SessionStart and compaction**. (Re-rendering at compaction is free — the prefix is being rebuilt anyway — and is where a long session picks up corrected/removed facts.)
17	- **Recall** — volatile, trailing, per-turn, **never cached**.
18	
19	Mutation policy:
20	
21	- **Mutations never touch a live session's core.** A write/merge/remove lands in `~/.agents/memory` and only re-renders into a harness's core at *that harness's* next boundary. Mid-session, a new relevant fact still surfaces — via the volatile recall region, not by rewriting the prefix.
22	- **Removal = soft-invalidate** (tombstone + decay via `decay-prune.ts`); physical prune happens only at consolidation, so cached prefix bytes never shift under a running session.
23	- **Cache domains are per-harness.** Sharing the store ≠ sharing prefix bytes. Each harness renders its own core; a mutation pays the cache cost only on *its* next boundary — never mid-session, never cross-harness.
24	
25	`pi-memory`'s `profile-base` snapshot is Pi's proven cache-safe core renderer; the bridge's `active-memory` tail is the volatile recall. The same split is required of CC and Codex rendering.
26	
27	## Alternatives Considered
28	
29	| Alternative | Rejected because |
30	|---|---|
31	| All memory in the trailing region (no cached core) | Zero cache-bust risk, but forfeits the prefix-cache cost win (41–80% on stable prefixes) and re-bills stable facts every turn. |
32	| Re-render the core every turn | Busts the prefix cache on every turn — the exact failure the golden rule exists to prevent. |
33	| Immediate physical delete of a removed memory mid-session | Shifts cached prefix bytes under a live session. Soft-invalidate + deferred prune avoids it. |
34	| Freeze the core for the whole session, never re-render | Misses corrected/removed facts for the life of a long session; compaction is a free re-render point already being paid for. |
35	
36	## Consequences
37	
38	- The bridge gains a **compaction subscription** to re-render the core: CC exposes `PreCompact`; Pi has context-mode compaction (verify the extension hook); Codex likely exposes none and **gracefully degrades to SessionStart-only** refresh. Any Pi-core compaction hook that needs the fork is logged in `docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.
39	- **Accepted tension:** a corrected or removed fact can persist in a long-running session's *frozen core* until its next boundary (SessionStart or compaction). The volatile recall can *add* a correction alongside it but cannot *unsend* the stale prefix line. Acceptable given the cache win; compaction bounds the staleness window.
40	- All future memory work must honour this contract; the `pi-cache-stability` skill checklist is the enforcement point and links here.
41

(Re-rendering at compaction is free — the prefix is being rebuilt anyway — and is where a long session picks up corrected/removed facts.)

| Freeze the core for the whole session, never re-render | Misses corrected/removed facts for the life of a long session; compaction is a free re-render point already being paid for. |

## Consequences

- The bridge gains a **compaction subscription** to re-render the core: CC exposes `PreCompact`; Pi has context-mode compaction (verify the extension hook); Codex likely exposes none and **gracefully degrades to SessionStart-only** refresh. Any Pi-core compaction hook that needs the fork is logged in `docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.
- **Accepted tension:** a corrected or removed fact can persist in a long-running session's *frozen core* until its next boundary (SessionStart or compaction). 1	# Cross-Harness Memory Unification — Implementation Spec
2	
3	**Status:** Draft (2026-06-22) — spec first; GitHub program tracker pending Luke's go-ahead
4	**Decisions of record:** ADR 0007 (unified store), ADR 0008 (cache contract)
5	**Owner extension:** `extensions/dream-memory` (the bridge) + `extensions/pi-memory` (Pi core injector / capture)
6	**Supersedes:** the 2026-06-30 A/B "choose primary path" deadline in `docs/memory-architecture.md`
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	One canonical, namespaced memory store (`~/.agents/memory`) that all three harnesses (Pi, Claude Code, Codex) read, write (via one consolidation owner), actively recall, and dream over — without breaking the prompt-prefix cache, and preserving chronicle and each harness's native capture.
11	
12	## Non-goals
13	
14	- Adopting Mem0/Letta as runtime (they stay offline benchmarks — ADR 0007).
15	- Changing each harness's *core injector* (CC native, Codex native, `pi-memory` `profile-base` stay — ADR 0008). The bridge owns the canonical store + cross-harness recall + harvest, not injection.
16	- A live Obsidian sync surface (Obsidian is a read-only view; push-sync is an open question, not a deliverable here).
17	
18	## Architecture (target)
19	
20	```
21	CC native      ─┐ capture + self-inject own subset
22	Codex+chronicle ─┤→ bridge harvests (read-only)  ┐
23	Pi (write repoint)─┘  Pi writes canonical directly │
24	                                                   ▼
25	                                   ~/.agents/memory  ← single writer (bridge consolidation)
26	                                   shared/ + harness/{claude,codex,pi}/ + episodic/ + inbox/
27	                                                   │
28	                          ┌────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
29	                          ▼                        ▼                         ▼
30	                  dream/consolidate         qmd indexes canonical      inject:
31	                  (patch + decay +                                     core @ SessionStart+compaction
32	                   quarantine)                                        recall @ turn = global MINUS self
33	                                                                       (provenance tag + embedding dedup)
34	```
35	
36	Namespacing: `shared/` (cross-harness) ∪ `harness/X` (X-specific). Recall scope for harness X = `shared ∪ harness/X`. Every memory carries a `provenance` frontmatter field (origin harness + capture path).
37	
38	## Phases (become ordered child issues once the tracker is approved)
39	
40	**P0 — Spec + ADRs.** This document + ADR 0007/0008. *Done when:* merged and indexed.
41	
42	**P1 — Canonical skeleton + qmd re-point.** Define `~/.agents/memory` layout + `provenance` frontmatter; re-point qmd collections to index the canonical corpus; dual-read shim (read old + new during transition). *Gate:* qmd indexes canonical; federated recall returns canonical hits; no daily-driver cache-base churn (`pi-cache-stats`).
43	
44	**P2 — One-off migration (dream-engine batch).** Union pi + obsidian as full members; ingest CC/Codex as read-only sources; chronicle 10-min summaries → `episodic/`. Dedupe/stale/conflict via `patch-applier`; provenance tiers. Run **dry-run → quarantine review → apply**. *Gate:* dry-run patch set reviewed; union-count reconciliation (no silent drop of the ~124 pi + ~81 obsidian facts); idempotent re-run is a no-op.
45	
46	**P3 — Harvest watchers.** Diff CC + Codex native dirs on SessionStart/Stop → fold new/changed entries into canonical via the patch pipeline, provenance-tagged; never write back into native dirs. *Gate:* a new CC native memory lands in canonical within one session boundary; native dirs are never mutated by the bridge.
47	
48	**P4 — Dedup-on-inject + per-harness scope.** Inject `global − self`: provenance-tag pass + qmd embedding-similarity backstop; recall scope = `shared ∪ harness/X`. *Gate:* no in-context duplication of a self-injected fact; a CC-specific learning is not injected to Pi.
49	
50	**P5 — Cache contract (ADR 0008).** `PreCompact` (and Pi compaction) subscription; core re-render at SessionStart + compaction; soft-invalidate removal (tombstone + decay), physical prune at consolidation only. *Gate:* core byte-stable within a cached span; mutation re-renders only at a boundary; `pi-cache-stability` checklist passes. Any fork hook logged in `pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.
51	
52	**P6 — Shadow relocation + re-bench.** Move `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` out of the daily-driver profile into a `bench`/`eval` profile; re-run `scripts/bench` against the canonical corpus; record overlap@5 / rank-correlation vs the own stack. *Gate:* bench runs green; build-vs-buy result recorded (own ≥ shadows, or a flagged adopt decision).
53	
54	**P7 — Cutover + retire old roots.** Make canonical the source of truth; Obsidian → read-only view; decommission the dual-read shim; rewrite `memory-architecture.md` as the descriptive map. *Gate:* full extension gate + fork gate green; 30-session soak or metric parity on the ADR 0007 metric set.
55	
56	## Proof / gates (program-level)
57	
58	Metric set inherited from the 2026-06-10 disposition: cache-base churn, recall precision, recall usefulness (did it change the next action?), user-correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool-call overhead, prompt bytes per session. Each phase ships its own gate above; P7 is the soak.
59	
60	## Open questions

# Cross-Harness Memory Unification — Implementation Spec

**Status:** Draft (2026-06-22) — spec first; GitHub program tracker pending Luke's go-ahead
**Decisions of record:** ADR 0007 (unified store), ADR 0008 (cache contract)
**Owner extension:** `extensions/dream-memory` (the bridge) + `extensions/pi-memory` (Pi core injector / capture)
**Supersedes:** the 2026-06-30 A/B "choose primary path" deadline in `docs/memory-architecture.md`

## Goal

One canonical, namespaced memory store (`~/.agents/memory`) that all three harnesses (Pi, Claude Code, Codex) read, write (via one consolidation owner), actively recall, and dream over — without breaking the prompt-prefix cache, and preserving chronicle and each harness's native capture.

## Non-goals

- Adopting Mem0/Letta as runtime (they stay offline benchmarks — ADR 0007).
- Changing each harness's *core injector* (CC native, Codex native, `pi-memory` `profile-base` stay — ADR 0008). The bridge owns the canonical store + cross-harness recall + harvest, not injection.
- A live Obsidian sync surface (Obsidian is a read-only view; push-sync is an open question, not a deliverable here).

## Architecture (target)

```
CC native      ─┐ capture + self-inject own subset
Codex+chronicle ─┤→ bridge harvests (read-only)  ┐
Pi (write repoint)─┘  Pi writes canonical directly │
                                                   ▼
                                   ~/.agents/memory  ← single writer (bridge consolidation)
                                   shared/ + harness/{claude,codex,pi}/ + episodic/ + inbox/
                                                   │
                          ┌────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
                          ▼                        ▼                         ▼
                  dream/consolidate         qmd indexes canonical      inject:
                  (patch + decay +                                     core @ SessionStart+compaction
                   quarantine)                                        recall @ turn = global MINUS self
                                                                       (provenance tag + embedding dedup)
```

Namespacing: `shared/` (cross-harness) ∪ `harness/X` (X-specific). Recall scope for harness X = `shared ∪ harness/X`. Every memory carries a `provenance` frontmatter field (origin harness + capture path).

## Phases (become ordered child issues once the tracker is approved)

**P0 — Spec + ADRs.** This document + ADR 0007/0008. *Done when:* merged and indexed.

**P1 — Canonical skeleton + qmd re-point.** Define `~/.agents/memory` layout + `provenance` frontmatter; re-point qmd collections to index the canonical corpus; dual-read shim (read old + new during transition). *Gate:* qmd indexes canonical; federated recall returns canonical hits; no daily-driver cache-base churn (`pi-cache-stats`).

**P2 — One-off migration (dream-engine batch).** Union pi + obsidian as full members; ingest CC/Codex as read-only sources; chronicle 10-min summaries → `episodic/`. Dedupe/stale/conflict via `patch-applier`; provenance tiers. Run **dry-run → quarantine review → apply**. *Gate:* dry-run patch set reviewed; union-count reconciliation (no silent drop of the ~124 pi + ~81 obsidian facts); idempotent re-run is a no-op.

**P3 — Harvest watchers.** Diff CC + Codex native dirs on SessionStart/Stop → fold new/changed entries into canonical via the patch pipeline, provenance-tagged; never write back into native dirs. *Gate:* a new CC native memory lands in canonical within one session boundary; native dirs are never mutated by the bridge.

**P4 — Dedup-on-inject + per-harness scope.** Inject `global − self`: provenance-tag pass + qmd embedding-similarity backstop; recall scope = `shared ∪ harness/X`. *Gate:* no in-context duplication of a self-injected fact; a CC-specific learning is not injected to Pi.

**P5 — Cache contract (ADR 0008).** `PreCompact` (and Pi compaction) subscription; core re-render at SessionStart + compaction; soft-invalidate removal (tombstone + decay), physical prune at consolidation only. *Gate:* core byte-stable within a cached span; mutation re-renders only at a boundary; `pi-cache-stability` checklist passes. Any fork hook logged in `pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.

**P6 — Shadow relocation + re-bench.** Move `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` out of the daily-driver profile into a `bench`/`eval` profile; re-run `scripts/bench` against the canonical corpus; record overlap@5 / rank-correlation vs the own stack. *Gate:* bench runs green; build-vs-buy result recorded (own ≥ shadows, or a flagged adopt decision).

**P7 — Cutover + retire old roots.** Make canonical the source of truth; Obsidian → read-only view; decommission the dual-read shim; rewrite `memory-architecture.md` as the descriptive map. *Gate:* full extension gate + fork gate green; 30-session soak or metric parity on the ADR 0007 metric set.

## Proof / gates (program-level)

Metric set inherited from the 2026-06-10 disposition: cache-base churn, recall precision, recall usefulness (did it change the next action?), user-correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool-call overhead, prompt bytes per session. Each phase ships its own gate above; P7 is the soak.

## Open questions

- Embedding-similarity threshold for dedup-on-inject (tune on the migrated corpus in P4).
- Chronicle `episodic/` → `semantic/` promotion policy (when does a screen summary earn durable memory?).
- Obsidian view: on-demand render vs a push-sync job (out of scope; decide if/when Luke wants browsing back).
- Does Pi expose a compaction event to extensions, or is a fork hook required (P5)?
- `pi-memory` thin-shim vs full write-path repoint — settle in P3 against the harvest design.

# ADR 0007: Unified cross-harness memory store (`~/.agents/memory`)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-22)
**Related:** `docs/memory-architecture.md`, `docs/memory-systems-comparison.md`, `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md`, ADR 0008, the 2026-06-10 A/B-deadline disposition in `memory-architecture.md`

## Context

Memory had diverged across five stores: `pi-memory` (`~/.pi/agent/memory/`), the dream bridge (`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`), Claude Code native auto-memory (`~/.claude/projects/<proj>/memory/`), Codex native memories + chronicle (`~/.codex/memories/`), and the `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` eval lanes. The two agent-facing stores were already disjoint (124 vs 81 profile files, different filenames; 25 vs 39 project dirs) — neither a superset of the other. Per-store consolidators on divergent corpora is the named industry anti-pattern (definition drift, irreconcilable conflicts).

Two forcing functions converged. (1) The requirement that **CC/Codex learnings be *actively recalled* like Pi's**, not merely injected once at session start. (2) The 2026-06-10 disposition in `memory-architecture.md` set an A/B deadline (2026-06-30 / 30 sessions) to *choose the primary memory path*. This ADR resolves that deadline.

The unification target is not greenfield: `extensions/dream-memory/src/lib/agents-path.ts` already defines `~/.agents/projects/<git-root>/memory/` as "the write target for agentic dream mode," `dream/agentic.ts` already writes there, and `claudeMemoryRoot()` already reads CC's native dir as a read-only source. The dream bridge already normalises pi/claude/codex hook payloads (`harness-cli.ts`) and already owns extract → consolidate (`dream/`, incl. `patch-applier.ts` ADD/UPDATE/DELETE) → index (qmd) → recall (`active-memory/`).

## Decision

1. **Canonical store = `~/.agents/memory`**, namespaced `shared/` + `harness/{claude,codex,pi}/` + `episodic/` + `inbox/`. Obsidian demotes to an optional **read-only view**, never load-bearing.

2. **Single writer of the canonical consolidated record = the dream bridge's consolidation engine.** "Single writer" governs the canonical *store*, not injection. Each harness keeps its own **core injector** (CC native, Codex native, `pi-memory` `profile-base.ts`); the bridge owns the canonical store + cross-harness active recall + harvest. This preserves the 2026-06-10 rule that `pi-memory` — not dream-memory — owns Pi profile-core injection.

3. **Build on the own stack; do not adopt Mem0/Letta as runtime.** Every component an external memory system sells already exists in the bridge, tuned to constraints they do not model (cache byte-stability per ADR 0008, human-gated dreaming, three-harness normalisation, structured patch edits). Borrow *algorithms* (the conflict-merge verbs are already mirrored in `dream/patch-schema.ts`), never the dependency. This is the primary-path choice the 2026-06-10 deadline asked for.

4. **Fold natives by capture + harvest, not by disabling.** CC `autoMemory` and Codex `memories` (+ chronicle) stay **ON as capture surfaces**: they capture and self-inject their own subset; the bridge **harvests their dirs read-only** into the canonical store via the dream/patch pipeline, provenance-tagged. The bridge **never writes back into native dirs** (keeps single-writer intact). Keeping Codex `memories=true` preserves chronicle's screen-memory injection. `pi-memory`'s write/extraction repoints to the canonical store; its Pi-core injection role stays.

5. **Recall = global minus self, namespaced.** The bridge's injected recall for harness X = canonical memory **minus what X already self-injects** — a cheap provenance-tag pass plus a qmd embedding-similarity backstop (catches dreamed/reworded duplicates). Per-harness uniqueness falls out of the same machinery: recall scope for X = `shared ∪ harness/X`, so a Claude-specific tool learning surfaces to CC and never noise-injects into Pi.

6. **Shadows = offline-bench backends only.** `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` register nothing live and are evaluated by snapshot-replay (`scripts/bench/`), not live traffic. Move them out of the daily-driver profile; re-bench against the new canonical corpus post-migration as the build-vs-buy proof.

## Alternatives Considered

| Alternative | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| Per-harness stores + a reconciler pass | The named anti-pattern; divergent corpora already proved drift (disjoint 124/81 sets). |
| Adopt Mem0/Letta as the runtime | Regresses human-gated dreaming (ahead of the commercial pack), discards the bridge's tuned pipeline, and retrofits constraints they don't model. Kept only as offline benchmarks. |
| Disable CC + Codex native memory; bridge owns all capture | Simplest, but loses CC's extractor (whose memories Luke wants surfaced) and — because Codex's memory switch gates chronicle — kills chronicle's screen-memory injection. |
| Symlink native dirs at the canonical store | Format pollution (CC owns its file shape) + two writers on one dir; breaks single-writer. |
| Make the bridge the single *injector* too | Violates the 2026-06-10 cache-governance decision; `pi-memory`'s `profile-base` is the proven cache-safe Pi core renderer. |

## Consequences

- Implementation is a grouped program — see `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md` (canonical skeleton, one-off migration, harvest watchers, dedup-on-inject, qmd re-point, `pi-memory` write repoint, shadow relocation, cutover).
- The mutation/cache behaviour of the unified store is governed by **ADR 0008** (two-region contract).
- This **supersedes the 2026-06-30 A/B "choose primary path" deadline**: primary = own unified stack; shadows retained only as offline benchmarks with the existing metric set (cache-base churn, recall precision/usefulness, correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool overhead, prompt bytes).
- One-off migration must union pi + obsidian as full members and ingest CC/Codex (chronicle → episodic) as read-only sources, deduped in a single pass, via dry-run → quarantine review → apply.
- `memory-architecture.md` becomes the descriptive map of the unified system after cutover; this ADR is the decision of record.

# ADR 0007: Unified cross-harness memory store (`~/.agents/memory`)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-22)
**Related:** `docs/memory-architecture.md`, `docs/memory-systems-comparison.md`, `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md`, ADR 0008, the 2026-06-10 A/B-deadline disposition in `memory-architecture.md`

## Context

Memory had diverged across five stores: `pi-memory` (`~/.pi/agent/memory/`), the dream bridge (`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`), Claude Code native auto-memory (`~/.claude/projects/<proj>/memory/`), Codex native memories + chronicle (`~/.codex/memories/`), and the `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` eval lanes. The two agent-facing stores were already disjoint (124 vs 81 profile files, different filenames; 25 vs 39 project dirs) — neither a superset of the other. Per-store consolidators on divergent corpora is the named industry anti-pattern (definition drift, irreconcilable conflicts).

Two forcing functions converged. (1) The requirement that **CC/Codex learnings be *actively recalled* like Pi's**, not merely injected once at session start. (2) The 2026-06-10 disposition in `memory-architecture.md` set an A/B deadline (2026-06-30 / 30 sessions) to *choose the primary memory path*. This ADR resolves that deadline.

The unification target is not greenfield: `extensions/dream-memory/src/lib/agents-path.ts` already defines `~/.agents/projects/<git-root>/memory/` as "the write target for agentic dream mode," `dream/agentic.ts` already writes there, and `claudeMemoryRoot()` already reads CC's native dir as a read-only source. The dream bridge already normalises pi/claude/codex hook payloads (`harness-cli.ts`) and already owns extract → consolidate (`dream/`, incl. `patch-applier.ts` ADD/UPDATE/DELETE) → index (qmd) → recall (`active-memory/`).

## Decision

1. **Canonical store = `~/.agents/memory`**, namespaced `shared/` + `harness/{claude,codex,pi}/` + `episodic/` + `inbox/`. Obsidian demotes to an optional **read-only view**, never load-bearing.

2. **Three write classes, not one writer (resolves the "single writer" ambiguity).** The store has exactly three mutation authorities, each scoped:
   - **Raw capture writers** (any harness, any harvester) may append *only* into `inbox/` as immutable events. Pi included — Pi does **not** write canonical records directly; it appends to `inbox/` like every other source.
   - **Canonical consolidated writer = one** dream-bridge consolidation process, holding a global store lock (see ADR 0008 + spec P3). It is the *only* mutator of `shared/`, `harness/*`, `episodic/`.
   - **Model-facing injectors = one per harness** (CC native, Codex native, `pi-memory` `profile-base.ts`). "Single writer" was always about the canonical *store*, never injection. This preserves the 2026-06-10 rule that `pi-memory` — not dream-memory — owns Pi profile-core injection. For Pi the bridge may *compute* recall candidates but **must not inject**; a single-owner injection guard enforces it (spec P4).

3. **Build on the own stack; do not adopt Mem0/Letta as runtime.** Every component an external memory system sells already exists in the bridge, tuned to constraints they do not model (cache byte-stability per ADR 0008, human-gated dreaming, three-harness normalisation, structured patch edits). Borrow *algorithms* (the conflict-merge verbs are already mirrored in `dream/patch-schema.ts`), never the dependency. This is the primary-path choice the 2026-06-10 deadline asked for.

4. **Fold natives by capture + harvest, not by disabling.** CC `autoMemory` and Codex `memories` (+ chronicle) stay **ON as capture surfaces**: they capture and self-inject their own subset; the bridge **harvests their dirs read-only** into `inbox/` via the dream/patch pipeline, provenance-tagged. The bridge **never writes back into native dirs** (keeps single-writer intact). Keeping Codex `memories=true` preserves chronicle's screen-memory injection. `pi-memory`'s write/extraction repoints to the canonical **inbox** (append-only); consolidation promotes — its Pi-core injection role stays.
   - **Harvested native memory is untrusted external input.** It lands in `inbox/quarantine/<origin>/`, **not** `shared/`. Promotion to `shared/` or `harness/*` requires the consolidation pass to classify it (scope + sensitivity). A native self-injected fact that canonical has since *corrected* must not silently win: when canonical contradicts a still-surfacing native fact, the bridge injects an explicit appended correction rather than relying on dedup to suppress it (see Decision 5).

5. **Recall = global minus self, namespaced.** The bridge's injected recall for harness X = canonical memory **minus what X already self-injects** — a cheap provenance-tag pass plus a qmd embedding-similarity backstop (catches dreamed/reworded duplicates). Per-harness uniqueness falls out of the same machinery: recall scope for X = `shared ∪ harness/X`, so a Claude-specific tool learning surfaces to CC and never noise-injects into Pi.

6. **Shadows = offline-bench backends only.** `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` register nothing live and are evaluated by snapshot-replay (`scripts/bench/`), not live traffic. Move them out of the daily-driver profile; re-bench against the new canonical corpus post-migration as the build-vs-buy proof.

## Alternatives Considered

| Alternative | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| Per-harness stores + a reconciler pass | The named anti-pattern; divergent corpora already proved drift (disjoint 124/81 sets). |
| Adopt Mem0/Letta as the runtime | Regresses human-gated dreaming (ahead of the commercial pack), discards the bridge's tuned pipeline, and retrofits constraints they don't model. Kept only as offline benchmarks. |
| Disable CC + Codex native memory; bridge owns all capture | Simplest, but loses CC's extractor (whose memories Luke wants surfaced) and — because Codex's memory switch gates chronicle — kills chronicle's screen-memory injection. |
| Symlink native dirs at the canonical store | Format pollution (CC owns its file shape) + two writers on one dir; breaks single-writer. |
