- [ ] #385 — **P5** Cache contract (ADR 0008)
- [ ] #386 — **P6** Shadow relocation + re-bench
- [ ] #387 — **P7** Cutover + retire old roots

Dependency spine: P0.5 → P1 → {P2, P3} → P4 → P5 → P6 → P7. Hard gates run **early** (per phase), not at the P7 soak.

## Non-negotiable invariants (from the review)
1. Cached core renders from a **versioned promoted snapshot**, never live canonical/qmd/dedup/native state.
2. `pi-memory` is the **only** Pi model-facing injector; the bridge computes recall but never injects for Pi.
3. Three write classes: append-only `inbox/` capture / one locked consolidator / one injector per harness.
4. Migration is a **claim-level ledger** with transactional apply + rollback — not file-count reconciliation.
5. **Privacy first:** secret/PII scan before index and before inject; harvested natives default to quarantine; `visibility ≠ origin`.
6. `recall-routing.ts` rewritten for canonical collections **before** qmd cutover.
7. Embedding similarity is a **candidate signal, never a deletion authority**.

# ADRs

## Objective

Keep a thin, durable decision log for each bounded context so future agents know why the codebase is shaped this way.

## Workflow

1. Verify the repo/context:
   - Work from the git root.
   - If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, use it to choose the bounded context.
   - Otherwise use root `docs/adr/`.
2. Read existing ADRs in the chosen context before proposing a decision change.
3. Offer or create an ADR only when all three are true:
   - **Hard to reverse** — changing course later has meaningful cost.
   - **Surprising without context** — a future reader will wonder why this path was chosen.
   - **Real trade-off** — genuine alternatives existed and one was chosen for specific reasons.
4. If any criterion is missing, skip the ADR:
   - Use a code comment for local implementation rationale.
   - Use a commit/PR note for historical change details.
   - Use no artifact for obvious or reversible choices.
5. Create one ADR per decision. Number it `NNNN-kebab-title.md`, incrementing from the highest existing ADR in that context.
6. Keep it short. Start with Matt Pocock's one-paragraph format; add sections only when they carry real decision memory.
7. Update `CONTEXT-MAP.md` only when adding a new bounded context or moving the ADR location.

## Placement

- Single-context repo → `docs/adr/` at repo root.
- Multi-context repo → root `docs/adr/` for system-wide decisions; `<context>/docs/adr/` for context-specific decisions.
- One stack of ADRs per bounded context.

## References

- For the ADR template and examples of what qualifies, read `references/format.md`.

It is review-only, recommends the next artifact (PRD / issues / handoff), and stops before implementation.

## Import note

Current upstream source: `https://github.com/mattpocock/skills` (synced against commit `6eeb81b`, 2026-06-18).

These refs are a **curated, locally-adapted subset**, not a mirror. Upstream has since reorganized into a categorized plugin monorepo (`skills/engineering/*`, `skills/productivity/*`, multi-file skill dirs, Claude-Code `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter) and in several cases replaced self-contained skills with thin pointers to new upstream-only skills (`grill-me` → `/grilling`, `tdd` → `/codebase-design`). A wholesale re-sync would be a migration, not a refresh: it would regress the richer local `grill-with-docs` / `improve-codebase-architecture`, drop the local "use when" trigger descriptions, and introduce dangling references. So the full restructure is intentionally **out of scope**. The 2026-06-18 refresh adopted only safe additive upstream improvements (`to-prd` single-seam guidance, `to-issues` prefactor maxim) and preserved local-only refs (`fix-until-green`, `zoom-out`, `caveman`, `write-a-skill`).

Keep these as child refs, not standalone global skills, so Luke's primary skills stay canonical unless a Matt workflow is explicitly requested.

content.text:
Now I have the full picture. This is a stop-and-report moment, and an important one.

**Finding: the P0.5 "build the requalification tests" work is already done.** The dream-memory suite (385 passing) already covers every item the plan enumerated. I traced each one to an existing test:

| Planned P0.5 test | Already exists |
|---|---|
| Hook normalization (pi/claude/codex) | `harness-cli.spec.ts:44-91` |
| Injection-ownership — **bridge returns project-only for Pi, profile rides the cacheable base** (the safety-critical invariant) | `harness-cli.spec.ts:95-147` |
| patch-applier idempotency + atomicity | `patch-applier.spec.ts:134-189` |
| Cache byte-stability (5 sessions → byte-identical stdout, frontmatter stripped, no inbox leak) | `harness-cli.spec.ts:219-254` |
| Cross-harness end-to-end (Pi capture → dream merge → Claude+Codex SessionStart surface) | `cross-harness-smoke.spec.ts:106` |
| qmd reindex | `runner-qmd-reindex.spec.ts` + active-memory/cli-dream |
| Secret/PII redaction | `redact.spec.ts` |

Writing these would be rebuilding already-merged work — the exact PR #204 scar. So I stopped before writing a line of duplicate test.

**The genuine deltas the ADRs introduced are real but belong to *later* phases, not P0.5:**
- **Inject-time redaction.** `redact()` is wired into the *write* paths (`store.ts:210` appendEvent, `:360` appendInboxNote, `quarantine.ts:46`, `dream.ts:1101/1156` pre-LLM assert) but **not** the *read/inject* path (`loadProfileContext`/`loadProjectContext` → `readIndexFile`, no scan). ADR 0007 D7 wants "scan before index *and inject*" → that's a P4 (#384) item.
- **Embedding = candidate signal, never deletion authority** (invariant 7) → no explicit guard. P1/P4.
- **CC `PreCompact` hook** — `harness-cli` has no compaction handler (already documented on #380). P3/P5.

So P0.5's only true residual is the **pi-memory repoint design** (design doc, not tests) — the compaction question is already resolved and recorded.

I made no edits; the throwaway worktree is clean. One fork decides the next move:

- Per-turn recall as a `"pi_memory_recall"` custom message delivered via `sendMessage({ deliverAs: "nextTurn" })` in `pi.on("input", ...)` lines 363–386

Both extensions fire their `systemPrompt:build` filter at priority 10, so both profile blocks enter the base. The `before_agent_start` persistent-memory block from dream-memory and the `INJECT_MARKER` section from pi-memory are both appended to the system prompt on the first turn.

---

### Q5. What "repoint" would touch, and is Pi already effectively repointed?

**Pi is NOT currently repointed to `~/.agents/memory`.** The two stores are siloed:

| Extension | Active read root | Active write root |
|---|---|---|
| dream-memory injection | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` (wiki/qmd) | `~/.dream-memory/events/` (event log) + `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` (fast dream) |
| dream-memory agentic dream | reads `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/` + optionally `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` (read-only) | **writes `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/`** |
| pi-memory injection | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` |

The agentic dream (`agentic.ts`) is the ONLY component that already writes to `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/`. But the injection path in `extension.ts` never reads from `~/.agents/`; it reads from `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`. The qmd collection `"dream-memory"` indexes `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`, not `~/.agents/`. **Concrete read/write call sites that would change for a "full repoint":**

1. `store.ts` `wikiRoot()` / `memoryDir()` lines 54–64 — these return `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`. Repointing = make these return `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/` (or a project-neutral `~/.agents/memory/`). This changes where `loadProfileContext`, `loadProjectContext`, `readMemoryTree`, `appendInboxNote`, and all dream-phase writes go.

2. `harness-cli.ts` `dispatchSessionStart` lines 360–366 — calls `loadProfileContext` and `loadProjectContext` which both delegate to `memoryDir()`. Repointing `memoryDir()` propagates automatically.

3. `dream/dream.ts` (fast-mode dream consolidation) — writes markdown files under `memoryDir()`. Same dependency.

4. `active-memory.ts` `searchMemory` calls — currently queries the `"dream-memory"` qmd collection which indexes `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`. Repointing = change `DREAM_QMD_COLLECTION` to point to a collection indexing `~/.agents/memory/`, or reindex it.

5. `profile-base.ts` in **pi-memory** (`/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/pi-memory/src/profile-base.ts`) lines 31–38 — reads profile from `DREAM_WIKI_HOME ?? ~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/`. The profile snapshot path is `~/.pi/agent/dream-memory/profile-memory.md`. Repointing = change `wikiHome()` here too, or make this read from `~/.agents/memory/profile/`.

6. **pi-memory's own store** (`~/.pi/agent/memory/`) would remain unchanged unless specifically migrated. The `memoryRoot()` in `util.ts` line 10 is independent of dream-memory's roots. If the goal is a unified canonical store under `~/.agents/memory/`, pi-memory's file writes (`profileDir()`, `projectDir()`) and its SQLite DB (`db/memory.sqlite`) would also need repointing via `PI_MEMORY_DIR`.

**Summary conclusion on "repoint" work:** Dream-memory's agentic path already writes to `~/.agents/projects/<gitRoot>/memory/` but the injection reads happen from `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` (wiki). The work is: (a) flip `wikiRoot()` (or `DREAM_WIKI_HOME`) to serve `~/.agents/memory/` as the wiki root, (b) migrate existing `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` content, (c) reindex the qmd collection, and (d) if full unification is desired, also flip `PI_MEMORY_DIR` to point pi-memory at `~/.agents/memory/` and migrate `~/.pi/agent/memory/` content + sqlite. There is no migration shortcut — the live injection and the agentic-dream write are currently to different directories.

content.text: Luke's follow-up — "how do we keep our autowiki + dreaming + dedupe" — is exactly the right design concern, and it folds into this same residual. Let me read the full ADR decision block and investigate the autowiki/dream/dedupe mechanics so the design is accurate, in parallel.

content.content:
14	## Decision
15	
16	1. **Canonical store = `~/.agents/memory`**, namespaced `shared/` + `harness/{pi,claude-code,codex}/` + `episodic/` + `inbox/` (canonical harness IDs `pi`/`claude-code`/`codex`, no aliases — spec). Obsidian demotes to an optional **read-only view**, never load-bearing.
17	
18	2. **Three write classes, not one writer (resolves the "single writer" ambiguity).** The store has exactly three mutation authorities, each scoped:
19	   - **Raw capture writers** (any harness, any harvester) may append *only* into `inbox/` as immutable events. Pi included — Pi does **not** write canonical records directly; it appends to `inbox/` like every other source.
20	   - **Canonical consolidated writer = one** dream-bridge consolidation process, holding a global store lock (see ADR 0008 + spec P3). It is the *only* mutator of `shared/`, `harness/*`, `episodic/`.
21	   - **Model-facing injectors = one per harness** (CC native, Codex native, `pi-memory` `profile-base.ts`). "Single writer" was always about the canonical *store*, never injection. This preserves the 2026-06-10 rule that `pi-memory` — not dream-memory — owns Pi profile-core injection. For Pi the bridge may *compute* recall candidates but **must not inject**; a single-owner injection guard enforces it (spec P4).
22	
23	3. **Build on the own stack; do not adopt Mem0/Letta as runtime.** Every component an external memory system sells already exists in the bridge, tuned to constraints they do not model (cache byte-stability per ADR 0008, human-gated dreaming, three-harness normalisation, structured patch edits). Borrow *algorithms* (the conflict-merge verbs are already mirrored in `dream/patch-schema.ts`), never the dependency. This is the primary-path choice the 2026-06-10 deadline asked for.
24	
25	4. **Fold natives by capture + harvest, not by disabling.** CC `autoMemory` and Codex `memories` (+ chronicle) stay **ON as capture surfaces**: they capture and self-inject their own subset; the bridge **harvests their dirs read-only** into `inbox/` via the dream/patch pipeline, provenance-tagged. The bridge **never writes back into native dirs** (keeps single-writer intact). Keeping Codex `memories=true` preserves chronicle's screen-memory injection. `pi-memory`'s write/extraction repoints to the canonical **inbox** (append-only); consolidation promotes — its Pi-core injection role stays.
26	   - **Harvested native memory is untrusted external input.** It lands in `inbox/quarantine/<origin>/`, **not** `shared/`. Promotion to `shared/` or `harness/*` requires the consolidation pass to classify it (scope + sensitivity). A native self-injected fact that canonical has since *corrected* must not silently win: when canonical contradicts a still-surfacing native fact, the bridge injects an explicit appended correction rather than relying on dedup to suppress it (see Decision 5).
27	
28	5. **Recall = global minus self, namespaced — tail only.** The bridge's injected recall for harness X = canonical memory **minus what X already self-injects**, scoped to `shared ∪ harness/X`. Two hard constraints:
29	   - **Tail-recall only.** "Global minus self" depends on volatile per-session state (native dirs, qmd index, similarity scores) and therefore **must never influence cached-core bytes** — it touches only the volatile trailing region (ADR 0008). Core dedup is manifest/snapshot-based, never embedding-based.
30	   - **Embedding similarity is a candidate signal, never a deletion authority.** Suppression of a candidate requires an exact source ID, an exact normalised-text hash, or an entailment check — because corrections, negations, dates, numbers, and scope changes sit *embedding-near* the stale fact they replace. A candidate carrying correction/negation/date/number/repo/tool/scope language defaults to **injected**. Visibility (not origin) decides cross-harness surfacing — see Decision 7.
31	
32	6. **Shadows = offline-bench backends only.** `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` register nothing live and are evaluated by snapshot-replay (`scripts/bench/`), not live traffic. Move them out of the daily-driver profile; re-bench against the new canonical corpus post-migration. The build-vs-buy *decision* (don't adopt) rests on grounds the benchmark cannot measure — human-gated dreaming, the cache contract external systems don't model, the already-tuned three-harness pipeline — **not** on snapshot-replay overlap, which is circular (it scores retrieval on a corpus already shaped by the own stack). The benchmark is a smoke test plus falsification harness (spec P6), not the justification.
33	
34	7. **Privacy is a first-class boundary; `origin ≠ visibility`.** Namespaces are functional, not security boundaries, so every record carries explicit `visibility` (`private | harness:<x> | project:<slug> | shared`), `sensitivity` (`public | private | secret`), `scope`, and `origin` — **visibility is never inferred from origin**. New harvested/captured facts (incl. chronicle screen summaries) default to **origin-private**, promoted to broader visibility only by a classification pass. A **secret/PII scan runs before indexing and again before injection** (API keys, tokens, private keys, credentials, client identifiers, local paths, payment/legal/medical, screen captures); the recall layer enforces ACLs *before* qmd ranking and *again* before final injection. This is what stops a Codex-captured client token surfacing as Pi or CC context.
35	
36	## Alternatives Considered
37	
38	| Alternative | Rejected because |
39	|---|---|
40	| Per-harness stores + a reconciler pass | The named anti-pattern; divergent corpora already proved drift (disjoint 124/81 sets). |
41	| Adopt Mem0/Letta as the runtime | Regresses human-gated dreaming (ahead of the commercial pack), discards the bridge's tuned pipeline, and retrofits constraints they don't model. Kept only as offline benchmarks. |
42	| Disable CC + Codex native memory; bridge owns all capture | Simplest, but loses CC's extractor (whose memories Luke wants surfaced) and — because Codex's memory switch gates chronicle — kills chronicle's screen-memory injection. |
43	| Symlink native dirs at the canonical store | Format pollution (CC owns its file shape) + two writers on one dir; breaks single-writer. |
44	| Make the bridge the single *injector* too | Violates the 2026-06-10 cache-governance decision; `pi-memory`'s `profile-base` is the proven cache-safe Pi core renderer. |
45	
46	## Consequences
47	
48	- Implementation is a grouped program — see `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md` (canonical skeleton, one-off migration, harvest watchers, dedup-on-inject, qmd re-point, `pi-memory` write repoint, shadow relocation, cutover).
49	- The mutation/cache behaviour of the unified store is governed by **ADR 0008** (two-region contract).
50	- This **supersedes the 2026-06-30 A/B "choose primary path" deadline**: primary = own unified stack; shadows retained only as offline benchmarks with the existing metric set (cache-base churn, recall precision/usefulness, correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool overhead, prompt bytes).
51	- One-off migration must union pi + obsidian as full members and ingest CC/Codex (chronicle → episodic) as read-only sources, deduped in a single pass, via dry-run → quarantine review → apply. **File-count reconciliation is not a data-loss gate** — migration runs on a **claim-level ledger** (atomic claims, source hashes/spans, content-addressed IDs, transactional apply + rollback, ledger-driven idempotent rerun). Spec P2.
52	- **Blocking preconditions** (decisions are accepted; these must close before migration applies — spec P0.5/P1): (a) dream-bridge code is *requalified* as live, not the retired/dead path `memory-architecture.md` describes; (b) Pi compaction-event availability and Pi write-path ownership are resolved (they determine cache safety and the single-writer claim); (c) `recall-routing.ts` is updated for canonical collections **before** the qmd cutover; (d) a canonical store write-lock + atomic-write/WAL protocol exists before any concurrent harvester runs.
53	- `memory-architecture.md` becomes the descriptive map of the unified system after cutover; this ADR is the decision of record.

3. **Build on the own stack; do not adopt Mem0/Letta as runtime.** Every component an external memory system sells already exists in the bridge, tuned to constraints they do not model (cache byte-stability per ADR 0008, human-gated dreaming, three-harness normalisation, structured patch edits). Borrow *algorithms* (the conflict-merge verbs are already mirrored in `dream/patch-schema.ts`), never the dependency. This is the primary-path choice the 2026-06-10 deadline asked for.

4. **Fold natives by capture + harvest, not by disabling.** CC `autoMemory` and Codex `memories` (+ chronicle) stay **ON as capture surfaces**: they capture and self-inject their own subset; the bridge **harvests their dirs read-only** into `inbox/` via the dream/patch pipeline, provenance-tagged. The bridge **never writes back into native dirs** (keeps single-writer intact). Keeping Codex `memories=true` preserves chronicle's screen-memory injection. `pi-memory`'s write/extraction repoints to the canonical **inbox** (append-only); consolidation promotes — its Pi-core injection role stays.
   - **Harvested native memory is untrusted external input.** It lands in `inbox/quarantine/<origin>/`, **not** `shared/`. Promotion to `shared/` or `harness/*` requires the consolidation pass to classify it (scope + sensitivity). A native self-injected fact that canonical has since *corrected* must not silently win: when canonical contradicts a still-surfacing native fact, the bridge injects an explicit appended correction rather than relying on dedup to suppress it (see Decision 5).

5. **Recall = global minus self, namespaced — tail only.** The bridge's injected recall for harness X = canonical memory **minus what X already self-injects**, scoped to `shared ∪ harness/X`. Two hard constraints:
   - **Tail-recall only.** "Global minus self" depends on volatile per-session state (native dirs, qmd index, similarity scores) and therefore **must never influence cached-core bytes** — it touches only the volatile trailing region (ADR 0008). Core dedup is manifest/snapshot-based, never embedding-based.
   - **Embedding similarity is a candidate signal, never a deletion authority.** Suppression of a candidate requires an exact source ID, an exact normalised-text hash, or an entailment check — because corrections, negations, dates, numbers, and scope changes sit *embedding-near* the stale fact they replace. A candidate carrying correction/negation/date/number/repo/tool/scope language defaults to **injected**. Visibility (not origin) decides cross-harness surfacing — see Decision 7.

6. **Shadows = offline-bench backends only.** `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` register nothing live and are evaluated by snapshot-replay (`scripts/bench/`), not live traffic. Move them out of the daily-driver profile; re-bench against the new canonical corpus post-migration. The build-vs-buy *decision* (don't adopt) rests on grounds the benchmark cannot measure — human-gated dreaming, the cache contract external systems don't model, the already-tuned three-harness pipeline — **not** on snapshot-replay overlap, which is circular (it scores retrieval on a corpus already shaped by the own stack). The benchmark is a smoke test plus falsification harness (spec P6), not the justification.

7. **Privacy is a first-class boundary; `origin ≠ visibility`.** Namespaces are functional, not security boundaries, so every record carries explicit `visibility` (`private | harness:<x> | project:<slug> | shared`), `sensitivity` (`public | private | secret`), `scope`, and `origin` — **visibility is never inferred from origin**. New harvested/captured facts (incl. chronicle screen summaries) default to **origin-private**, promoted to broader visibility only by a classification pass. A **secret/PII scan runs before indexing and again before injection** (API keys, tokens, private keys, credentials, client identifiers, local paths, payment/legal/medical, screen captures); the recall layer enforces ACLs *before* qmd ranking and *again* before final injection. This is what stops a Codex-captured client token surfacing as Pi or CC context.

## Alternatives Considered

| Alternative | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| Per-harness stores + a reconciler pass | The named anti-pattern; divergent corpora already proved drift (disjoint 124/81 sets). |
| Adopt Mem0/Letta as the runtime | Regresses human-gated dreaming (ahead of the commercial pack), discards the bridge's tuned pipeline, and retrofits constraints they don't model. Kept only as offline benchmarks. |
| Disable CC + Codex native memory; bridge owns all capture | Simplest, but loses CC's extractor (whose memories Luke wants surfaced) and — because Codex's memory switch gates chronicle — kills chronicle's screen-memory injection. |
| Symlink native dirs at the canonical store | Format pollution (CC owns its file shape) + two writers on one dir; breaks single-writer. |
| Make the bridge the single *injector* too | Violates the 2026-06-10 cache-governance decision; `pi-memory`'s `profile-base` is the proven cache-safe Pi core renderer. |

## Consequences

- Implementation is a grouped program — see `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md` (canonical skeleton, one-off migration, harvest watchers, dedup-on-inject, qmd re-point, `pi-memory` write repoint, shadow relocation, cutover).
- The mutation/cache behaviour of the unified store is governed by **ADR 0008** (two-region contract).
- This **supersedes the 2026-06-30 A/B "choose primary path" deadline**: primary = own unified stack; shadows retained only as offline benchmarks with the existing metric set (cache-base churn, recall precision/usefulness, correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool overhead, prompt bytes).
- One-off migration must union pi + obsidian as full members and ingest CC/Codex (chronicle → episodic) as read-only sources, deduped in a single pass, via dry-run → quarantine review → apply. **File-count reconciliation is not a data-loss gate** — migration runs on a **claim-level ledger** (atomic claims, source hashes/spans, content-addressed IDs, transactional apply + rollback, ledger-driven idempotent rerun). Spec P2.
- **Blocking preconditions** (decisions are accepted; these must close before migration applies — spec P0.5/P1): (a) dream-bridge code is *requalified* as live, not the retired/dead path `memory-architecture.md` describes; (b) Pi compaction-event availability and Pi write-path ownership are resolved (they determine cache safety and the single-writer claim); (c) `recall-routing.ts` is updated for canonical collections **before** the qmd cutover; (d) a canonical store write-lock + atomic-write/WAL protocol exists before any concurrent harvester runs.
- `memory-architecture.md` becomes the descriptive map of the unified system after cutover; this ADR is the decision of record.

I now have everything I need. Here is the complete structured findings document.

---

## Findings: dream-memory and pi-memory — Three Mechanisms

---

### 1. AUTOWIKI

#### How notes are structured as a wiki

There is **no traditional wikilink graph**. The term "autowiki" does not appear in either codebase as a first-class concept. The "wiki" is simply a directory of plain Markdown files under `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` (the `wikiRoot()` → `memoryDir()` path), organized under `memory/{profile,project,tools,inbox}/`. Each file carries YAML frontmatter with a `permalink` field (e.g. `profile/my-note`, `project/my-pi/boot-profile`). The `[[wiki-link]]` syntax appears only as a hint in the `memory_note` tool description string (`extension.ts:745`) — it is **not parsed, indexed, or graph-built anywhere**. There is no backlink generation pass, no `Relations:` section processing (those are explicitly stripped — see below), and no wiki-graph builder.

- **`wikiRoot()`**: `store.ts:54` → `process.env.DREAM_WIKI_HOME ?? join(homedir(), "obsidian", "dream-memory")`
- **`memoryDir()`**: `store.ts:63` → `join(wikiRoot(), "memory")`
- **`permalink` in frontmatter**: defined in `schema.ts:21` as a required string; used in `patch-applier.ts:67-69` to build a `byPermalink` map for target resolution during patch application
- **`## Relations` / `## Observations` stripping**: `dream.ts:310-316` — `stripBasicMemorySections()` removes these sections on every serialise call, explicitly severing the old basic-memory wiki graph surface. The comment says "QMD reads the body as plain text and the wiki frontmatter is the only structured surface" (`dream.ts:308`).
- **Obsidian path**: Yes — `wikiRoot()` defaults to `~/obsidian/dream-memory/`. The vault Obsidian opens **is** `~/obsidian/dream-memory/`, and the `memory/` subdirectory inside it is the canonical wiki corpus. (`store.ts:54-56`)

#### What maintains the link graph

Nothing does. There is no automatic backlink or relations pass. The `permalink` field in frontmatter is used only as a patch-target resolution key in `patch-applier.ts:67-69` and as a search-hit identifier in `store.ts:805`. No graph is built or maintained.

#### What qmd indexes and which collection names

**dream-memory** runs `qmd update` + `qmd embed` after every successful dream commit, over the vault at `~/obsidian/dream-memory/` (`dream.ts:399-410`). The default collection name is `"dream-memory"` (`store.ts:774`), but the system distinguishes profile- and project-scoped sub-collections: `dream-memory-profile` and `dream-memory-project` (referenced in `recall-routing.ts:16` and in pi-memory's `config.ts:314`). The qmd reindex is triggered by `runner.ts:382-383` via `spawnDetachedQmdReindex()` after a successful commit SHA.

**pi-memory** runs a debounced `qmd update` after every memory write (per the CLAUDE.md: "After every write, a debounced (500ms) `qmd update` runs fire-and-forget"). Its collection is `"pi-memory"` (`config.ts:313`); it can also federate across `["pi-memory", "dream-memory-profile", "dream-memory-project", "dream-memory-tools"]` (`config.ts:314`). The corpus on disk is `~/.pi/agent/memory/` (pi-memory's `memoryRoot()`; `util.ts:10`).

Active recall (dream-memory extension) queries `["pi-memory", "scars", "changes"]` by default — notably **excluding** `dream-memory-profile` and `dream-memory-project` because those are already deterministically injected into every session's system prompt (`recall-routing.ts:16-21`, `recall-routing.ts:23-27`).

---

### 2. DREAMING

#### Two dream modes: "fast" (default) vs "agentic"

**Fast mode** (default, `DREAM_AGENTIC` not set):
- **Reads**: JSONL event files in `~/.dream-memory/events/<sessionId>.jsonl` (via `readEventsSince()`, `store.ts:492`), the inbox memtable `memory/inbox/notes.md` (via `readInbox()`, `store.ts:399`), the wiki markdown snapshot (via `readMemoryTree()` — up to 64 files / 64 kB, `dream.ts:1202-1204`), a file index of all memory paths (via `listAllMemoryFiles()`, `dream.ts:1208`), and the live pi-memory snapshot (MEMORY.md, SCRATCHPAD.md, last 7 daily logs from `~/.pi/agent/memory/`, `dream.ts:137-177`).
- **Calls**: Pi's LLM (sonnet-class via `piRuntimeMerger`, `dream.ts:892`) with a prompt built by `buildDreamPrompt()` / `buildPatchPrompt()` (`dream.ts:672`).
- **Writes**: Staged files under `<eventsRoot>/staging/<run-id>/`, then copies into `memory/` under `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`, runs `git add -A` + `git commit` in the vault, updates per-session ULID watermarks, evicts processed inbox entries. (`dream.ts:1011+`, `runner.ts:354-355`)
- **Mode toggle**: `DREAM_MERGER_MODE=patch` switches to the patch-only LLM output format (`dream.ts:604-606`).

**Agentic mode** (`DREAM_AGENTIC=1`):
- **Reads**: Nothing directly — instead spawns `pi --source child-agent --print --mode json <prompt>` as a subprocess (`agentic.ts:228`). The prompt lists new session JSONL files since `last-dream.json`, instructs the sub-agent to grep the events dir and read `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/`. Optionally reads `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/MEMORY.md` as read-only source context.
- **Writes**: The spawned `pi` subprocess writes directly to `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/` using Write/Edit tools. No staging, no git commit, no ULID watermark advancement. (`agentic.ts:5-12`, `agentic.ts:317-319`)
- **Watermark**: NOT advanced. Only `last-dream.json` timestamp is updated on success (`agentic.ts:393`).
- **Progress**: Watched by monitoring `tool_execution_end` events on stdout for `write`/`edit` tool calls (`agentic.ts:249-259`).

#### Cadence / trigger chain

1. **On `session_shutdown`**: `extension.ts:1542` calls `dispatchStop()` → `harness-cli.ts:606` calls `maybeEnqueueDream(sessionId)`.
2. **`maybeEnqueueDream`** (`harness-cli.ts:285-312`): counts non-Stop events since the watermark for this session; if ≥1 event OR inbox bytes ≥ threshold, writes `~/.dream-memory/dream-pending` JSON marker file.
3. **Runner pickup**: `runPendingDream()` in `runner.ts:295` reads the marker, applies time gate (≥ `GATE_MIN_HOURS` = 24h since last dream, `runner.ts:22`) AND session gate (≥ `GATE_MIN_SESSIONS` = 5 sessions since last dream, `runner.ts:23`). Gates can be bypassed with `skipGates: true` (used by `/dream now`, `extension.ts:533`).
4. **Lock**: acquires `dream-runner.lock` (EEXIST exclusive create) before running; stale locks auto-cleared (`runner.ts:319-339`).
5. **Post-run**: qmd reindex is spawned detached (`runner.ts:382-383`) after a successful commit SHA. Decay-prune also runs on the dream cadence (`runner.ts:374-377`).

The LaunchAgent / cron that actually calls `runPendingDream` at session end is not in this src directory — the `dream-pending` marker file is the inter-process signal.

#### Does dreaming PRODUCE the wiki notes?

**Yes** — dreaming is the **sole writer** to canonical memory markdown under `memory/{profile,project,tools}/`. The `memory_note` tool only appends an `AgentNote` event to the JSONL log and the inbox memtable (`extension.ts:795-818`); it explicitly does NOT write wiki files. The dream phase LLM takes raw events and inbox entries and serialises `DreamFile` objects back to disk. (`dream.ts:7`, `dream.ts:308`)

#### pi-memory's own consolidation

Yes, pi-memory has a separate consolidation path — it does not use dream-memory's dream runs:

- **Extraction fork** (`util.ts:599+`): fires as a `context:"fork"` child agent on `turn_end` (every N turns / on session shutdown), using `buildExtractionPrompt()` → the forked agent writes directly to `~/.pi/agent/memory/` using Write/Edit tools. Gated by CC-parity thresholds (50k new tokens AND 5 new tool calls since last extraction). (`util.ts:704-727`)
- **`/dream` command** (`dream.ts:28-83`): `enqueueDreamConsolidation()` enqueues a SQLite `extraction_jobs` job; `runNextDreamConsolidationWithAgent()` or `runNextDreamConsolidation()` process it. The agent path (`runNextDreamConsolidationWithAgent`) uses `ctx.forkAgent` to run `buildDreamMergePrompt()` against `MEMORY.md` for the project. The non-agent path (`runNextDreamConsolidation`) calls `upsertProjectMemoryIndex()` which writes directly. (`dream.ts:66-83`)
- Both write to `~/.pi/agent/memory/project/<slug>/MEMORY.md` or `profile/MEMORY.md`. This is entirely separate from dream-memory's ULID watermark / staging / git-commit pipeline.

---

### 3. DEDUPE

#### Write / consolidation-time dedup (patch-applier)

Three mechanisms in `patch-applier.ts`:

1. **`replace_file` noop-on-equal** (`patch-applier.ts:142-143`): in `applyOne()`, after computing the full serialised content for a `replace_file` op, if `existing?.content === content` the action is `"noop"` and the file is not written. Exact citation: `patch-applier.ts:142`.

2. **`append_to_section` block/line/none dedup** (`patch-applier.ts:280-297`): `appendToSection()` takes the `dedupe` field from the patch (`"block" | "line" | "none"`). It splits both existing section content and new content by either paragraph blocks or lines, builds a `Set` of normalized existing blocks, and filters out additions that are already present (when dedupe !== "none"). Exact citations: `patch-applier.ts:280`, `patch-applier.ts:289-292`.

3. **`source_event_ids` union (provenance merge)** (`patch-applier.ts:170-182`): `mergeProvenance()` computes the union of existing `source_event_ids` array and new patch ids, capped at `PROVENANCE_CAP = 200` entries (oldest truncated). Applied on every patch op via `mergeSectionFrontmatter()` and directly in `replace_file`. Exact citations: `patch-applier.ts:170`, `patch-applier.ts:48`.

#### Cross-source / cross-note dedup (supersedes, decay, merge)

1. **`supersedes` frontmatter**: The schema (`schema.ts:26`) defines `supersedes: z.array(z.string()).optional()` — an optional array of permalinks the current file supersedes. The LLM prompt instructions in both `buildDreamPrompt()` and `buildPatchPrompt()` explicitly instruct: "Set `supersedes: ['<old-permalink>']` on the surviving file when absorbing another" (`dream.ts:796-797`). No code automatically reads or enforces `supersedes` after write — it is a human/LLM-facing convention only. The patch-applier does not act on it.

2. **Merge-at-dream-time dedup**: Both the full-mode and patch-mode prompts instruct the LLM to check the full file index before creating any new file, merge into existing files rather than creating duplicates, and consolidate files sharing ≥3 identical Recall trigger phrases (`dream.ts:787-803`, `dream.ts:663-666`). The file index injected is ALL memory files (via `listAllMemoryFiles()`, `dream.ts:1208`), not just the 64 shown in the content snapshot.

3. **Temporal decay**: Both extensions share the same `decayWeight()` formula (`decay.ts` in both — the dream-memory copy is explicitly a verbatim mirror, `dream-memory/src/decay.ts:5`). Formula: `recency = 2^(-ageDays/halfLifeDays); usageBoost = 1 - 1/(1+usageCount); weight = recency + (1 - recency) * usageBoost * 0.5`. Applied at **recall ranking time** only — mutates `hit.score` in `applyDecayRanking()` (`recall-selection.ts:273`). The auto-delete pass (`decay-prune.ts`) runs on dream cadence and hard-deletes files from pi-memory's corpus that are ≥90 days old AND usage_count ≤ 0 (`decay-prune.ts:59-111`). **Decay does not deduplicate cross-note content**; it only rank-suppresses or deletes stale never-recalled notes.

4. **No automated cross-note merging outside the LLM**: Other than the LLM instructions, there is no code-level pass that detects two notes with overlapping content and merges them.

#### Inject-time / recall dedup

**dream-memory active recall** (`active-memory.ts:361-371`): After fetching `qmdHits`, deduplicates by permalink using a `Set<string>`. The key is `h.permalink ?? h.title + h.file_path`. Then filters by `cfg.min_score`. Caps at `cfg.max_hits`. This is pure within-request dedup of the qmd result set — it does NOT deduplicate against what passive recall already injected, or against the session system prompt.

```typescript
// active-memory.ts:361-371
const seen = new Set<string>();
const hits: SearchHit[] = [];
for (const h of qmdHits) {
  const key = h.permalink ?? `${h.title}\u0000${h.file_path ?? ""}`;
  if (seen.has(key)) continue;
  seen.add(key);
  ...
  hits.push(h);
}
```

**pi-memory recall** (`recall.ts:84-94`): `finalizeRecall()` sorts candidates by score and slices to `maxCandidates`. No explicit dedup by permalink — the lexical scorer and qmd scorer are already separate and the results are merged/sorted, but there is no dedup Set for same-path hits from both sources.

**Cross-extension double-injection gap — confirmed present**: dream-memory's active recall queries `["pi-memory", "scars", "changes"]` (`recall-routing.ts:23-27`). Pi-memory's own recall separately injects a `## Relevant memory` block via `before_agent_start` in `index.ts` (the pi-memory extension's `buildMemoryIndexSnapshot()` / `renderRecall()`). **There is no coordination between the two**. A file in `~/.pi/agent/memory/` can appear in pi-memory's system-prompt injection AND in dream-memory's active recall injection in the same turn. No dedup-against-already-injected logic exists in either extension. The two injections use different XML wrapper tags (`<persistent-memory>` vs `<active-recall>`) and fire at different hook points, but the model receives duplicate content without any dedup signal.

Key citations for this gap:
- dream-memory active recall collections: `recall-routing.ts:23-27`
- pi-memory recall injection: `util.ts:293-307` (`buildParentMemoryPromptSection`) + pi-memory `index.ts` session start hook
- No cross-extension dedup: there is no shared state or coordination between `runActiveRecall()` in dream-memory and the pi-memory recall injection path

The default collection name is `"dream-memory"` (`store.ts:774`), but the system distinguishes profile- and project-scoped sub-collections: `dream-memory-profile` and `dream-memory-project` (referenced in `recall-routing.ts:16` and in pi-memory's `config.ts:314`). The qmd reindex is triggered by `runner.ts:382-383` via `spawnDetachedQmdReindex()` after a successful commit SHA.

**pi-memory** runs a debounced `qmd update` after every memory write (per the CLAUDE.md: "After every write, a debounced (500ms) `qmd update` runs fire-and-forget"). Its collection is `"pi-memory"` (`config.ts:313`); it can also federate across `["pi-memory", "dream-memory-profile", "dream-memory-project", "dream-memory-tools"]` (`config.ts:314`). The corpus on disk is `~/.pi/agent/memory/` (pi-memory's `memoryRoot()`; `util.ts:10`).

Active recall (dream-memory extension) queries `["pi-memory", "scars", "changes"]` by default — notably **excluding** `dream-memory-profile` and `dream-memory-project` because those are already deterministically injected into every session's system prompt (`recall-routing.ts:16-21`, `recall-routing.ts:23-27`).

---

### 2. DREAMING

#### Two dream modes: "fast" (default) vs "agentic"

**Fast mode** (default, `DREAM_AGENTIC` not set):
- **Reads**: JSONL event files in `~/.dream-memory/events/<sessionId>.jsonl` (via `readEventsSince()`, `store.ts:492`), the inbox memtable `memory/inbox/notes.md` (via `readInbox()`, `store.ts:399`), the wiki markdown snapshot (via `readMemoryTree()` — up to 64 files / 64 kB, `dream.ts:1202-1204`), a file index of all memory paths (via `listAllMemoryFiles()`, `dream.ts:1208`), and the live pi-memory snapshot (MEMORY.md, SCRATCHPAD.md, last 7 daily logs from `~/.pi/agent/memory/`, `dream.ts:137-177`).
- **Calls**: Pi's LLM (sonnet-class via `piRuntimeMerger`, `dream.ts:892`) with a prompt built by `buildDreamPrompt()` / `buildPatchPrompt()` (`dream.ts:672`).
- **Writes**: Staged files under `<eventsRoot>/staging/<run-id>/`, then copies into `memory/` under `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`, runs `git add -A` + `git commit` in the vault, updates per-session ULID watermarks, evicts processed inbox entries. (`dream.ts:1011+`, `runner.ts:354-355`)
- **Mode toggle**: `DREAM_MERGER_MODE=patch` switches to the patch-only LLM output format (`dream.ts:604-606`).

**Agentic mode** (`DREAM_AGENTIC=1`):
- **Reads**: Nothing directly — instead spawns `pi --source child-agent --print --mode json <prompt>` as a subprocess (`agentic.ts:228`). The prompt lists new session JSONL files since `last-dream.json`, instructs the sub-agent to grep the events dir and read `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/`. Optionally reads `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/MEMORY.md` as read-only source context.
- **Writes**: The spawned `pi` subprocess writes directly to `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/` using Write/Edit tools. No staging, no git commit, no ULID watermark advancement. (`agentic.ts:5-12`, `agentic.ts:317-319`)
- **Watermark**: NOT advanced. Only `last-dream.json` timestamp is updated on success (`agentic.ts:393`).
- **Progress**: Watched by monitoring `tool_execution_end` events on stdout for `write`/`edit` tool calls (`agentic.ts:249-259`).

#### Cadence / trigger chain

1. **On `session_shutdown`**: `extension.ts:1542` calls `dispatchStop()` → `harness-cli.ts:606` calls `maybeEnqueueDream(sessionId)`.
2. **`maybeEnqueueDream`** (`harness-cli.ts:285-312`): counts non-Stop events since the watermark for this session; if ≥1 event OR inbox bytes ≥ threshold, writes `~/.dream-memory/dream-pending` JSON marker file.
3. **Runner pickup**: `runPendingDream()` in `runner.ts:295` reads the marker, applies time gate (≥ `GATE_MIN_HOURS` = 24h since last dream, `runner.ts:22`) AND session gate (≥ `GATE_MIN_SESSIONS` = 5 sessions since last dream, `runner.ts:23`). Gates can be bypassed with `skipGates: true` (used by `/dream now`, `extension.ts:533`).
4. **Lock**: acquires `dream-runner.lock` (EEXIST exclusive create) before running; stale locks auto-cleared (`runner.ts:319-339`).
5. **Post-run**: qmd reindex is spawned detached (`runner.ts:382-383`) after a successful commit SHA. Decay-prune also runs on the dream cadence (`runner.ts:374-377`).

The LaunchAgent / cron that actually calls `runPendingDream` at session end is not in this src directory — the `dream-pending` marker file is the inter-process signal.

#### Does dreaming PRODUCE the wiki notes?

**Yes** — dreaming is the **sole writer** to canonical memory markdown under `memory/{profile,project,tools}/`. The `memory_note` tool only appends an `AgentNote` event to the JSONL log and the inbox memtable (`extension.ts:795-818`); it explicitly does NOT write wiki files. The dream phase LLM takes raw events and inbox entries and serialises `DreamFile` objects back to disk. (`dream.ts:7`, `dream.ts:308`)

#### pi-memory's own consolidation

Yes, pi-memory has a separate consolidation path — it does not use dream-memory's dream runs:

- **Extraction fork** (`util.ts:599+`): fires as a `context:"fork"` child agent on `turn_end` (every N turns / on session shutdown), using `buildExtractionPrompt()` → the forked agent writes directly to `~/.pi/agent/memory/` using Write/Edit tools. Gated by CC-parity thresholds (50k new tokens AND 5 new tool calls since last extraction). (`util.ts:704-727`)
- **`/dream` command** (`dream.ts:28-83`): `enqueueDreamConsolidation()` enqueues a SQLite `extraction_jobs` job; `runNextDreamConsolidationWithAgent()` or `runNextDreamConsolidation()` process it. The agent path (`runNextDreamConsolidationWithAgent`) uses `ctx.forkAgent` to run `buildDreamMergePrompt()` against `MEMORY.md` for the project. The non-agent path (`runNextDreamConsolidation`) calls `upsertProjectMemoryIndex()` which writes directly. (`dream.ts:66-83`)
- Both write to `~/.pi/agent/memory/project/<slug>/MEMORY.md` or `profile/MEMORY.md`. This is entirely separate from dream-memory's ULID watermark / staging / git-commit pipeline.

---

### 3. DEDUPE

#### Write / consolidation-time dedup (patch-applier)

Three mechanisms in `patch-applier.ts`:

1. **`replace_file` noop-on-equal** (`patch-applier.ts:142-143`): in `applyOne()`, after computing the full serialised content for a `replace_file` op, if `existing?.content === content` the action is `"noop"` and the file is not written. Exact citation: `patch-applier.ts:142`.

2. **`append_to_section` block/line/none dedup** (`patch-applier.ts:280-297`): `appendToSection()` takes the `dedupe` field from the patch (`"block" | "line" | "none"`). It splits both existing section content and new content by either paragraph blocks or lines, builds a `Set` of normalized existing blocks, and filters out additions that are already present (when dedupe !== "none"). Exact citations: `patch-applier.ts:280`, `patch-applier.ts:289-292`.

3. **`source_event_ids` union (provenance merge)** (`patch-applier.ts:170-182`): `mergeProvenance()` computes the union of existing `source_event_ids` array and new patch ids, capped at `PROVENANCE_CAP = 200` entries (oldest truncated). Applied on every patch op via `mergeSectionFrontmatter()` and directly in `replace_file`. Exact citations: `patch-applier.ts:170`, `patch-applier.ts:48`.

#### Cross-source / cross-note dedup (supersedes, decay, merge)

1. **`supersedes` frontmatter**: The schema (`schema.ts:26`) defines `supersedes: z.array(z.string()).optional()` — an optional array of permalinks the current file supersedes. The LLM prompt instructions in both `buildDreamPrompt()` and `buildPatchPrompt()` explicitly instruct: "Set `supersedes: ['<old-permalink>']` on the surviving file when absorbing another" (`dream.ts:796-797`). No code automatically reads or enforces `supersedes` after write — it is a human/LLM-facing convention only. The patch-applier does not act on it.

2. **Merge-at-dream-time dedup**: Both the full-mode and patch-mode prompts instruct the LLM to check the full file index before creating any new file, merge into existing files rather than creating duplicates, and consolidate files sharing ≥3 identical Recall trigger phrases (`dream.ts:787-803`, `dream.ts:663-666`). The file index injected is ALL memory files (via `listAllMemoryFiles()`, `dream.ts:1208`), not just the 64 shown in the content snapshot.

3. **Temporal decay**: Both extensions share the same `decayWeight()` formula (`decay.ts` in both — the dream-memory copy is explicitly a verbatim mirror, `dream-memory/src/decay.ts:5`). Formula: `recency = 2^(-ageDays/halfLifeDays); usageBoost = 1 - 1/(1+usageCount); weight = recency + (1 - recency) * usageBoost * 0.5`. Applied at **recall ranking time** only — mutates `hit.score` in `applyDecayRanking()` (`recall-selection.ts:273`). The auto-delete pass (`decay-prune.ts`) runs on dream cadence and hard-deletes files from pi-memory's corpus that are ≥90 days old AND usage_count ≤ 0 (`decay-prune.ts:59-111`). **Decay does not deduplicate cross-note content**; it only rank-suppresses or deletes stale never-recalled notes.

4. **No automated cross-note merging outside the LLM**: Other than the LLM instructions, there is no code-level pass that detects two notes with overlapping content and merges them.

#### Inject-time / recall dedup

**dream-memory active recall** (`active-memory.ts:361-371`): After fetching `qmdHits`, deduplicates by permalink using a `Set<string>`. The key is `h.permalink ?? h.title + h.file_path`. Then filters by `cfg.min_score`. Caps at `cfg.max_hits`. This is pure within-request dedup of the qmd result set — it does NOT deduplicate against what passive recall already injected, or against the session system prompt.

```typescript
// active-memory.ts:361-371
const seen = new Set<string>();
const hits: SearchHit[] = [];
for (const h of qmdHits) {
  const key = h.permalink ?? `${h.title}\u0000${h.file_path ?? ""}`;
  if (seen.has(key)) continue;
  seen.add(key);
  ...
  hits.push(h);
}
```

**pi-memory recall** (`recall.ts:84-94`): `finalizeRecall()` sorts candidates by score and slices to `maxCandidates`. No explicit dedup by permalink — the lexical scorer and qmd scorer are already separate and the results are merged/sorted, but there is no dedup Set for same-path hits from both sources.

**Cross-extension double-injection gap — confirmed present**: dream-memory's active recall queries `["pi-memory", "scars", "changes"]` (`recall-routing.ts:23-27`). Pi-memory's own recall separately injects a `## Relevant memory` block via `before_agent_start` in `index.ts` (the pi-memory extension's `buildMemoryIndexSnapshot()` / `renderRecall()`). **There is no coordination between the two**. A file in `~/.pi/agent/memory/` can appear in pi-memory's system-prompt injection AND in dream-memory's active recall injection in the same turn. No dedup-against-already-injected logic exists in either extension. The two injections use different XML wrapper tags (`<persistent-memory>` vs `<active-recall>`) and fire at different hook points, but the model receives duplicate content without any dedup signal.

Key citations for this gap:
- dream-memory active recall collections: `recall-routing.ts:23-27`
- pi-memory recall injection: `util.ts:293-307` (`buildParentMemoryPromptSection`) + pi-memory `index.ts` session start hook
- No cross-extension dedup: there is no shared state or coordination between `runActiveRecall()` in dream-memory and the pi-memory recall injection path

                                   shared/ + harness/{pi,claude-code,codex}/ + episodic/ + inbox/
                                                              │
                          ┌───────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
                          ▼                                   ▼                                ▼
                  dream/consolidate                   qmd indexes canonical          recall candidates =
                  (patch + decay + tombstone)         (tombstone-aware, ACL-filtered)  global MINUS self,
                          │                                                            tail-only
                          ▼                                                                  │
                  core-snapshots/<harness>/<scope>/<epoch>.md                              ┌─┴─ per-harness INJECTOR
                  (promoted at consolidation; renders the cached core)                     │   (pi-memory for Pi;
                                                                                           │    CC/Codex native)
                                                                                           ▼
                                                              core @ SessionStart+compaction (from snapshot)
                                                              recall @ turn (tail; ACL-enforced; no embedding-delete)
```

**Injection is per-harness, never centralized.** The bridge *computes* recall candidates but does not inject; each harness's own injector speaks. For Pi, `pi-memory` is the sole model-facing injector for both core and recall tail — the bridge MUST NOT touch Pi's cached base or transcript (a single-owner injection guard, P4, scans the final Pi `system`/tools/SessionStart/recall for duplicate or dream-owned blocks before release).

**Canonical harness IDs (one enum, used in paths, provenance, qmd collection names, tests, docs):** `pi`, `claude-code`, `codex`. No informal aliases (`cc`, `claude`, `claude-code-native`).

Namespacing: `shared/` (cross-harness) ∪ `harness/X` (X-specific). **`origin ≠ visibility`** — recall surfacing is decided by the `visibility` field, not by where a fact was captured; an origin-`codex` fact reaches Pi only if classified `shared`/`visibility:harness:pi`, and a generally-useful fact is promoted to `shared` by a rule, not left stranded under its origin. Structured frontmatter on every record:

```yaml
origin:          codex            # where captured (provenance, not a visibility decision)
visibility:      private | harness:<x> | project:<slug> | shared
sensitivity:     public | private | secret
scope:           profile | project:<slug> | tool:<name> | harness:<x>
confidence:      extracted | consolidated | confirmed
provenance:                       # for migration/dedup/audit/rollback (M2)
  source_store:   pi | obsidian | claude-code | codex-memories | chronicle
  source_path:    <path>
  source_span:    <line/offset>
  source_content_hash: <sha>
  source_record_id:    <id>
  migration_batch_id:  <id>
  first_seen / last_seen: <ts>
  capture_mechanism:   native | harvest | dream | manual
supersedes:      [<id>]           # corrections only
```
New harvested/captured facts default to `visibility: private` (origin-private) + `sensitivity: private`, promoted only by the classification pass.

## Phases (become ordered child issues once the tracker is approved)

> **Hard gates run early, not at soak (M5).** Each dangerous failure class is gated *before* the phase that could trigger it — claim-loss before P2 apply, lock/crash before P3, false-suppression before P4, byte-stability before P5, secret/PII isolation before any cross-harness recall. P7's soak confirms, it does not discover.

**P0 — Spec + ADRs.** This document + ADR 0007/0008. *Done when:* merged and indexed.

**P0.5 — Requalify the dream bridge (blocking; H7).** `memory-architecture.md` records dream-memory as retired / not in any profile manifest. Before it can own a canonical store: live hook-normalisation tests for `pi`/`claude-code`/`codex`; `patch-applier` idempotency tests; qmd index tests; recall injection-ownership test (bridge never injects for Pi); cache-byte-stability harness. Dead code is either removed or reactivated under an explicit feature flag. *Gate:* the pipeline is proven live + soak-able, not assumed. **Also resolve here:** does Pi expose a compaction event to extensions or is a fork hook required (empirical — see below); `pi-memory` is a **full write-path repoint** (decided 2026-06-22, not a shim): rewrite its write/extraction to natively emit canonical `inbox/` events with structured frontmatter + provenance, making it a first-class canonical capture writer. Both are cache-safety / single-writer preconditions (H8), not P3/P5 details.

**P1 — Canonical skeleton + routing + qmd re-point.** Define `~/.agents/memory` layout + structured frontmatter (above). **Rewrite `recall-routing.ts` for canonical collections *before* the qmd cutover (H3):** add collection names/aliases for canonical `shared`/`harness/*`/`episodic`, old `pi-memory`, old `dream-memory-{profile,project}`, `scars`, `changes`; the router currently defaults to `pi-memory`/`scars`/`changes` and excludes dream collections on the now-stale assumption they are injected deterministically. **P2 — One-off migration via a claim-level ledger (C5/M2).** Union pi + obsidian as full members; ingest CC/Codex + chronicle (→ `episodic/`) as read-only sources. **Replace file-count reconciliation with a claim ledger:** extract atomic claims (source store, path, span, content hash, timestamp, scope); every source claim maps to exactly one of {canonical record, conflict group, explicit quarantine/reject}; canonical IDs are content-addressed or ledger-assigned (never LLM-invented); huge files (267 KB Codex `MEMORY.md`, 438 KB `raw_memories.md`) chunked with spans preserved; the LLM may *propose* merges but is **not** the deletion authority. Apply is transactional (temp tree → validate → atomic swap → retain rollback snapshot → rebuild qmd); reruns consult the ledger + source hashes, not fresh LLM judgment. Run **dry-run → quarantine review → apply**. *Gate (before apply):* ledger maps 100% of source claims with no unexplained drops; a forced mid-apply crash rolls back clean (or resumes clean); idempotent re-run is a ledger-verified no-op — not an aspiration.

**P3 — Harvest watchers + concurrency safety (H4).** Diff CC + Codex native dirs on SessionStart/Stop → enqueue events into `inbox/`; **one consolidator** applies patches under a **global canonical-store write lock + per-scope locks**, via a write-ahead log; file writes are temp-file + fsync + atomic rename; qmd consumes **committed snapshots only**. Never write back into native dirs. Harvested entries land in `inbox/quarantine/<origin>/` as origin-private. *Gate (before concurrent harvesters run):* a new CC native memory lands in canonical within one boundary; native dirs untouched; a kill-during-apply crash test verifies clean rollback/resume; no lost-update under a Pi-repoint + CC-harvest + Codex-harvest race.

**P4 — Dedup-on-inject + ACL + per-harness scope.** Inject `global − self` **tail-only**: exact source-ID / normalised-text-hash match first; qmd embedding similarity **only ranks/flags candidates, never deletes or suppresses** (a candidate with negation/correction/date/number/repo/tool/scope language defaults to injected — H1). Recall enforces **ACL (visibility/sensitivity) before qmd ranking and again before final injection**; recall scope = `shared ∪ harness/X` by *visibility*, not origin (H6). When canonical contradicts a still-surfacing native fact, inject an explicit appended correction (C3). *Gate (before any cross-harness recall is live):* no in-context duplication of a self-injected fact; a self-injected stale fact's canonical correction is **never** suppressed; a `sensitivity:secret`/origin-private fact never crosses a harness boundary (secret/PII isolation test); a CC-specific learning is not injected to Pi.

**P5 — Cache contract (ADR 0008).** Core renders from a **versioned promoted snapshot** (`core-snapshots/<harness>/<scope>/<epoch>.md`), epoch bumped only at consolidation — never a live read of canonical. `PreCompact` (and Pi compaction, per P0.5) subscription re-renders the *current* epoch; soft-invalidate removal (tombstone + decay), physical prune at consolidation only; tombstone-aware retrieval. Mutability classes enforced (no corrections/secrets/“do-not-X” in core); critical-revocation tail block for high-harm overrides. *Gate (before daily-driver cutover):* **two same-cwd sessions with canonical mutated between them render byte-identical `system + tools[]`**; mutation re-renders only at a boundary; tombstoned fact never appears in recall; `pi-cache-stability` checklist passes. Any fork hook logged in `pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.

Snapshot-replay overlap@5 / rank-correlation is a **smoke test only — it is circular** (corpus already shaped by the own stack). The build-vs-buy *decision* stands on grounds the benchmark can't measure (ADR 0007 D6). Record **falsification criteria**: run Mem0/Letta as non-injecting live shadows over the same raw event stream, same privacy filters, no access to canonical labels; compare on blinded recall-usefulness, correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, wrong-action prevention, write precision, latency, cost, cache-base churn. *Gate:* bench runs green; result recorded as smoke + the falsification criteria documented (not "own ≥ shadows on the circular metric").

**P7 — Cutover + retire old roots.** Make canonical the source of truth; **Obsidian → read-only view with an explicit contract: generated from canonical, no edits accepted, no sync-back** (editable later only via an `inbox/import` queue with provenance + review — L2). Decommission the dual-read shim; rewrite `memory-architecture.md` as the descriptive map. *Gate:* full extension gate + fork gate green; 30-session soak **confirms** the metric set (the dangerous classes were already gated in P2–P5).

## Proof / gates (program-level)

Metric set inherited from the 2026-06-10 disposition: cache-base churn, recall precision, recall usefulness (did it change the next action?), user-correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool-call overhead, prompt bytes per session. Each phase ships its own gate above; P7 is the soak.

## Repoint design (P0.5 residual) — what survives: autowiki · dreaming · dedupe

**Architecture as found (corrects the earlier mental model).** `pi-memory` and `dream-memory` are **two separate, simultaneously-mounted Pi extensions** with their own stores, not one extension with a Pi half. Two consequences shape the repoint:

1. **Live double-injection of Pi's profile core.** Both register a `systemPrompt:build` profile-base filter at **priority 10** (`pi-memory/src/index.ts:81-91`, `dream-memory/src/extension.ts:380-404`) *and* both append a system-prompt block in `before_agent_start` (pi-memory `INJECT_MARKER` `index.ts:314-324`; dream-memory `<persistent-memory>` `extension.ts:1417-1507`). Pi receives profile memory **twice**, from two stores, in its cacheable base. No cross-extension dedup exists in either (`active-memory.ts:361` dedups only within its own qmd result set). Killing this duplication is a primary payoff of the unification, not a nicety.
2. **Canonical store is a read dead-end today.** Agentic dream already *writes* `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/` (`agentic.ts:317`), but Pi injection *reads* `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` (the wiki). Nothing reads canonical back. "Repoint" = make the injector read what the consolidator writes.

**End state.** *One* consolidation authority writes canonical (ADR 0007 D2). `pi-memory` becomes the **sole Pi injector** (D2/P4), reading the promoted core snapshot (ADR 0008) and the recall tail; `dream-memory` **stops injecting for Pi** — drops its priority-10 profile filter and its `before_agent_start` append for the `pi` client, retaining only consolidation + capture. The single-injector guard (P4) is what removes the double-injection by construction.

**Autowiki — preserved (with one honesty note).** There is **no backlink/wikilink graph today**: `[[…]]` is only a hint string in the `memory_note` description (`extension.ts:745`), never parsed/indexed, and `## Relations`/`## Observations` are *stripped* on every write (`dream.ts:310-316`). What "autowiki" actually is = markdown + YAML frontmatter (`permalink`, `scope`, `supersedes`) + the **Obsidian vault** that opens it + the **qmd index**. All three survive unchanged: canonical stays Obsidian-readable markdown; the vault repoints to a read-only view that **symlinks both canonical roots** (P7 read-only contract); qmd reindexes canonical (collections `dream-memory-*` → canonical names, the `recall-routing.ts` rewrite already gated in P1). *Opt-in future:* a genuine bidirectional link graph is net-new — flagged, not assumed.

**Dreaming — preserved.** The consolidator engine and cadence are unchanged: `Stop → dream-pending marker → runner` with the 24h / 5-session gates + lock + post-run qmd reindex + decay-prune (`harness-cli.ts:285-312`, `runner.ts:295-383`). Two changes: (a) the canonical write becomes the default (agentic mode already writes `~/.agents/...`; fast mode repoints `wikiRoot()`/`memoryDir()` → canonical); (b) **today's two consolidators collapse to one** — `pi-memory`'s own extraction-fork + `/dream` path (`pi-memory/src/dream.ts`, `util.ts:599+`) stops consolidating into `~/.pi/agent/memory/` and instead emits append-only `inbox/` capture events (the decided full write-path repoint); the single dream consolidator promotes. Dreaming still **produces** the notes — it is the sole canonical writer.

**Dedupe — three layers, all kept, one strengthened.**
- **L1 write/consolidation-time** (keep as-is): `patch-applier` — `append_to_section` block/line dedup (`patch-applier.ts:280-297`), `replace_file` noop-on-equal (`:142`), `source_event_ids` provenance union capped at 200 (`:170-182`).
- **L2 cross-source / cross-note** (strengthened by P2): today LLM-prompt-driven (merge into existing, consolidate ≥3 shared triggers, `supersedes`) + decay-prune (`decay-prune.ts:59-111`, rank/delete only — never content-merge). The unification adds the **claim-level ledger** (P2): the same fact arriving from Pi/CC/Codex inboxes maps to one canonical claim; the LLM may *propose* merges but is never the deletion authority; `supersedes` stays a correction convention; embedding stays a candidate signal (D5).
- **L3 inject-time** (the fix): today each extension dedups only within its own request and **never against the other** → the double-injection above. End state: one Pi injector reading the promoted snapshot ⇒ no cross-injector duplicate by construction, plus P4 dedup-on-inject (`global − self`, tail-only, exact-ID/hash match — embedding never suppresses).

**Concrete call sites the repoint touches** (from code survey): `store.ts:54-64` `wikiRoot()`/`memoryDir()`; `harness-cli.ts:360-366` `dispatchSessionStart` (inherits via `memoryDir()`); `dream/dream.ts` fast-mode writes; `active-memory.ts` + `recall-routing.ts:16-27` qmd collection targets; `pi-memory/src/profile-base.ts:31-38` `wikiHome()`; `pi-memory/src/util.ts:10` `memoryRoot()` + its SQLite `db/memory.sqlite`. Pi receives profile memory **twice**, from two stores, in its cacheable base. No cross-extension dedup exists in either (`active-memory.ts:361` dedups only within its own qmd result set). Killing this duplication is a primary payoff of the unification, not a nicety.
2. **Canonical store is a read dead-end today.** Agentic dream already *writes* `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/` (`agentic.ts:317`), but Pi injection *reads* `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` (the wiki). Nothing reads canonical back. "Repoint" = make the injector read what the consolidator writes.

The single-injector guard (P4) is what removes the double-injection by construction.

**Autowiki — preserved (with one honesty note).** There is **no backlink/wikilink graph today**: `[[…]]` is only a hint string in the `memory_note` description (`extension.ts:745`), never parsed/indexed, and `## Relations`/`## Observations` are *stripped* on every write (`dream.ts:310-316`). # ADRs

## Objective

Keep a thin, durable decision log for each bounded context so future agents know why the codebase is shaped this way.

## Workflow

1. Verify the repo/context:
   - Work from the git root.
   - If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, use it to choose the bounded context.
   - Otherwise use root `docs/adr/`.
2. Read existing ADRs in the chosen context before proposing a decision change.
3. Offer or create an ADR only when all three are true:
   - **Hard to reverse** — changing course later has meaningful cost.
   - **Surprising without context** — a future reader will wonder why this path was chosen.
   - **Real trade-off** — genuine alternatives existed and one was chosen for specific reasons.
4. If any criterion is missing, skip the ADR:
   - Use a code comment for local implementation rationale.
   - Use a commit/PR note for historical change details.
   - Use no artifact for obvious or reversible choices.
5. Create one ADR per decision. Number it `NNNN-kebab-title.md`, incrementing from the highest existing ADR in that context.
6. Keep it short. Start with Matt Pocock's one-paragraph format; add sections only when they carry real decision memory.
7. Update `CONTEXT-MAP.md` only when adding a new bounded context or moving the ADR location.

## Placement

- Single-context repo → `docs/adr/` at repo root.
- Multi-context repo → root `docs/adr/` for system-wide decisions; `<context>/docs/adr/` for context-specific decisions.
- One stack of ADRs per bounded context.

## References

- For the ADR template and examples of what qualifies, read `references/format.md`.

- Zoom out / map unfamiliar code area → `references/zoom-out.md`.
- Throwaway prototype for logic or UI exploration → `references/prototype/SKILL.md`, then pick `LOGIC.md` or `UI.md`.

It is review-only, recommends the next artifact (PRD / issues / handoff), and stops before implementation.

## Import note

Current upstream source: `https://github.com/mattpocock/skills` (synced against commit `6eeb81b`, 2026-06-18).

These refs are a **curated, locally-adapted subset**, not a mirror. Upstream has since reorganized into a categorized plugin monorepo (`skills/engineering/*`, `skills/productivity/*`, multi-file skill dirs, Claude-Code `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter) and in several cases replaced self-contained skills with thin pointers to new upstream-only skills (`grill-me` → `/grilling`, `tdd` → `/codebase-design`). A wholesale re-sync would be a migration, not a refresh: it would regress the richer local `grill-with-docs` / `improve-codebase-architecture`, drop the local "use when" trigger descriptions, and introduce dangling references. So the full restructure is intentionally **out of scope**. The 2026-06-18 refresh adopted only safe additive upstream improvements (`to-prd` single-seam guidance, `to-issues` prefactor maxim) and preserved local-only refs (`fix-until-green`, `zoom-out`, `caveman`, `write-a-skill`).

Keep these as child refs, not standalone global skills, so Luke's primary skills stay canonical unless a Matt workflow is explicitly requested.

1	# ADR 0007: Unified cross-harness memory store (`~/.agents/memory`)
2	
3	**Status:** Proposed (2026-06-22) — decisions locked with Luke; moves to Accepted when the P0.5 blocking preconditions (Consequences) close.
4	**Related:** `docs/memory-architecture.md`, `docs/memory-systems-comparison.md`, `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md`, ADR 0008, the 2026-06-10 A/B-deadline disposition in `memory-architecture.md`
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	Memory had diverged across five stores: `pi-memory` (`~/.pi/agent/memory/`), the dream bridge (`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`), Claude Code native auto-memory (`~/.claude/projects/<proj>/memory/`), Codex native memories + chronicle (`~/.codex/memories/`), and the `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` eval lanes. The two agent-facing stores were already disjoint (124 vs 81 profile files, different filenames; 25 vs 39 project dirs) — neither a superset of the other. Per-store consolidators on divergent corpora is the named industry anti-pattern (definition drift, irreconcilable conflicts).
9	
10	Two forcing functions converged. (1) The requirement that **CC/Codex learnings be *actively recalled* like Pi's**, not merely injected once at session start. (2) The 2026-06-10 disposition in `memory-architecture.md` set an A/B deadline (2026-06-30 / 30 sessions) to *choose the primary memory path*. This ADR resolves that deadline.
