That's the complete picture. Here's what the docs say, concretely.

---

## Claude Code Memory & Staleness — As of June 2026

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (updated 2026-06-22)

---

### 1. CLAUDE.md files

**Always loaded, every session — unconditionally.**

- Walked up from cwd; every `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and `.claude/rules/*.md` in the directory hierarchy above cwd is concatenated into context at launch, ordered root→cwd.
- Subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` files lazy-load on demand when Claude reads a file in that subdirectory.

content.text:
Both your points land, and the research backs you up hard. Here's the synthesis — including one place I had it wrong.

## Point 1: you're right — I had the "exclude" tier wrong

My earlier "hard-filter `status:superseded` out of recall" was wrong, for exactly the reason you gave: a filtered record is *unreachable*, so recall can't surface it even when a query genuinely wants history ("what was the old tunnel approach before the NetworkPolicy fix?"). The external research is unambiguous that the right move is **soft demotion via weighting**, not deletion:

- **Mem0** explicitly designed this: memory decay "leaves memories in place but down-ranks them at retrieval" — a recent memory gets a ~1.5× boost, an idle one dampened toward 0.3× — "a 5× spread between fresh and stale, enough to meaningfully reorder candidates without ever swamping the underlying relevance score." ([Mem0: Introducing Memory Decay](https://mem0.ai/blog/introducing-memory-decay-in-mem0))
- Their own caveat is the key nuance: "Decay handles low-relevance memories. Staleness in **high-relevance** memories is the harder, open problem" — the fix is "time-based decay **on top of** supersession, so old facts gradually lose retrieval weight even without a contradiction." ([Mem0: eviction & forgetting](https://mem0.ai/blog/memory-eviction-and-forgetting-in-ai-agents)) That's precisely your instinct: supersede *and* age both feed one weight.
- **Claude Code is the cautionary tale.** It has **no decay, no staleness detection, no recency weighting, no expiry** — CLAUDE.md + the auto-memory `MEMORY.md` are always-loaded and "everything is equally authoritative." Its only pressure valve is a dumb 200-line/25KB truncation that silently drops overflow. ([CC memory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md)) So CC punts entirely — we're already ahead of it because we *have* decay ranking. Copying CC would be a regression.

### The revised read-path model — one score, not a filter
Everything stays in the qmd index and stays reachable. Surfacing is a single multiplicative score, extending the `decayWeight` we already have (`decay.ts:34` does `recency + (1−recency)·usageBoost·0.5`):

```
score = semantic_similarity
      × decay(age, last_used)          ← already built
      × statusWeight(active 1.0, superseded ≈0.3)   ← NEW: fold supersede in as a penalty, not a filter
      × confidenceWeight(confirmed > consolidated > extracted)  ← NEW
```

Then **freshness caveats on whatever survives** (dream-memory already wraps >1-day-old hits in `<system-reminder>` tags via `recall-selection.ts` — that's the safety net that makes surfacing a superseded record safe: it comes with "this was corrected by X").

**The one thing that stays a hard gate is ACL** — `sensitivity:secret` and cross-harness `visibility`. That's not a relevance question, it's a security/privacy invariant: a secret must *never* auto-surface across a boundary no matter how relevant. So: **relevance/staleness → soft weight; security/privacy → hard gate.** That's the whole distinction.

## Point 2: dreaming already skips dormant projects — and the cheap/expensive split is the answer

I checked the runner. Consolidation is **already event-watermark-gated**: "no events since watermark and inbox empty; skip" (`dream.ts:1062`), "all events are noise; skipping LLM, advancing watermarks only" (`dream.ts:1144`). It processes *new inbox events*, which only touch scopes you actually worked in — it does **not** iterate and re-dream every project. So the token waste you're worried about is largely avoided by construction today.

The clean principle to lock in:

- **Expensive work (LLM consolidation / index revision) = activity-gated.** Only re-render a scope's index/core-snapshot when that scope's watermark advanced (new events). A dormant project's epoch never bumps → zero LLM spend. This is already what P5 specifies ("epoch bumped only at consolidation").
- **Cheap work (decay) = always-on, everything.** Decay is pure SQL/math, no LLM (`decay.ts`). So a dormant project's facts *still* age out of relevance passively, for free — recall just quietly down-weights them. You get staleness handling on dormant projects **without** spending a token revising them.

So your two points reinforce each other: recall covers everything cheaply (weighted), consolidation touches only what's active (gated). Dormant projects cost nothing and still fade correctly.

## How the field handles it (steer)

| System | Staleness model | Takeaway for us |
|---|---|---|
| **Mem0** | Decay down-ranks, never deletes; recency boost ×1.5/×0.3; decay layered on supersession | The reference design — matches your instinct; we already have the decay primitive |
| **Zep/Graphiti** | Temporal knowledge graph with fact-validity windows; +15pts vs Mem0 on temporal retrieval | Heavier (validity intervals per fact) — overkill now, but the ceiling if recall quality matters later |
| **Claude Code** | None — always-load + manual edit + 200-line truncation | Anti-pattern; don't copy |

Sources: [Mem0 decay](https://mem0.ai/blog/introducing-memory-decay-in-mem0) · [Mem0 eviction/forgetting](https://mem0.ai/blog/memory-eviction-and-forgetting-in-ai-agents) · [State of AI Agent Memory 2026](https://mem0.ai/blog/state-of-ai-agent-memory-2026) · [Frameworks tested: Mem0/Zep/Letta](https://particula.tech/blog/agent-memory-frameworks-tested-mem0-zep-letta-cognee-2026) · [Claude Code memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md)

## Revised recommendation (replaces my earlier "#1 add status:active filter")

1. **Extend `decayWeight` to factor `status` + `confidence`** (one function, surgical) instead of filtering. Superseded ≈ heavy penalty, never excluded. Keep the existing freshness caveat on survivors.
2. **ACL stays the only hard gate** (secret/visibility) — that's P4 and it's security, not relevance.
3. **Scope-gate index/snapshot re-render** on watermark advance so dormant projects cost zero LLM; let decay demote them passively.

This changes ADR 0009 §5's recall contract from "filter `status:active`" to "**weight** status, never filter." That's a real, hard-to-reverse contract change with a tradeoff (a corrected fact *can* resurface, mitigated by the caveat) — exactly ADR-shaped.

State: decision required — want me to (a) amend **ADR 0009** (supersede recall: filter → decay-weight) + note the scope-gated-render rule, so it's the decision of record before any code, or (b) just proceed and fold it into the P4/P5 implementation when we get there? I'd do (a) first — it's the kind of call that should be written down before it's built. No code until you pick.

168	| **CC** | ~61 | ~116 tok | **7.1k** | **none — index not deferrable; hide-entirely is the only lever** |
169	
170	### 8e. Why CC's 7.1k skills index won't shrink via `skillListingBudgetFraction` — bundle-confirmed (binlens over v2.1.185)
171	
172	Luke's hypothesis ("the percentage is too small") was *half* right — it **is** small, but it's the wrong knob. Extracted from the Bun bundle with `binlens search`/`schema` (constants + application + over-budget UI):
173	
174	```js
175	function bPt(){ return qr().skillListingMaxDescChars ?? IEd }     // IEd = 1536 (default per-entry cap)
176	function j6r(){ return qr().skillListingBudgetFraction ?? kEd }   // kEd = 0.01 (default fraction)
177	function EPt(e,t){ let n=j6r(), r=(e??HEd)*t*n; return Math.max(1,Math.floor(r)) }  // budget = floor(windowChars × fraction)
178	// over-budget UI: "...raise skillListingBudgetFraction (currently <T>) in settings.json"
179	//                 "N descriptions exceed the per-entry cap: <cappedSkills>"
180	```
181	
182	- **Defaults:** fraction `kEd = 0.01` (1%), per-entry cap `IEd = 1536` chars. Luke ran `0.002` + `300`.
183	- `0.002` passes validation (`.gt(0).lte(1)`) and is read verbatim — **not floored**. `EPt` computes a genuinely small char budget from it.
184	- **But the budget is a soft total-ceiling that triggers a *warning*, not a truncation of the full listing.** When the listing exceeds budget, CC **caps each description to the per-entry cap (`maxSkillDescriptionChars`) and warns** — "N descriptions exceed the per-entry cap … raise `skillListingBudgetFraction` or disable some skills." It **never drops skills or names.**
185	- Therefore the 7.1k floor = **(model-visible skill count) × (name + ≤300-char description + XML wrapper)** — which the fraction cannot touch. Lowering it does nothing; raising it only permits more.
186	- **The only CC-native lever that moves 7.1k is cutting the model-visible count** (`skillOverrides: user-invocable-only`/`off`) — ~116 tok per skill removed — and/or lowering `maxSkillDescriptionChars`. The fraction override was deleted (reverted to default) because it was load-bearing for nothing.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Overarching program (active):** Get Claude Code and Codex to use Luke's Pi memory + dreaming with active recall (per-turn auto-injection) like Pi's. GitHub program tracker #388, phases P0.5–P7. P2 = issue #382. Spec: `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md` (ADRs 0007 unified store, 0008 cache contract, 0009 reconciliation contract).
   - **This session's completed arc:** Finish Task #4 (planner tests), build Task #5 (dry-run apply + `APPLY-DIFF.md` binding artifact), investigate the TOC-quarantine data-loss question.
   - **Luke ACCEPTED the lossless diff** as the binding sign-off on the migration CONTENT (1449 records, 0 dropped). Blanket MEMORY.md quarantine was rejected as unsafe.
   - **New design thread (active):** "how do we prune / make proper use of progressive disclosure instead of always loaded artifacts?" Luke then corrected the approach: stale/superseded records should be **soft decay-weighted, NOT hard-filtered** (so recall can still reach them); the MEMORY.md index should be revised regularly by dreaming, but **dormant projects must not be re-revised** (token waste). Luke asked for online research to steer this (how CC handles staleness).
   - **Luke approved (msg "1. yes 2. yep 3. ok cool"):** (1) extend decayWeight to factor status+confidence, (2) ACL stays the only hard gate, (3) scope-gate index/snapshot render — AND amend ADR 0009 (filter→decay-weight) to record the decision before code.
   - **Newest explicit request (the immediate task):** "check the claude code auto dreaming function, use binlens to see how it works and does it do any decay / filtering / dedupe etc?"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Disposition-vs-edge model (ADR 0009):** every eligible claim gets ONE disposition (novel|merge); supersede is an EDGE — superseding (new_id) claim is record bearer via its own novel/merge; superseded_id gets a record flagged `status:superseded` + `superseded_by`, drops from active recall. Verified: 1404 novel + 16 merge-canonical + 16 collapsed-members + 29 superseded = 1465 eligible; 1449 record bearers (1420 active + 29 superseded).
   - **Three runtime tiers (mapped from Explore agent):** Tier 1 always-loaded = `profile/MEMORY.md` + `project/<slug>/MEMORY.md` index files only, 24KB (SESSION_START_MAX_BYTES=24*1024) / 8-file / 150ms budget (harness-cli.ts:57-59). Tier 2 per-turn = passive recall (qmd top-5 USER_PROMPT_TOP_N + inbox top-3, 10KB) + active recall (haiku-curated, opt-in DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=1). Tier 3 on-demand tool = DOES NOT EXIST (no memory_search the model can call; no deferLoading).
   - **INERT frontmatter knobs (KEY FINDING):** status (active/superseded), sensitivity (secret/private), visibility, confidence are written but NOT enforced in any qmd search/recall path. Only decay weight + auto_none_threshold(0.4) + min_prompt_length(20) have runtime effect. Decay is RANKING only (never excludes); decay-PRUNE hard-deletes stale+low-usage on dream cadence.
   - **Decay model (decay.ts:34):** `weight = recency + (1-recency)*usageBoost*0.5`, `recency = 2^(-ageDays/halfLifeDays)`, halfLifeDays=30. Applied via applyDecayRanking (recall-selection.ts:273-298).
   - **DECISION (approved): soft decay-weight, not hard-filter.** Unified read-path score = `semantic_similarity × decay(age,last_used) × statusWeight(active 1.0, superseded ≈0.3) × confidenceWeight(confirmed>consolidated>extracted)`. ACL (secret/visibility) is the ONLY hard gate (security/privacy invariant, not relevance). Freshness caveats (`<system-reminder>` for >1day old, recall-selection.ts) make surfacing superseded safe. This changes ADR 0009 §5 from "filter status:active" to "weight status, never filter."
   - **DECISION (approved): expensive=activity-gated, cheap=always-on.** Dreaming/consolidation is already event-watermark-gated (dream.ts:1062, 1144) — skips dormant projects. Refine snapshot/index re-render to bump a scope's epoch only on watermark advance. Decay (SQL, no LLM) demotes dormant projects passively for free.
   - **Industry steer:** Mem0 = decay down-ranks never deletes (×1.5 recent/×0.3 idle, 5× spread; "decay on top of supersession"). Zep/Graphiti = temporal knowledge graph with fact-validity windows (+15pts vs Mem0). Claude Code = NO decay/dedup/staleness (always-load + manual curation + 200-line/25KB truncation; "everything equally authoritative") — the anti-pattern.
   - **binlens:** binary/bundle inspector at `/Users/luke/.local/bin/binlens`. Subcommands: search/schema/strings/xrefs. Flag `--max-scan-ms N` (default 90000). Streams `strings` for large binaries (200MB+). No `--help`/`help` (errors "unknown command"); bare `binlens` prints usage. Previously used over CC bundle v2.1.185 (findings-progressive-disclosure-impl.md §8e: `binlens search`/`schema` over the Bun bundle).
   - **Stack:** TS strict (NodeNext, .ts imports, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes), vitest, zod ^3.23.8, run via `pnpm tsx`. tsconfig include = src+tests (scripts/ excluded — typecheck scripts via in-dir temp tsconfig extending ./tsconfig.json). Package = `@valkyriweb/dream-memory-harness`.
   - **Worktree:** `/tmp/p2-reconcile-run`, branch `feat/p2-reconcile-run`, base origin/main fab66cd4. node_modules symlinked from primary.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`tests/migration-apply.spec.ts`** (CREATED, Task #4 tests): 9 tests. `mkClaim(over)` helper wraps makeClaim with defaults (source_store pi, span whole, scope_hint profile). `mkManifest(decisions, quarantined=[])` returns `{decisions, quarantined} as unknown as ReconciliationManifest`. Mapper tests: obsidian project→origin pi/provenance obsidian/capture dream/confidence consolidated/scope project:lue-kube/rootKind project/relPath harness/pi; episodic codex→episodic/ + source_store codex-memories; secret→sensitivity secret; permalink deterministic = slug+claim_id[:8]; title from first heading. Planner tests: novel→1 active; merge→1 record + merged_from=[member] + member no record; supersede→old status superseded + superseded_by [newPermalink] + new active; quarantined excluded + silent drop→unaccounted + complete false. 14 pass (incl 5 serialize). tsc exit 0.
   - **`src/migration/apply/plan.ts`** (verified): `planApply(claims, manifest, opts={})` → `{records, stats, unaccounted, over_disposed, complete}`. Pass 1 dispositions (novel→bear; merge→bear canonical with `record.frontmatter={...record.frontmatter, merged_from:others}`, collapse others). Pass 2 supersede edges (`newPermalink = records.get(d.new_id)?.permalink ?? claimToCanonical(need(d.new_id),opts).permalink`; set `{...frontmatter, status:"superseded", superseded_by:[newPermalink]}`). Accounting: eligible = all\quarantined; unaccounted = eligible\(records∪collapsed); over_disposed via recordBearerCount>1 or (records∧collapsed). stats: total_records, active=total-superseded, superseded, merged_records, collapsed_members, quarantined, by_namespace (from relPath dir).
   - **`src/migration/apply/map-claim.ts`** (verified): `claimToCanonical(claim, opts={})` → CanonicalRecord {claim_id, permalink, rootKind, projectSlug?, relPath, frontmatter, body}. ORIGIN_BY_STORE (obsidian→pi), PROVENANCE_STORE_BY_STORE (obsidian→obsidian, codex→codex-memories), CAPTURE_BY_STORE (obsidian→dream, rest native), confidenceFor (obsidian→consolidated else extracted). body = `parseFrontmatter(claim.text).body.trim() || claim.text.trim()`. permalink = `${slugify(title)}-${claim.claim_id.slice(0,8)}`. sensitivity = redact hitCount>0?secret:private. dir = scope_hint episodic?episodic:`harness/${origin}`. rootKind = scope.startsWith("project:")?project:global.

# Pi fork package publishing strategy — upstream-by-default

Publish and control `@valkyriweb/pi-*` support packages only while they carry real fork delta required by `pi-coding-agent`. If a package has zero fork delta or its delta has been upstreamed or retired, depend on upstream `@earendil-works/*` again. Avoid self-maintaining packages that upstream already maintains.

**Why:** On 2026-05-30, Luke asked why `pi-ai`, `pi-tui`, and `pi-agent-core` were being versioned/controlled. The policy emerged: these packages should only be in the fork's control while they carry meaningful fork-specific changes. Extra packages create maintenance burden without benefit when upstream is healthy.

**How to apply:**
- Default: depend on `@earendil-works/*` upstream packages.
- Fork and publish as `@valkyriweb/pi-*` only when: (a) the package contains fork delta required by `pi-coding-agent`, or (b) upstream is broken and a patch is needed urgently.
- When fork delta is upstreamed or retired: revert dependency back to `@earendil-works/*` and remove the forked package.
- Keep forked support packages internal/lockstep — not independent products with their own release trains.
- Track which packages carry fork delta in `docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.

**Current state (2026-05-30):** Packages renamed to `@valkyriweb/pi-* 0.78.0-luke.0` with GH Packages `publishConfig`. The `@earendil-works/pi-ai` missing package error (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`) was addressed via compatibility shims; long-term fix is clean rebuild once delta scope is clarified.

# Deliberate

## Objective

Run the OODA **Orient → Decide** step: synthesize the current state, identify the real decision, recommend a path, and define exactly what action happens after approval.

This is not the Act step. `deliberate` means: **self-unblock only when the next move is already safe and authorized; otherwise give Luke the relevant information, pros/cons, and recommendation so he can decide.**

## OODA boundary

- **Observe / explore** — gather live evidence: git state, PRs, CI, review output, plans/issues, runtime state, constraints.
- **Orient** — turn evidence into state, target, gap, risk, and blockers.
- **Decide** — present options, pros/cons, recommendation, and the exact next action.
- **Act** — happens only after the plan/decision is completed, reviewed, and approved, or when explicit prior authority already covers the action.

## Workflow

1. **Inventory live state** — check concrete artifacts for the target. Do not rely on memory, stale TODOs, or old plans without verifying them.
2. **Orient the situation**:
   - current state: what is true now;
   - target: what done should look like;
   - gap: what prevents action;
   - constraints: risk, ownership, permissions, timing, cost, taste, business priority.
3. **Classify each item**:
   - `CAN-ACT` — one safe, reversible, clearly correct action exists and is already authorized; do it, verify, and report.
   - `READY-FOR-ACT` — plan/review/approval is complete, but action is external, destructive, public, costly, or merge/deploy shaped; ask or use the explicit approval already given.
   - `DECISION` — multiple valid paths exist and Luke's judgment is needed.
   - `BLOCKED` — missing auth, access, external approval, unavailable service, or unsafe action without consent.
4. **Do not punt fixable work** — if the agent can safely gather missing evidence, fix a local issue, rerun a check, or clarify plan status, do that before asking.
5. **Produce a decision brief** for every remaining `DECISION`/`READY-FOR-ACT` item, ordered by unlock value.

## Action consent

`deliberate` alone is not merge/deploy/destructive consent.

Act only when one of these is true:

- the action is safe, reversible, local, and clearly correct;
- Luke explicitly approved the action in this turn;
- an existing plan/issue/PR says the action is approved, and live gates still match that plan.

For merges, deploys, releases, destructive changes, spend, public replies, or ownership-sensitive calls, treat the result as `READY-FOR-ACT` unless explicit consent is present.

## Decision brief format

Keep it short enough that Luke can answer from a phone:

```markdown
## Decision needed: <one-line question>

State: <what is true now, with artifact links/paths>
Target: <desired end state>
Gap/blocker: <why action should not proceed without a decision>
Plan status: <drafted / reviewed / approved / stale / missing>
Options:
1. <option>
   - Pros: <why choose it>
   - Cons: <risk/cost/tradeoff>
2. <option>
   - Pros: <why choose it>
   - Cons: <risk/cost/tradeoff>
Recommendation: <one option, with why>
If approved: <exact action I will take next>
```

Rules:

- Ask one load-bearing decision at a time unless the choices are independent.
- Provide a recommended default; do not end with "thoughts?".
- Include only evidence that changes the decision.
- Use `bearings` when state itself is unclear.
- Use `polish` when the work needs proof/review, `go` when it needs PR/CI prep, and `land` when it is approved for the Act step.

## Final report

Return four buckets:

- `Acted` — safe/authorized actions completed, with checks.
- `Ready for act` — plan/review/approval state and missing consent, if any.
- `Decision needed` — decision brief(s), ordered by unlock value.
- `Blocked` — exact external ask or missing access.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/land

# Land

## Objective

Move approved work from "ready" to landed: run `polish`, babysit checks, merge only with authority, clean docs/notes, and close the session cleanly.

`land` is the OODA **Act** step. Use `deliberate` first when the plan/decision is not approved.

## References

- Post-deploy browser/live smoke check → `references/canary.md`.
- Read-only queue/merge readiness dashboard → `references/landing-report.md`.

## Preconditions

Before acting, confirm:

- scope is clear: changed files, branch/PR, base branch, and owner/repo authority;
- unrelated dirty work is absent or explicitly dispositioned;
- plan/decision is approved, or Luke explicitly asked you to land/merge;
- destructive, public, external, deploy, spend, or data-changing actions have explicit consent.

If approval is missing or the next move is a judgment call, stop and use `deliberate`.

## Workflow

1. **Run `polish` first** — define success criteria, verify artifacts, run selected review lenses (`code-craft`, `autoreview`/`rusty-review`/`codex-review`, `/improve`, optional `/fuse`, adversarial review, `clawpatch`, or domain lenses), track surfaced work, and close local WIP state.
2. **PR/CI babysit** — open/update the PR if needed, push fixes, watch checks, triage failures, and keep looping until green or blocked. Prefer existing repo automation (`/go`, `autofix-pr`, CI links) over hand-rolled polling. Passive waits run in background Bash; fix/triage loops run in a background `Agent(general)`/`autofix-pr`, not foreground `--watch`.
3. **Merge only when authorized** — merge when explicit authority exists and criteria are met. Never merge red, never force-skip required checks, never hide unresolved review threads.
4. **Docs and notes closeout** — after the work lands, revise or delete stale docs/comments/TODOs created or invalidated by the change. Store future work where it belongs: issue, PR follow-up, `plans/`, `docs/`, or project/repo notes — not only chat.
5. **Final work closeout** — run `work-closeout` again after merge: classify remaining dirty files/stashes/branches, preserve WIP with links, clean scratch output where appropriate, and report the final state.

## Success artifact template

Use this in the PR, issue, closeout file, or final reply:

```markdown
## Polish proof
- Success criteria: <pass/fail + proof links>
- Review lenses: <code-craft/autoreview/improve/extra lenses>
- Surfaced work: <durable links or none>

## Landed state
- PR/merge: <link/commit>
- Docs cleaned: <files or n/a>
- Follow-ups: <issue/plan links or none>
- Work closeout: <clean / preserved WIP links>
```

## Stop conditions

Stop and brief Luke when:

- success criteria cannot be measured with available tools;
- CI is red for reasons outside the work or needs credentials/access;
- `polish` finds a ship-blocker that needs scope/priority judgment;
- merge/deploy/release consent is missing;
- future work is real but has nowhere durable to live.

## Final report

Return:

- `Landed` — PR/commit/merge links.
- `Success proof` — criteria + artifacts.
- `Polish proof` — success criteria, artifacts, and review lens results.
- `Docs/follow-ups` — revised docs and durable future-work links.
- `Closeout` — repo cleanliness or preserved WIP.

content.subject: Write canonical frontmatter serializer
content.description: src/canonical/serialize.ts: serializeCanonical(fm: CanonicalFrontmatter, body) -> md string. Hand-rolled (no yaml dep), handles nested provenance object + string arrays + field order, JSON-quoted scalars matching patch-applier serialise() style. Round-trips with parseFrontmatter. + unit test.

content.subject: Build claim→canonical mapper
content.description: src/migration/apply/map-claim.ts: claimToCanonical(claim) -> CanonicalRecord {permalink, rootKind: global|project, projectSlug?, relPath, frontmatter, body}. Maps origin (obsidian→pi, codex→codex, cc→claude-code, pi→pi), provenance.source_store (obsidian→obsidian, codex→codex-memories/chronicle), visibility=private, sensitivity via redact(), scope from scope_hint/project_slug, confidence=extracted, permalink=slug(title)+claim_id[:8], body via parseFrontmatter. Placement: episodic→episodic/, else harness/<origin>/; root global if profile else project. + tests.

content.subject: Build apply planner (decisions→records, disposition+supersede edge)
content.description: src/migration/apply/plan.ts: planApply(claims, manifest) -> ApplyPlan {records, stats}. Disposition-vs-edge: novel→1 record; merge→canonical record with merged_from=other members (members collapsed, no own record); supersede edge→flip superseded claim's record to status:superseded + superseded_by:[new permalink]. Quarantined skipped. No-drops accounting: every eligible claim either has a record or is merged-away. + tests (supersede flips status, merge collapses, accounting).

content.subject: Dry-run apply script + canonical diff report
content.description: scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts: load manifest.json + ledger-claims.jsonl, run planApply, write canonical records to a SCRATCH preview root (DREAM_RECONCILE_OUT/canonical-preview, never ~/.agents/memory), emit APPLY-DIFF.md: total records by namespace, all 16 merged records (full), all 29 superseded (what drops from recall), sample novel, no-drops proof. This is Luke's binding-gate artifact.

1	# ADR 0009: Memory reconciliation contract (shared ingestion + migration, supersede-not-delete)
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-23). Refines ADR 0007 Decisions 5 + 8.
4	**Related:** ADR 0007 (D5 dedup-is-candidate-not-authority, D8 explicit edges), ADR 0008 (cache regions), `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md` (P2/P3), `docs/specs/p2-claim-ledger-design.md`, `extensions/dream-memory/src/canonical/` (frontmatter, backlinks), `services/qmd-vector-sidecar/src/embed.ts`, `extensions/dream-memory/src/lib/pi-model.ts`
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	P2 (#382) must detect and resolve duplicate/conflicting claims when consolidating ~2,500 migrated claims into the canonical store. A read-only survey of the real corpus (2026-06-23) found **zero exact cross-store duplicates** across 2,507 claims — so dedup here is inherently *semantic*, not hash-based. It also found the conflict surface is small: ~7 genuine near-duplicate title groups, plus ~1,050 codex episodic *boilerplate* fragments (three repeating template section types) and one 446 KB single-section blob.
9	
10	The decisive observation (Luke, 2026-06-22): the detect-and-resolve logic the one-off migration needs is the **same** logic the ongoing ingestion path needs — every time the dream consolidation pass promotes a captured `inbox/` event into a canonical record, it must ask "is this already known? does it contradict something?" Today the dream merger does this only *implicitly* (it re-reads the memory tree each batch and trusts the LLM to consolidate). Building a migration-only reconciler would be a throwaway and would re-create, in miniature, the per-store-consolidator drift anti-pattern ADR 0007 rejects.
11	
12	ADR 0007 already fixed the guardrails: embedding similarity is a *candidate signal, never a deletion authority* (D5), and conflicts are carried by *explicit `supersedes` edges*, not similarity (D8). This ADR specifies the concrete reconciliation contract that satisfies them and is shared by both callers.
13	
14	## Decision
15	
16	1. **One reconciliation core, two callers — scoped to the canonical *writer*, not the recall tail.** Define a single operation `reconcile(candidate, corpusIndex) → Decision`, where `Decision ∈ { novel | merge(into, sources[]) | supersede(target) }` with a rationale. Migration (P2b) calls `reconcileBulk(claims)` over the ledger; dream consolidation (later phase) calls `reconcileOne(candidate, index)` per inbox-promoted claim. Same embedder, same judge, same schema. **Scope:** this is the *consolidation writer* path (ADR 0007 D2's single canonical writer) — both callers are batch and human-gated. It is **not** the per-turn recall tail, which stays exact/manifest-based per ADR 0007 D5 (embeddings must never touch cached-core bytes).
17	
18	2. **Embedding clusters; entailment decides (satisfies ADR 0007 D5).** Embedding similarity *generates candidate clusters only*. The merge/supersede authority is one of: (a) exact normalised-text hash, (b) an explicit edge (`supersedes`/`links`), or (c) an LLM entailment judge — **never cosine distance alone**. A candidate carrying correction/negation/date/number/scope/repo/tool language defaults to keep-both-or-supersede, never silent drop.
19	
20	3. **Reuse the stack's embedder + judge; no new dependency, no API cost (ADR 0007 D3).** Embeddings come from the already-running local MLX embedder via `embedBatch()` (`services/qmd-vector-sidecar/src/embed.ts`); the judge is `callPiModel()` (`src/lib/pi-model.ts`) over claude-bridge — the same path the dream merger and active recall use. Cosine similarity is ~5 lines in-process. Nothing external (mem0/Letta) is adopted as runtime.
21	
22	4. **Two non-destructive verbs — merge (parallel) and supersede (temporal). Automated paths never hard-delete.**
23	   - **Merge** — parallel captures of one fact (migration's cross-store case; ingestion exact-dup): collapse into one canonical record, recording every source `claim_id` in `provenance`.
24	   - **Supersede** — a new claim corrects/contradicts an existing one (ingestion's temporal case): the old record flips to `status: superseded` and gains a `superseded_by` edge; the new record is active.
25	   - **Hard-delete is reserved for explicit human action.** No automated path destroys a record.
26	
27	5. **Superseded ≠ surfaced.** A `superseded` record stays on disk (audit trail, reversibility, provenance) but is **excluded from active recall** (recall filters `status: active`) and from candidate generation. The hot path carries only current truth, so keeping history costs no recall noise. Compaction/GC of superseded records is a separate, later, explicitly human-triggered policy — never part of `reconcile`.
28	
29	6. **Propose, then gate.** The judge only *proposes*. For migration, the full reconciled ledger (merges + supersedes + scope assignments) is presented for Luke's sign-off before any apply (P2 decision). For ingestion, `reconcileOne` slots into the existing human-gated dream consolidation — it adds no always-on automation. (ADR 0007: human-gated dreaming is a kept advantage.)
30	
31	7. **Filter scaffolding before reconcile.** Codex episodic boilerplate (the three repeating template section types, ~1,050 fragments) and oversized claims (e.g. the 446 KB blob) are quarantined *before* embedding/judging: they are scaffolding, not facts, and would waste judge calls and pollute clusters. They remain in the ledger as explicit quarantine, never dropped.
32	
33	## Alternatives Considered
34	
35	| Alternative | Rejected because |
36	|---|---|
37	| mem0-style in-place `ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NOOP` | Hard-delete is unrecoverable under a fallible LLM judge, discards provenance, and violates ADR 0007 D5 ("never a deletion authority"). |
38	| Migration-only reconciler (throwaway) | Ingestion needs the identical detect-resolve; two implementations drift — the per-store-consolidator anti-pattern ADR 0007 rejects, in miniature. |
39	| Keep superseded records in the active index | Pollutes recall with stale truth; current-truth recall is the entire point of supersede. |
40	| Embedding cosine as the merge/supersede authority | ADR 0007 D5: corrections, negations, dates, numbers, and scope changes sit *embedding-near* the fact they replace; similarity cannot carry `supersedes`. |
41	| Add an external embedding/memory dependency | The local MLX `embedBatch` already runs (ADR 0007 D3 build-on-own-stack); a new dep adds cost and a singleton-dep footgun for zero gain. |
42	| Share the reconciler with the per-turn recall path too | Recall-time suppression must stay exact/manifest-based to protect cached-core bytes (ADR 0007 D5/ADR 0008); only the *writer* path may use embedding+judge. |
43	
44	## Consequences
45	
46	- New module `extensions/dream-memory/src/reconcile/` (not under `migration/`, because it is not migration-specific): an `Embedder` seam over `embedBatch`, a `judge()` over `callPiModel`, `reconcileBulk`/`reconcileOne`, and Zod `Decision`/`MergeProposal` schemas. P2b (#382) builds it and wires the migration caller; a later spec phase wires the dream-consolidation caller.
47	- Canonical frontmatter (`canonical/frontmatter.ts`) gains additive fields: `status: active | superseded` (default `active`), `superseded_by`, and `provenance: claim_id[]`.
48	- Active recall routing (`active-memory/recall-routing.ts`) filters `status: active`.
49	- This **refines ADR 0007 D5/D8**: it specifies *how* the consolidation writer dedups (embedding-cluster → exact/edge/entailment authority → merge/supersede), while leaving the per-turn recall tail exact-only.
50	- **Disposition vs edge (no-drops, clean partition).** Every claim gets exactly one *disposition* — a `novel` or a `merge` — recording where its record lands. `supersede` is an *edge* layered on top: the superseding claim is disposed by its own novel/merge, and each superseded claim (plus its exact duplicates) is disposed by a `supersede`. The migration manifest proves this at the claim level: `accountReconciliation` fails the run (`complete: false`) if any eligible claim has zero dispositions (`unaccounted` — a silent drop) or more than one (`over_disposed` — an apply ambiguity). Quarantined claims carry no disposition.
51	- Migration apply remains gated on Luke's full-ledger sign-off (P2 decision). No automated delete exists anywhere in the contract.

# ADR 0009: Memory reconciliation contract (shared ingestion + migration, supersede-not-delete)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-23). Refines ADR 0007 Decisions 5 + 8.
**Related:** ADR 0007 (D5 dedup-is-candidate-not-authority, D8 explicit edges), ADR 0008 (cache regions), `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md` (P2/P3), `docs/specs/p2-claim-ledger-design.md`, `extensions/dream-memory/src/canonical/` (frontmatter, backlinks), `services/qmd-vector-sidecar/src/embed.ts`, `extensions/dream-memory/src/lib/pi-model.ts`

## Context

P2 (#382) must detect and resolve duplicate/conflicting claims when consolidating ~2,500 migrated claims into the canonical store. A read-only survey of the real corpus (2026-06-23) found **zero exact cross-store duplicates** across 2,507 claims — so dedup here is inherently *semantic*, not hash-based. It also found the conflict surface is small: ~7 genuine near-duplicate title groups, plus ~1,050 codex episodic *boilerplate* fragments (three repeating template section types) and one 446 KB single-section blob.

The decisive observation (Luke, 2026-06-22): the detect-and-resolve logic the one-off migration needs is the **same** logic the ongoing ingestion path needs — every time the dream consolidation pass promotes a captured `inbox/` event into a canonical record, it must ask "is this already known? does it contradict something?" Today the dream merger does this only *implicitly* (it re-reads the memory tree each batch and trusts the LLM to consolidate). Building a migration-only reconciler would be a throwaway and would re-create, in miniature, the per-store-consolidator drift anti-pattern ADR 0007 rejects.

ADR 0007 already fixed the guardrails: embedding similarity is a *candidate signal, never a deletion authority* (D5), and conflicts are carried by *explicit `supersedes` edges*, not similarity (D8). This ADR specifies the concrete reconciliation contract that satisfies them and is shared by both callers.

## Decision

1. **One reconciliation core, two callers — scoped to the canonical *writer*, not the recall tail.** Define a single operation `reconcile(candidate, corpusIndex) → Decision`, where `Decision ∈ { novel | merge(into, sources[]) | supersede(target) }` with a rationale. Migration (P2b) calls `reconcileBulk(claims)` over the ledger; dream consolidation (later phase) calls `reconcileOne(candidate, index)` per inbox-promoted claim. Same embedder, same judge, same schema. **Scope:** this is the *consolidation writer* path (ADR 0007 D2's single canonical writer) — both callers are batch and human-gated. It is **not** the per-turn recall tail, which stays exact/manifest-based per ADR 0007 D5 (embeddings must never touch cached-core bytes).

2. **Embedding clusters; entailment decides (satisfies ADR 0007 D5).** Embedding similarity *generates candidate clusters only*. The merge/supersede authority is one of: (a) exact normalised-text hash, (b) an explicit edge (`supersedes`/`links`), or (c) an LLM entailment judge — **never cosine distance alone**. A candidate carrying correction/negation/date/number/scope/repo/tool language defaults to keep-both-or-supersede, never silent drop.

3. **Reuse the stack's embedder + judge; no new dependency, no API cost (ADR 0007 D3).** Embeddings come from the already-running local MLX embedder via `embedBatch()` (`services/qmd-vector-sidecar/src/embed.ts`); the judge is `callPiModel()` (`src/lib/pi-model.ts`) over claude-bridge — the same path the dream merger and active recall use. Cosine similarity is ~5 lines in-process. Nothing external (mem0/Letta) is adopted as runtime.

4. **Two non-destructive verbs — merge (parallel) and supersede (temporal). Automated paths never hard-delete.**
   - **Merge** — parallel captures of one fact (migration's cross-store case; ingestion exact-dup): collapse into one canonical record, recording every source `claim_id` in `provenance`.
   - **Supersede** — a new claim corrects/contradicts an existing one (ingestion's temporal case): the old record flips to `status: superseded` and gains a `superseded_by` edge; the new record is active.
   - **Hard-delete is reserved for explicit human action.** No automated path destroys a record.

5. **Superseded ≠ surfaced.** A `superseded` record stays on disk (audit trail, reversibility, provenance) but is **excluded from active recall** (recall filters `status: active`) and from candidate generation. The hot path carries only current truth, so keeping history costs no recall noise. Compaction/GC of superseded records is a separate, later, explicitly human-triggered policy — never part of `reconcile`.

6. **Propose, then gate.** The judge only *proposes*. For migration, the full reconciled ledger (merges + supersedes + scope assignments) is presented for Luke's sign-off before any apply (P2 decision). For ingestion, `reconcileOne` slots into the existing human-gated dream consolidation — it adds no always-on automation. (ADR 0007: human-gated dreaming is a kept advantage.)

7. **Filter scaffolding before reconcile.** Codex episodic boilerplate (the three repeating template section types, ~1,050 fragments) and oversized claims (e.g. the 446 KB blob) are quarantined *before* embedding/judging: they are scaffolding, not facts, and would waste judge calls and pollute clusters. They remain in the ledger as explicit quarantine, never dropped.

## Alternatives Considered

| Alternative | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| mem0-style in-place `ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NOOP` | Hard-delete is unrecoverable under a fallible LLM judge, discards provenance, and violates ADR 0007 D5 ("never a deletion authority"). |
| Migration-only reconciler (throwaway) | Ingestion needs the identical detect-resolve; two implementations drift — the per-store-consolidator anti-pattern ADR 0007 rejects, in miniature. |
| Keep superseded records in the active index | Pollutes recall with stale truth; current-truth recall is the entire point of supersede. |
| Embedding cosine as the merge/supersede authority | ADR 0007 D5: corrections, negations, dates, numbers, and scope changes sit *embedding-near* the fact they replace; similarity cannot carry `supersedes`. |
| Add an external embedding/memory dependency | The local MLX `embedBatch` already runs (ADR 0007 D3 build-on-own-stack); a new dep adds cost and a singleton-dep footgun for zero gain. |
| Share the reconciler with the per-turn recall path too | Recall-time suppression must stay exact/manifest-based to protect cached-core bytes (ADR 0007 D5/ADR 0008); only the *writer* path may use embedding+judge. |

## Consequences

- New module `extensions/dream-memory/src/reconcile/` (not under `migration/`, because it is not migration-specific): an `Embedder` seam over `embedBatch`, a `judge()` over `callPiModel`, `reconcileBulk`/`reconcileOne`, and Zod `Decision`/`MergeProposal` schemas. P2b (#382) builds it and wires the migration caller; a later spec phase wires the dream-consolidation caller.
- Canonical frontmatter (`canonical/frontmatter.ts`) gains additive fields: `status: active | superseded` (default `active`), `superseded_by`, and `provenance: claim_id[]`.
- Active recall routing (`active-memory/recall-routing.ts`) filters `status: active`.
- This **refines ADR 0007 D5/D8**: it specifies *how* the consolidation writer dedups (embedding-cluster → exact/edge/entailment authority → merge/supersede), while leaving the per-turn recall tail exact-only.
- **Disposition vs edge (no-drops, clean partition).** Every claim gets exactly one *disposition* — a `novel` or a `merge` — recording where its record lands. `supersede` is an *edge* layered on top: the superseding claim is disposed by its own novel/merge, and each superseded claim (plus its exact duplicates) is disposed by a `supersede`. The migration manifest proves this at the claim level: `accountReconciliation` fails the run (`complete: false`) if any eligible claim has zero dispositions (`unaccounted` — a silent drop) or more than one (`over_disposed` — an apply ambiguity). Quarantined claims carry no disposition.
- Migration apply remains gated on Luke's full-ledger sign-off (P2 decision). No automated delete exists anywhere in the contract.

content.subject: Add status/superseded_by/merged_from to canonical frontmatter
content.description: Additive fields to CanonicalFrontmatterSchema (src/canonical/frontmatter.ts): StatusSchema (active|superseded, default active), status, superseded_by: string[], merged_from: string[] (claim_ids collapsed by a merge). Per ADR 0009 consequences. + unit test.

content.subject: Write canonical frontmatter serializer
content.description: src/canonical/serialize.ts: serializeCanonical(fm: CanonicalFrontmatter, body) -> md string. Hand-rolled (no yaml dep), handles nested provenance object + string arrays + field order, JSON-quoted scalars matching patch-applier serialise() style. Round-trips with parseFrontmatter. + unit test.

content.subject: Build claim→canonical mapper
content.description: src/migration/apply/map-claim.ts: claimToCanonical(claim) -> CanonicalRecord {permalink, rootKind: global|project, projectSlug?, relPath, frontmatter, body}. Maps origin (obsidian→pi, codex→codex, cc→claude-code, pi→pi), provenance.source_store (obsidian→obsidian, codex→codex-memories/chronicle), visibility=private, sensitivity via redact(), scope from scope_hint/project_slug, confidence=extracted, permalink=slug(title)+claim_id[:8], body via parseFrontmatter. Placement: episodic→episodic/, else harness/<origin>/; root global if profile else project. + tests.

content.subject: Build apply planner (decisions→records, disposition+supersede edge)
content.description: src/migration/apply/plan.ts: planApply(claims, manifest) -> ApplyPlan {records, stats}. Disposition-vs-edge: novel→1 record; merge→canonical record with merged_from=other members (members collapsed, no own record); supersede edge→flip superseded claim's record to status:superseded + superseded_by:[new permalink]. Quarantined skipped. No-drops accounting: every eligible claim either has a record or is merged-away. + tests (supersede flips status, merge collapses, accounting).

content.subject: Dry-run apply script + canonical diff report
content.description: scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts: load manifest.json + ledger-claims.jsonl, run planApply, write canonical records to a SCRATCH preview root (DREAM_RECONCILE_OUT/canonical-preview, never ~/.agents/memory), emit APPLY-DIFF.md: total records by namespace, all 16 merged records (full), all 29 superseded (what drops from recall), sample novel, no-drops proof. This is Luke's binding-gate artifact.

content.description: pi + obsidian extractors: detect pure table-of-contents index files (basename MEMORY.md, or "# X Memory" heading followed only by [title](file.md) link bullets) and skip them with reason "toc_index". Removes ~5 low-harm index-bullet→doc supersedes (S3/S4/S5/S7/S9). Requires a reconcile re-run to regenerate the manifest. Fold in only if time allows; otherwise annotate those 5 in the diff.

5. **Superseded = down-weighted, not filtered (amended 2026-06-23 — see Amendment 1).** A `superseded` record stays on disk and stays **reachable by recall**, but ranks low. Two read surfaces, two rules:
   - **Always-loaded index** (Tier 1, `MEMORY.md`): renders **active records only**, scope-gated — current truth in the cached-core budget, nothing stale. This is a *render* budget choice, not a reachability gate.

A superseded record is reachable at low weight (`statusWeight ≈ 0.3` vs active `1.0`), so a query that *only* matches the old truth can still surface it; a query that matches both surfaces the current one first. The existing freshness caveat (`<system-reminder>` appended for records older than ~1 day, `recall-selection.ts`) makes surfacing a superseded record safe — the model is told it may be stale.
   - **ACL is the only hard gate.** `sensitivity`/`visibility` exclusions run *before* scoring (a security/privacy invariant, not a relevance call); `status`/`confidence`/`age` only *weight*, never exclude. Rationale (Luke, 2026-06-22): a hard `status:active` filter makes a record unreachable — "how would recall know about other artifacts if they're not visible?" — destroying the audit-trail/reversibility value of keeping it on disk. Temporal decay already solves "old truth ranks below new truth" without hiding anything.

   Compaction/GC of superseded records is a separate, later, explicitly human-triggered policy — never part of `reconcile`.

## Amendment 1 (2026-06-23): decay-weight supersession + scope-gated render

The original Decision 5 said a superseded record is "excluded from active recall (recall filters `status: active`)." Luke rejected the hard filter: *"how would recall know about other artifacts if they are not visible? this should rather be like temporal decay where it is weighted less if it's older / stale."* He approved three changes (verbatim sign-off, 2026-06-22):

1. **Decay-weight, not hard-filter.** Extend the decay weight to factor `status` + `confidence`; superseded records stay reachable, ranked low. (See the revised Decision 5 score formula.)
2. **Scope-gated render.** The `MEMORY.md` index is re-revised by dreaming, but **dormant projects are never re-revised** — gate the index/snapshot epoch bump on the per-scope consolidation watermark (token-waste avoidance).
3. **ACL stays the only hard gate.** `sensitivity`/`visibility` are a security/privacy invariant and exclude before scoring; `status`/`confidence`/`age` only weight.

### Why hard-filter is wrong, in one line

A hard `status:active` filter and on-disk retention are contradictory: you pay to keep the record (audit, reversibility, "what did we believe before?") and then make it unreachable. Decay-weighting gets the only property the filter was protecting — *current truth ranks above stale* — without the unreachability.

### External evidence (read-path comparison)

- **mem0** — decay down-ranks, never deletes (recency ×1.5 / idle ×0.3, ~5× spread); decay layered on top of supersession. Matches the approved direction.
- **Zep / Graphiti** — temporal knowledge graph with fact-validity windows; superseded facts retained with `valid_to` and excluded from the *current* view but queryable historically (+15 pts over mem0 on their bench). Same "retain + temporally rank, don't delete" shape.
- **Claude Code 2.1.186 (binary inspected via `binlens` over the native Mach-O, 2026-06-23)** — the cautionary anti-pattern, and it has shipped *more* memory automation than its docs admit:
  - **Auto-dream consolidation exists** and is **watermark-gated** exactly like our design — `autoDreamEnabled` setting, `listSessionsTouchedSince` + `minSessions`/`minHours` since `lastConsolidatedAt`, `tengu_auto_dream_skipped`/`_fired`/`_completed`. This is strong external precedent for Amendment point 2 (skip dormant scopes).
  - **No recall-time decay or status weighting.** There is no memory decay curve (`useDecayCurve` in the binary is terminal scroll-wheel acceleration, not memory). The memory index is injected wholesale as a `<memory>` block (`memory_load_prompt` / `# auto memory`) and **truncated by byte budget** ("will be truncated, so keep the index concise") — no relevance/recency ranking. Everything loaded is treated as equally authoritative until truncation drops the tail.
  - **Dedupe is destructive + non-algorithmic.** It's instruction-driven ("Do not write duplicate memories. First check if there is an existing memory you can update… Update or remove memories that turn out to be wrong or outdated") plus an LLM auto-dream agent granted `rm *.md` permission inside the memory dir ("Return a brief summary of what you consolidated, updated, or **pruned**"), and the multi-store sync **hard-deletes** "superseded" files (`filesDeleted`, "failed to remove superseded"). **Superseded = deleted**, not flagged — the exact lossy behavior this ADR rejects.

Both done. Here's the answer to your question and the ADR update.

## Does Claude Code's auto-dream do decay / filtering / dedupe?

Inspected the real binary (`binlens` over `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.186`, 216MB native Mach-O). CC ships **more memory automation than its docs admit** — and it's the cautionary case for our design:

| Behavior | CC 2.1.186 | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto-dream consolidation** | ✅ **YES** | Background forked agent, **watermark-gated**: `listSessionsTouchedSince` + `minSessions`/`minHours` since `lastConsolidatedAt` → `tengu_auto_dream_skipped`/`_fired`/`_completed`. Lock + rollback. Reads recent transcripts. **Same gating shape as my-pi `dream.ts`.** |
| **Recall decay / staleness ranking** | ❌ **NO** | No memory decay. (`useDecayCurve` in the binary is *terminal scroll-wheel* acceleration — false positive, I drilled in to confirm.) Index injected **wholesale** as a `<memory>` block, **truncated by byte budget** — everything equally authoritative until the tail is cut. |
| **Status/visibility filtering at recall** | ❌ **NO** | No `status` filter; read path = inject whole index + truncate. |
| **Dedupe** | ⚠️ **YES, but destructive + non-algorithmic** | Instruction-driven ("Do not write duplicate memories… update or remove outdated") + LLM prune in auto-dream (agent granted `rm *.md` in the memory dir) + multi-store sync **hard-deletes** superseded files (`filesDeleted`, "failed to remove superseded"). **Superseded = deleted, never soft-flagged.** No embedding dedup. |

**Net:** CC *validates* our watermark-gating (skip dormant scopes) and is the *anti-pattern* on staleness (hard-delete + always-load-truncate, no decay). Exactly what you rejected. Our retain-and-decay-weight contract is the deliberate improvement.

## ADR 0009 amended (before code, as approved)

`docs/adr/0009-memory-reconciliation-contract.md` in the worktree — **Amendment 1 (2026-06-23)**:
- **Decision 5 rewritten:** supersede recall is now **decay-weight, not hard-filter**. Two surfaces: always-loaded index renders active-only + scope-gated; per-turn recall scores *everything except ACL-blocked* by `semantic × decay(age,last_used) × statusWeight(active 1.0 / superseded ≈0.3) × confidenceWeight`. Superseded stays reachable, ranks low; freshness caveat keeps it safe.
- **ACL (`sensitivity`/`visibility`) = sole hard gate**, runs before scoring. `status`/`confidence`/`age` only weight.
- **Scope-gated render:** index/snapshot epoch bumps only when a scope's consolidation watermark advances → dormant projects never re-revised.
- Alternatives table + Consequences updated; CC/mem0/Zep evidence folded into the amendment as the external reference.

Saved the CC finding to memory (`cc-auto-memory-binary-truth`) — it contradicts CC's docs and is load-bearing for the unification program.

content.text:
Short version: **the finding closes the design question — it doesn't open new work, it confirms the plan and validates it externally.** What's left is execution, plus one new strategic call the finding forces.

## What the CC finding settled

- **Decay-weight (Amendment 1) is right** — CC's hard-delete-superseded + always-load-truncate is the lossy path you rejected; we now have a named anti-pattern to point at.
- **Watermark-gated consolidation (Amendment 2) is right** — CC independently arrived at `minSessions`/`minHours`-since-last-consolidation. Convergent design = low risk.
- **Tier-2 semantic recall + scoring is a real differentiator** — CC has *no* retrieval scoring at all. Nothing to reconsider there.

No design rework. The ADR is the spec.

## The one new thing it forces

CC isn't a blank slate we inject into — it has its **own** auto-memory + auto-dream that will **hard-delete and truncate**. When P6/P7 points CC at the unified `~/.agents/memory`, CC's native auto-dream would actively destroy our retain-and-decay contract (it deletes superseded files). So we need to decide: **suppress CC's native auto-memory** (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` / `autoDreamEnabled:false`) and own the read/consolidate path ourselves, vs. ride it. Recommend suppress — riding it defeats the whole ADR. Not blocking now (it's a P6/P7 concern), but worth logging as an ADR follow-up.

## Execution queue

1. **Commit P2c** (mapper/planner/serializer/tests/dryrun + ADR amendment) → PR. Done, diff-approved, gate-green, reversible.
2. **Build the decay-weight read-path** — extend `decayWeight` in `decay.ts` (status+confidence) + scope-gated index render. This is Amendment 1/2 in code (P4/P5).
3. **Run the migration apply** into the real store — 1449 records + rollback snapshot + qmd rebuild. Irreversible-ish; needs your explicit "go apply."

Natural order is 1 → 2 → 3 (apply last, so records land into a read-path that honors the weighting). Everything's on your no-commit-until-greenlight hold, so:

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/go

# /go

Announce at start: **"Using /go. Orchestrating verify → code-review polish → review gate → PR → CI-watch as clean-context subagents."**

You are the **orchestrator**. Phases run as sequential subagents except the review gate, which may fan out into parallel reviewers for non-trivial changes. File-based handoffs live in `./.go-output/`. The arc mirrors a manual ship cycle — clean up the diff, verify it works (surfacing regressions the request didn't ask about), get an independent review, open the PR, then watch CI and fix failures as they land — so the human can hand off the whole loop, not just the build.

`/go` prepares work for PR/CI; it does not merge. Use `land` when the ask is to babysit through merge and close out the session. For read-only merge readiness across a queue after PR prep, use `../land/references/landing-report.md`.

## References

| Phase | Handoff template |
|---|---|
| 1 Verify | `references/phase-1-verify.md` |
| 2 Code Review | `references/phase-2-code-review.md` |
| 3 Review gate | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md`; non-trivial fan-out also uses `references/phase-3-security.md` and `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md`; UI changes also use `references/phase-3-design.md` |
| 4 PR | `references/phase-4-pr.md` |
| 5 CI watch | `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` |

Each handoff is self-contained: the subagent gets the file's contents (with `{{CWD}}` interpolated), reads the artifacts from prior phases, and returns a single-line STATUS.

## File workspace

```
.go-output/
  context.md      # Phase 0 writes — scope, classification, commands
  verify.md       # Phase 1 writes
  slop-scan.md    # Phase 1 writes when slop-scan is available (advisory)
  verify-*.png    # Phase 1 writes (screenshots)
  code-review.md  # Phase 2 writes
  code-craft.md   # Phase 3 writes (## Fixed + ## Follow-ups)
  security.md     # Phase 3 fan-out writes when security review runs
  test-review.md  # Phase 3 fan-out writes when test review runs
  design.md       # Phase 3 fan-out writes when the diff touched UI
  review-gate.md  # Phase 3 synthesis writes
  pr.md           # Phase 4 writes (PR URL + commits)
  ci-watch.md     # Phase 5 writes (CI result + any autofix commits)
```

Create the directory in Phase 0 and add `.go-output/` to `.gitignore` if absent — these are ephemeral.

## Phase 0 — Orchestrator setup

1. Capture scope:
   ```bash
   git status --porcelain
   git diff --stat
   # If tree is clean and commits exist on a branch:
   base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD main)
   git log --oneline "$base"..HEAD
   git diff --stat "$base"..HEAD
   ```
2. **Detect unrelated changes.** Compare the modified files against the user's stated work. Any file that doesn't fit the intent (for example a debug script when the user is shipping CSV export) is unrelated. If unrelated changes exist, halt before writing `context.md` and surface three options to the user: commit them on the current branch, stash them, or move them to a separate branch. Do not dispatch phases until resolved. Phases must never silently sweep unrelated work into the PR.
3. Classify the change as one or more of: `backend-cli`, `web-ui`, `desktop-native`, `refactor`.
   - **Determine `UI-touched`** — the single relevance gate for the Core Web Vitals trace (Phase 1) and the design review (Phase 3). Set `yes` only if the diff changes a rendered UI surface: components/templates/markup (`.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.svelte/.astro/.html/.blade.php`), styles (`.css/.scss/.less`, Tailwind classes), or design tokens. Pure logic, API, config, test, build, or docs changes are `no` — even when the app has a UI. When `no`, Phase 1 skips the CWV trace and Phase 3 skips the design reviewer; never spin up browser/perf tooling for a change that can't move a pixel.
4. Derive project commands from `AGENTS.md` / `README` / `package.json` scripts / nearest config:
   - `TEST_CMD`, `LINT_CMD` (or `none`), `TYPECHECK_CMD` (or `none`), dev-server command if web-ui or backend-cli.
   - `SLOP_SCAN_CMD`: use `npm run review:slop` when present, otherwise `npx slop-scan scan . --lint` for JS/TS repos with `slop-scan` available, otherwise `none`.
5. Scan the user's prompt for context the phases should preserve: flaky-test warnings, known-broken tests on main, infra caveats, reviewer preferences. These go in the `Notes` field of `context.md`.
6. `mkdir -p .go-output` and write `.go-output/context.md`:

   ```markdown
   # /go context
   - Branch: <branch>
   - Base: <base-sha>
   - Classification: <kinds>
   - UI-touched: <yes|no>   # gates CWV trace (Phase 1) + design review (Phase 3)
   - Changed files:
     <list>
   - Test cmd: <cmd>
   - Lint cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Typecheck cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Slop-scan cmd: <cmd-or-none>  # advisory heuristic, not a standalone blocker
   - Dev-server cmd: <cmd-or-na>
   - Summary: <one-line intent suitable for branch slug + PR title>
   - Notes: <anything unusual>
   ```

7. Print: `/go context written: <N> files, classified <kinds>, dispatching verify subagent.`

## Phases 1–4 — Dispatch

For phases 1, 2, 4, and 5, dispatch a subagent with:
- **Prompt** = contents of that phase's reference file with `{{CWD}}` replaced by the absolute working directory.
- **Clean context** — do not carry parent conversation into the subagent.
- **Synchronous** — wait for the subagent to return before dispatching the next phase.

Harness mapping:
- **Claude Code** — `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"`.
- **Pi** — Pi's agent SDK with a fresh context.
- **Codex** — `SendMessage` to a spawned subagent, or Codex's native spawn mechanism.

After each return, read the phase's artifact file and the STATUS line. Apply the early-stop rules below.

### Phase 3 — Review gate with optional fan-out

Before Phase 3, classify whether this is **trivial**. Skip fan-out only if all are true:

- touches 2 files or fewer;
- diff is under 50 changed lines;
- does not touch auth, payments, data access, config, secrets, network boundaries, migrations, CI, deployment, or permissioning;
- Phase 1 found no verification gaps.

If trivial, run only `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` as the code-craft reviewer.

If non-trivial, dispatch these clean-context reviewers in parallel from the orchestrator:

| Reviewer | Prompt |
|---|---|
| Code craft | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` |
| Security | `references/phase-3-security.md` |
| Test engineer | `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md` |

#### Design review step (only when `UI-touched: yes`)

This is a first-class step of the review gate, not an optional extra. The rule is simple: **if `context.md` has `UI-touched: yes`, the design review runs; if `no`, it is skipped entirely.** It is gated on *touching UI*, not on diff size — a change small enough to be "trivial" in code terms (the video's like-button case) can still ship a contrast or layout-shift defect.

When `UI-touched: yes`, dispatch `references/phase-3-design.md` in parallel with the code reviewers above (it runs even when the code change is otherwise trivial). It consumes Phase 1's screenshots + Core Web Vitals and composes the `frontend` skill's `web-design-guidelines` and `taste-skill-anti-slop` references. A `DESIGN-NEEDS-WORK` verdict with unresolved blockers makes the gate `NO-GO`.

When `UI-touched: no`, do not dispatch it and do not load any browser/perf tooling — record `Design review: n/a (no UI surface)` in the synthesis.

Then synthesize their artifacts into `./.go-output/review-gate.md` with:

```markdown
## Decision
GO | NO-GO

## Required fixes before PR
<blockers with source artifact + file:line/evidence>

## Follow-ups
<non-blocking follow-ups>

## Rollback plan
<how to back out safely if this ships badly>
```

If any reviewer reports a blocker, stop before Phase 4 unless the fix is in-scope, applied, and the relevant tests are rerun green.

Before Phase 4 or final handoff, persist non-blocking follow-ups outside `.go-output/`: PR body/comment, GitHub issue, plan doc, repo notes, or the project's existing tracker. `.go-output/` is evidence, not the durable tracking surface.

### Phase 5 — Watch CI and autofix

After Phase 4 opens a PR on GitHub, dispatch `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` as an async CI babysitter and drive the PR to green. Passive CI waits use background Bash; failure interpretation and fix loops use background `Agent(general)` composing `autofix-pr`. Never foreground `gh pr checks --watch` from the orchestrator.

Skip Phase 5 only when:

- Phase 4 returned `PUSHED-NO-PR` (no GitHub PR to watch), or
- the repo has no CI checks (`gh pr checks` reports an empty set after the first poll), or
- the user asked for the PR to stay a draft / explicitly opted out of CI babysitting in their prompt (record in `context.md` Notes).

Phase 5 **never merges**. It stops at green and leaves the merge decision to the human. Unrelated/flaky failures are reported, not force-fixed (see the reference for the prefer-merge-main-over-bloat rule).

## Early-stop rules

- Phase 1 `BLOCKED` → stop. Surface `verify.md` to the user. Do not code-review or PR broken code.
- Phase 2 `BROKE-AND-REVERTED` → continue. The revert restored the green state from Phase 1.
- Phase 3 `NO-GO` or unresolved blocker → stop. Surface `review-gate.md` and the contributing reviewer artifacts.
- Phase 3 `REVIEW-FIXED` with failing tests → the subagent should have reverted; if it didn't, stop before Phase 4 and surface.
- Phase 4 `BLOCKED` → surface the reason (common causes: no `gh` auth, branch protection, dirty tree). Leave retry to the human. Do not run Phase 5 without an open PR.
- Phase 4 `PUSHED-NO-PR` → skip Phase 5 (nothing to watch); surface the remote + branch.
- Phase 5 `CI-RED` after its autofix attempts are exhausted → stop. Surface `ci-watch.md` with the remaining failing checks and their log evidence. Never merge a red PR; never `--no-verify` or force-skip a check to make it look green.

## Orchestrator finish

Print:

```
/go complete.
- Verify: <status>
- Code Review: <status>
- Review gate: <status>
- Design review: <status | n/a (no UI surface)>
- PR: <url>
- CI watch: <status> (green | red — <n> checks | skipped — <reason>)
```

Leave `.go-output/` on disk. The user can delete it when the PR merges. Any follow-ups from `.go-output/` must already be copied to a durable tracker before declaring `/go` complete.

## Guardrails

- If tests are already failing on `main` before /go starts, note it in `context.md`; downstream phases will not claim your change caused or fixed them.
- The human is the final gate. Never auto-merge.

Harness tooling per runtime + rationalizations to resist: `references/harness-notes.md` — read when selecting phase tooling or tempted to shortcut the gate.

Skill history: `references/changelog.md` — read when tracing a design decision.

Hold on — that message changes the ADR I'm about to commit, so let me settle it before committing anything. **Pausing `/go` at Phase 0** (nothing written yet).

Your two steers look like they conflict, but I think they're actually about **two different axes**, and that resolves it cleanly:

- **Staleness (age):** an *old but still-valid* record. Your earlier point — "weighted less if older, but recall must still reach it." → **decay-weight, keep reachable.**
- **Supersession (replacement):** a record a *newer, contradicting* claim has explicitly replaced. The new claim already carries the truth. → you're now saying you don't mind **deleting** these.

Those don't conflict — decay is about *age*, supersede is about *replacement*. The only real cost of deleting superseded records is **irreversibility**: supersession is decided by the LLM entailment judge, so a *wrong* supersede call deletes a record you can't get back. CC accepts that risk (it deletes). My ADR currently keeps them flagged-but-reachable precisely as a safety net.

The one place that bites hardest is the **migration**: 2555 claims, judge-decided supersedes, one shot — that's exactly when the judge is least proven and deletion is least recoverable.

P2b of the cross-harness memory unification (ADR 0009 / #382): the shared reconciliation core.

A single `reconcile` operation, called two ways: the one-off migration (`reconcileBulk` over the claim ledger) and ongoing dream consolidation (`reconcileOne` per promoted claim). Both run the same exact-hash check, the same entailment judge, and the same group→decision mapping, so migration and ingestion can never drift apart. Embedding similarity only *generates candidate clusters* (ADR 0007 D5); merge/supersede authority is exact-hash or the LLM judge — never cosine alone.

- `reconcile/` — the source-agnostic core: an injected `Embedder` seam (`createHttpEmbedder` mirrors the sidecar's OpenAI wire shape + `DREAM_EMBED_*` env), scope-blocked union-find `clusterBySimilarity`, an entailment `judge` over `callPiModel` (injectable `completeFn`), and `reconcileBulk`/`reconcileOne` emitting zod `Decision`s.
- Two non-destructive verbs only — `merge` (parallel captures → one canonical, all sources in provenance) and `supersede` (temporal correction; old record retained, dropped from active recall). No automated path deletes.
- `migration/reconcile-step.ts` — the migration caller: quarantines codex boilerplate + oversized blobs before reconcile (ADR 0009 D7), maps claims to the reconcile shape, and assembles a sign-off `ReconciliationManifest` with a claim-level no-drops guarantee (`accountReconciliation`).

Read-only and propose-only: the reconciler emits decisions for human sign-off; nothing writes into or deletes from the canonical store. The sign-off-gated transactional apply (P2c) follows.

Clean-context adversarial code review. Do NOT assume prior context; read the files yourself.

## Working tree
All under `/tmp/p2-reconcile-run/extensions/dream-memory/`. Review these (uncommitted) files:
- `src/canonical/serialize.ts` (NEW — frontmatter serializer)
- `src/canonical/frontmatter.ts` (MODIFIED — additive fields status/superseded_by/merged_from)
- `src/migration/apply/map-claim.ts` (NEW — claim→CanonicalRecord mapper)
- `src/migration/apply/plan.ts` (NEW — apply planner: dispositions + supersede edges + no-drops accounting)
- `scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts` (NEW — dry-run apply driver, renders preview tree + APPLY-DIFF.md)
- `tests/canonical-serialize.spec.ts`, `tests/migration-apply.spec.ts` (NEW — 14 passing tests)

Also read for context: `src/canonical/paths.ts`, and the contract this must satisfy: `/tmp/p2-reconcile-run/docs/adr/0009-memory-reconciliation-contract.md` (esp. the "disposition vs edge" consequence + Decision 4/5 supersede-not-delete-in-migration).

## What this subsystem does
Migration step that turns a reconciled claim ledger into canonical memory records — but writes only to a PREVIEW tree, never the live `~/.agents/memory` store, and only after a hard accounting gate. The whole point is **zero silent data loss**: every eligible claim must land in exactly one record (or be an explicitly-collapsed merge member, or quarantined). The dry-run on the real corpus produced 1449 records from 2555 claims, 0 dropped.

## Your job — be a skeptic. Hunt for:
1. **Silent data loss / accounting holes.** Can a claim be dropped without being counted as `unaccounted`? Can the `complete` gate return true while a record is missing? Is the eligible-set math (eligible = all claims minus quarantined; unaccounted = eligible minus records minus collapsed-members) actually airtight? Off-by-one or set-membership bugs in the disposition-vs-edge partition.
2. **Supersede-edge correctness.** When a claim is superseded, the new (superseding) record must exist and be active; the old gets `status:superseded` + `superseded_by:[newPermalink]`. Does `planApply` correctly resolve the new permalink even when the new claim is itself a merge-canonical? Any case where supersede silently no-ops or points at a wrong/missing permalink?
3. **Permalink collisions.** Permalink = slug(title) + claim_id[:8]. Can two different records collide? Can a collision overwrite a record on disk (preview tree)?
4. **The write guard.** `migrate-apply-dryrun.ts` rm's + rewrites a preview tree. Verify the guard that the target path must contain "canonical-preview" / be under the out dir actually prevents nuking an arbitrary directory if env vars are mis-set. This is the only destructive op — scrutinize it hard.
5. **Determinism.** Same ledger in → byte-identical records out? Any Map iteration order, Date.now(), or unsorted-collection nondeterminism that would make the APPLY-DIFF unstable across runs?
6. **Code craft** (secondary): naming, composability, dead code, anything a senior reviewer would call overcomplicated. Note but don't block on style.

## Output format (return as your final message, nothing else)
```
VERDICT: GO | NEEDS-WORK
BLOCKERS (must fix before PR):
- <file:line> — <issue> — <why it's a real bug, with the input that triggers it>
FOLLOW-UPS (non-blocking):
- <file:line> — <suggestion>
NOTES:
- <anything about test coverage gaps for the above>
```
Be concrete with file:line. If you claim a bug, give the triggering input. Don't invent issues to seem thorough — if it's solid, say GO.

```
VERDICT: NEEDS-WORK

BLOCKERS (must fix before PR):

- scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts:245 — Write guard is bypassable via either (a) a path containing the string "canonical-preview" outside the outDir, or (b) a raw-string path-traversal. The guard is `!previewRoot.includes("canonical-preview") && !previewRoot.startsWith(outDir)`. Neither check uses path.resolve(), so `DREAM_APPLY_PREVIEW=/tmp/canonical-preview` passes the first condition (includes match) and runs `rm -rf /tmp/canonical-preview`. Likewise, `outDir + "/../../evil"` passes the second condition (raw startsWith). Fix: resolve both paths before comparison, and use `resolvedPreview.startsWith(resolvedOut + "/")` (note the trailing slash to prevent prefix-collision, e.g. `/foo-bar` falsely matching `/foo`). The `includes("canonical-preview")` check adds nothing once you have the resolved-startsWith check and should be removed — it's a string-in-string test, not a path containment test.

FOLLOW-UPS (non-blocking):

- src/migration/apply/plan.ts:97 — The `?? claimToCanonical(need(d.new_id), opts).permalink` fallback for `newPermalink` is unreachable in any valid manifest: if `new_id` had no novel/merge disposition, it would be `unaccounted` and `plan.complete` would be false, blocking the write before this fallback's result could matter. The dead code is harmless but misleading — it implies `supersede` edges can have a new_id with no record, which is not the model. Remove the fallback and replace with a runtime assertion (`if (!records.has(d.new_id)) throw new Error(...)`) to surface manifest bugs explicitly rather than silently computing a phantom permalink.

- src/migration/apply/plan.ts (write loop in dryrun, line 253) / scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts:253 — No dedup check on `relPath` before writing. Two records from different `claim_id`s can produce the same `relPath` if they have the same slug prefix and the same `claim_id[:8]` (birthday probability ~0.076% for this corpus). The second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first; `written` is still incremented so the log says N files were written when only N-1 exist. The accounting gate counts `claim_id`s (not file paths), so `plan.complete` stays true. For the current 2555-claim corpus this is extremely unlikely in practice, but the invariant "N records written = N files on disk" is unstated and unverified. Fix: after the write loop, assert `written === (new Set(plan.records.map(r => previewPathFor(r, previewRoot)))).size` — or detect it before writing.

- scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts:114 — The APPLY-DIFF.md accounting identity `total_records + collapsed_members = manifest.eligible_claims` is displayed as a proof but never verified as a gate check. `planApply` computes eligible from the actual ledger; `manifest.eligible_claims` comes from the manifest file. If the manifest was regenerated from a different ledger version than what's on disk (race/operator error), the identity could display as e.g. `1449 + 10 = 1459 = 2555 eligible` which is obviously false. Add a gate check: `if (plan.stats.total_records + plan.stats.collapsed_members !== manifest.eligible_claims)` → mismatches, abort. This closes the one remaining gap between "plan is internally consistent" and "plan matches the manifest's stated scope."

- src/canonical/serialize.ts (general) — `unquote` in `parse.ts` only handles `\"` and `\\` JSON escape sequences. `JSON.stringify` in `serialize.ts` will also emit `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\uXXXX` for titles containing control characters or raw newlines. If a title like `"\tPrefixed"` comes from a malformed source claim, it round-trips as `"\\tPrefixed"`. This is a pre-existing limitation of the hand-rolled YAML subset contract (the serialize.ts comment acknowledges it), but the new `status` and `superseded_by` fields go through the same path and would survive since they contain only safe ASCII. Low real-world risk given titles are prose; note it if the serializer scope ever expands to free-form fields.

NOTES:
- Tests cover the core disposition + supersede paths well (14 cases). The missing cases are: (1) supersede where `new_id` is a merge canonical (covered by the over_disposed guard but not tested directly), (2) a relPath collision between two records (no test), and (3) the write guard itself (would need a test with a mocked `rm` + a malicious env var). The `complete` gate path under each valid topology is tested; the gate-bypass scenarios are not.
```
