## P2 reconcile migration runner + oversize-cluster guard

Part of the cross-harness memory unification (ADR 0009 / #382). P2b (#395) landed the shared reconcile core; this is the **production caller** that wires the real services to it and produces the **sign-off artifact**.

### What's here
- **`scripts/migrate-reconcile.ts`** — loads the live claim ledger across all stores (pi, obsidian, codex, per-project claude-code), embeds via the MLX sidecar (`createHttpEmbedder`), judges over claude-bridge sonnet (`createPiModelJudge`), runs `reconcileLedger`, and writes a propose-only `ReconciliationManifest` + `ledger-claims.jsonl`. A `preview` mode counts/dumps clusters without spending judge calls.
- **`reconcile` core** — new `maxJudgeClusterSize` dep on `reconcileBulk`. Clusters over the cap skip the judge; members fall through to `novel` (kept distinct — **no drop**) and are surfaced via the new `clusters_skipped_oversize` stat. Found running the real corpus: codex episodic session logs form large topically-similar-but-distinct clusters that produce one costly, unreliable judge call.

### Auth note
The judge runs over **claude-bridge** (OAuth), not a direct anthropic key — the `sonnet-class` alias would pick `anthropic/*` (no working key on this machine), so the runner defaults the model override to `claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-4-6` (still honoring `DREAM_RECONCILE_MODEL`). ADR 0009 D3.

### Proven end-to-end on the live corpus
```
2555 claims → 1465 eligible · 1090 quarantined (codex boilerplate sections + 1 oversized)
exact_dup_groups: 0   clusters_judged: 55   clusters_skipped: 3 (oversize, cap=8)
judge_failures: 0
decisions: merge=16  supersede=29  novel=1404
complete: true   unaccounted=0   over_disposed=0
```
~9 min wall (embed + 55 sequential bridge judge calls).

### Scope
Read-only and **propose-only**: the runner emits a manifest for human sign-off; nothing writes into or deletes from any store. The full-ledger sign-off and the sign-off-gated transactional apply (P2c) follow separately.

## P2 reconcile runner + sign-off-gated dry-run apply

Part of the cross-harness memory unification (ADR 0009 / #382). Two commits, one phase:
1. **P2b reconcile runner** — the production caller that produces the sign-off manifest.
2. **P2c dry-run apply** — turns that manifest into canonical records (preview only, gated).

---

## P2b — reconcile migration runner + oversize-cluster guard

P2b (#395) landed the shared reconcile core; this is the **production caller** that wires the real services to it and produces the **sign-off artifact**.

### What's here
- **`scripts/migrate-reconcile.ts`** — loads the live claim ledger across all stores (pi, obsidian, codex, per-project claude-code), embeds via the MLX sidecar (`createHttpEmbedder`), judges over claude-bridge sonnet (`createPiModelJudge`), runs `reconcileLedger`, and writes a propose-only `ReconciliationManifest` + `ledger-claims.jsonl`. A `preview` mode counts/dumps clusters without spending judge calls.
- **`reconcile` core** — new `maxJudgeClusterSize` dep on `reconcileBulk`. Clusters over the cap skip the judge; members fall through to `novel` (kept distinct — **no drop**) and are surfaced via the new `clusters_skipped_oversize` stat. Found running the real corpus: codex episodic session logs form large topically-similar-but-distinct clusters that produce one costly, unreliable judge call.

### Auth note
The judge runs over **claude-bridge** (OAuth), not a direct anthropic key — the `sonnet-class` alias would pick `anthropic/*` (no working key on this machine), so the runner defaults the model override to `claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-4-6` (still honoring `DREAM_RECONCILE_MODEL`). ADR 0009 D3.

### Proven end-to-end on the live corpus
```
2555 claims → 1465 eligible · 1090 quarantined (codex boilerplate sections + 1 oversized)
exact_dup_groups: 0   clusters_judged: 55   clusters_skipped: 3 (oversize, cap=8)
judge_failures: 0
decisions: merge=16  supersede=29  novel=1404
complete: true   unaccounted=0   over_disposed=0
```
~9 min wall (embed + 55 sequential bridge judge calls).

---

## P2c — sign-off-gated dry-run apply

Turns the reconciled ledger into canonical records — but only a **preview tree**, never the live store, and only behind a hard no-drops accounting gate.

### What's here
- **`canonical/serialize.ts`** — serializer for the additive `status`/`superseded_by`/`merged_from` frontmatter; round-trips through `parseFrontmatter`.
- **`migration/apply/map-claim.ts`** — `claimToCanonical`: ledger claim → `CanonicalRecord` (origin/provenance/capture/confidence by source store, deterministic permalink = slug + `claim_id[:8]`, scope → rootKind/relPath, sensitivity from redaction).
- **`migration/apply/plan.ts`** — `planApply`: realizes decisions via the **disposition-vs-edge** model (ADR 0009). Every claim gets one disposition (`novel`/`merge`); `supersede` is an edge on top. Hard-gates on claim-level no-drops (`complete`/`unaccounted`/`over_disposed`).
- **`scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts`** — reads manifest + ledger, runs `planApply`, **aborts before any write** unless accounting closes *and* matches the manifest stats (incl. the `bearers+collapsed == eligible` identity and a path-collision guard); renders the preview tree + `APPLY-DIFF.md` binding artifact. The only destructive op (`rm -rf` the scratch preview) is guarded by **resolved-path** containment, not string matching.

### ADR 0009 amended (decay-weight supersession)
- Superseded records are **decay-weighted, not hard-filtered** at recall (`semantic × decay × statusWeight × confidenceWeight`); **ACL is the sole hard gate**. A hard `status:active` filter would make superseded records unreachable — defeating the reason to keep them on disk.
- Index/snapshot re-render is **scope-gated by the consolidation watermark** — dormant projects are never re-revised.
- **Deletion of superseded records is allowed via a later human-triggered GC** (grace window), **never during migration** — the one-shot LLM judge is least proven there, so retention keeps it reversible.
- Folds in binary evidence (`binlens` over the CC 2.1.186 native Mach-O) that Claude Code hard-deletes superseded memories and always-loads-then-truncates with no recall decay — the named anti-pattern this contract improves on. CC *does* validate the watermark-gated consolidation design.

### Proven end-to-end (dry-run, no live store touched)
```
2555 claims → 1449 records, 0 dropped (1420 active · 29 superseded) · 1090 quarantined
accounting: complete=true  unaccounted=0  over_disposed=0
routing: 677 global · 772 project across 48 projects
```

### Review
Independent adversarial review (clean-context) found **one blocker — fixed in this PR**: the dry-run write guard was bypassable (`includes("canonical-preview")` + raw `startsWith`, no `path.resolve`), so a mis-set `DREAM_APPLY_PREVIEW` with a `../` traversal could `rm -rf` outside the workspace. Now resolved-path containment + a protected-dir floor (out dir / home / fs root). Also added two reviewer-suggested gates: the manifest-scope identity check and the path-collision guard.

**Follow-ups (non-blocking, tracked here):**
- `migration/apply/plan.ts` — the supersede `newPermalink` fallback is effectively unreachable for a valid manifest; harden to an explicit "resolve to merge canonical, else throw" so a bad manifest fails loudly rather than computing a phantom permalink. Deferred to avoid altering the approved diff in this PR.
- `canonical/serialize.ts` — the hand-rolled YAML-subset escaping handles only `\"`/`\\`; safe for the current ASCII-only fields, revisit if the serializer ever covers free-form values.

### Verification
- `pnpm typecheck` clean (src + the two apply scripts via temp tsconfig).
- New tests: 14 pass (`canonical-serialize.spec.ts` 5 + `migration-apply.spec.ts` 9). P2b's suite: 478 passed / 4 skipped.

---

### Scope (whole PR)
Read-only and **propose-only**: the runner emits a manifest, the apply writes only a scratch preview. **Nothing writes into or deletes from any live store.** The full-ledger sign-off and the real transactional swap into `~/.agents/memory` (+ rollback snapshot + qmd rebuild) are a separate, gated step. **Do not merge until Luke signs off** on the `APPLY-DIFF.md` content (already accepted) and greenlights the merge.

# Land

## Objective

Move approved work from "ready" to landed: run `polish`, babysit checks, merge only with authority, clean docs/notes, and close the session cleanly.

`land` is the OODA **Act** step. Use `deliberate` first when the plan/decision is not approved.

## References

- Post-deploy browser/live smoke check → `references/canary.md`.
- Read-only queue/merge readiness dashboard → `references/landing-report.md`.

## Preconditions

Before acting, confirm:

- scope is clear: changed files, branch/PR, base branch, and owner/repo authority;
- unrelated dirty work is absent or explicitly dispositioned;
- plan/decision is approved, or Luke explicitly asked you to land/merge;
- destructive, public, external, deploy, spend, or data-changing actions have explicit consent.

If approval is missing or the next move is a judgment call, stop and use `deliberate`.

## Workflow

1. **Run `polish` first** — define success criteria, verify artifacts, run selected review lenses (`code-craft`, `autoreview`/`rusty-review`/`codex-review`, `/improve`, optional `/fuse`, adversarial review, `clawpatch`, or domain lenses), track surfaced work, and close local WIP state.
2. **PR/CI babysit** — open/update the PR if needed, push fixes, watch checks, triage failures, and keep looping until green or blocked. Prefer existing repo automation (`/go`, `autofix-pr`, CI links) over hand-rolled polling. Passive waits run in background Bash; fix/triage loops run in a background `Agent(general)`/`autofix-pr`, not foreground `--watch`.
3. **Merge only when authorized** — merge when explicit authority exists and criteria are met. Never merge red, never force-skip required checks, never hide unresolved review threads.
4. **Docs and notes closeout** — after the work lands, revise or delete stale docs/comments/TODOs created or invalidated by the change. Store future work where it belongs: issue, PR follow-up, `plans/`, `docs/`, or project/repo notes — not only chat.
5. **Final work closeout** — run `work-closeout` again after merge: classify remaining dirty files/stashes/branches, preserve WIP with links, clean scratch output where appropriate, and report the final state.

## Success artifact template

Use this in the PR, issue, closeout file, or final reply:

```markdown
## Polish proof
- Success criteria: <pass/fail + proof links>
- Review lenses: <code-craft/autoreview/improve/extra lenses>
- Surfaced work: <durable links or none>

## Landed state
- PR/merge: <link/commit>
- Docs cleaned: <files or n/a>
- Follow-ups: <issue/plan links or none>
- Work closeout: <clean / preserved WIP links>
```

## Stop conditions

Stop and brief Luke when:

- success criteria cannot be measured with available tools;
- CI is red for reasons outside the work or needs credentials/access;
- `polish` finds a ship-blocker that needs scope/priority judgment;
- merge/deploy/release consent is missing;
- future work is real but has nowhere durable to live.

## Final report

Return:

- `Landed` — PR/commit/merge links.
- `Success proof` — criteria + artifacts.
- `Polish proof` — success criteria, artifacts, and review lens results.
- `Docs/follow-ups` — revised docs and durable future-work links.
- `Closeout` — repo cleanliness or preserved WIP.

## P2 reconcile runner + sign-off-gated dry-run apply

Part of the cross-harness memory unification (ADR 0009 / #382). Two commits, one phase:
1. **P2b reconcile runner** — the production caller that produces the sign-off manifest.
2. **P2c dry-run apply** — turns that manifest into canonical records (preview only, gated).

---

## P2b — reconcile migration runner + oversize-cluster guard

P2b (#395) landed the shared reconcile core; this is the **production caller** that wires the real services to it and produces the **sign-off artifact**.

### What's here
- **`scripts/migrate-reconcile.ts`** — loads the live claim ledger across all stores (pi, obsidian, codex, per-project claude-code), embeds via the MLX sidecar (`createHttpEmbedder`), judges over claude-bridge sonnet (`createPiModelJudge`), runs `reconcileLedger`, and writes a propose-only `ReconciliationManifest` + `ledger-claims.jsonl`. A `preview` mode counts/dumps clusters without spending judge calls.
- **`reconcile` core** — new `maxJudgeClusterSize` dep on `reconcileBulk`. Clusters over the cap skip the judge; members fall through to `novel` (kept distinct — **no drop**) and are surfaced via the new `clusters_skipped_oversize` stat. Found running the real corpus: codex episodic session logs form large topically-similar-but-distinct clusters that produce one costly, unreliable judge call.

### Auth note
The judge runs over **claude-bridge** (OAuth), not a direct anthropic key — the `sonnet-class` alias would pick `anthropic/*` (no working key on this machine), so the runner defaults the model override to `claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-4-6` (still honoring `DREAM_RECONCILE_MODEL`). ADR 0009 D3.

### Proven end-to-end on the live corpus
```
2555 claims → 1465 eligible · 1090 quarantined (codex boilerplate sections + 1 oversized)
exact_dup_groups: 0   clusters_judged: 55   clusters_skipped: 3 (oversize, cap=8)
judge_failures: 0
decisions: merge=16  supersede=29  novel=1404
complete: true   unaccounted=0   over_disposed=0
```
~9 min wall (embed + 55 sequential bridge judge calls).

---

## P2c — sign-off-gated dry-run apply

Turns the reconciled ledger into canonical records — but only a **preview tree**, never the live store, and only behind a hard no-drops accounting gate.

### What's here
- **`canonical/serialize.ts`** — serializer for the additive `status`/`superseded_by`/`merged_from` frontmatter; round-trips through `parseFrontmatter`.
- **`migration/apply/map-claim.ts`** — `claimToCanonical`: ledger claim → `CanonicalRecord` (origin/provenance/capture/confidence by source store, deterministic permalink = slug + `claim_id[:8]`, scope → rootKind/relPath, sensitivity from redaction).
- **`migration/apply/plan.ts`** — `planApply`: realizes decisions via the **disposition-vs-edge** model (ADR 0009). Every claim gets one disposition (`novel`/`merge`); `supersede` is an edge on top. Hard-gates on claim-level no-drops (`complete`/`unaccounted`/`over_disposed`).
- **`scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts`** — reads manifest + ledger, runs `planApply`, **aborts before any write** unless accounting closes *and* matches the manifest stats (incl. the `bearers+collapsed == eligible` identity and a path-collision guard); renders the preview tree + `APPLY-DIFF.md` binding artifact. The only destructive op (`rm -rf` the scratch preview) is guarded by **resolved-path** containment, not string matching.

### ADR 0009 amended (decay-weight supersession)
- Superseded records are **decay-weighted, not hard-filtered** at recall (`semantic × decay × statusWeight × confidenceWeight`); **ACL is the sole hard gate**. A hard `status:active` filter would make superseded records unreachable — defeating the reason to keep them on disk.
- Index/snapshot re-render is **scope-gated by the consolidation watermark** — dormant projects are never re-revised.
- **Deletion of superseded records is allowed via a later human-triggered GC** (grace window), **never during migration** — the one-shot LLM judge is least proven there, so retention keeps it reversible.
- Folds in binary evidence (`binlens` over the CC 2.1.186 native Mach-O) that Claude Code hard-deletes superseded memories and always-loads-then-truncates with no recall decay — the named anti-pattern this contract improves on. CC *does* validate the watermark-gated consolidation design.

### Proven end-to-end (dry-run, no live store touched)
```
2555 claims → 1449 records, 0 dropped (1420 active · 29 superseded) · 1090 quarantined
accounting: complete=true  unaccounted=0  over_disposed=0
routing: 677 global · 772 project across 48 projects
```

### Review
Independent adversarial review (clean-context) found **one blocker — fixed in this PR**: the dry-run write guard was bypassable (`includes("canonical-preview")` + raw `startsWith`, no `path.resolve`), so a mis-set `DREAM_APPLY_PREVIEW` with a `../` traversal could `rm -rf` outside the workspace. Now resolved-path containment + a protected-dir floor (out dir / home / fs root). Also added two reviewer-suggested gates: the manifest-scope identity check and the path-collision guard.

**Follow-ups (non-blocking, tracked here):**
- `migration/apply/plan.ts` — the supersede `newPermalink` fallback is effectively unreachable for a valid manifest; harden to an explicit "resolve to merge canonical, else throw" so a bad manifest fails loudly rather than computing a phantom permalink. Deferred to avoid altering the approved diff in this PR.
- `canonical/serialize.ts` — the hand-rolled YAML-subset escaping handles only `\"`/`\\`; safe for the current ASCII-only fields, revisit if the serializer ever covers free-form values.

### Verification
- `pnpm typecheck` clean (src + the two apply scripts via temp tsconfig).
- New tests: 14 pass (`canonical-serialize.spec.ts` 5 + `migration-apply.spec.ts` 9). P2b's suite: 478 passed / 4 skipped.

---

### Scope (whole PR)
Read-only and **propose-only**: the runner emits a manifest, the apply writes only a scratch preview. **Nothing writes into or deletes from any live store.** The full-ledger sign-off and the real transactional swap into `~/.agents/memory` (+ rollback snapshot + qmd rebuild) are a separate, gated step. **Do not merge until Luke signs off** on the `APPLY-DIFF.md` content (already accepted) and greenlights the merge.

https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED

## P2 reconcile migration runner + oversize-cluster guard

Part of the cross-harness memory unification (ADR 0009 / #382). P2b (#395) landed the shared reconcile core; this is the **production caller** that wires the real services to it and produces the **sign-off artifact**.

### What's here
- **`scripts/migrate-reconcile.ts`** — loads the live claim ledger across all stores (pi, obsidian, codex, per-project claude-code), embeds via the MLX sidecar (`createHttpEmbedder`), judges over claude-bridge sonnet (`createPiModelJudge`), runs `reconcileLedger`, and writes a propose-only `ReconciliationManifest` + `ledger-claims.jsonl`. A `preview` mode counts/dumps clusters without spending judge calls.
- **`reconcile` core** — new `maxJudgeClusterSize` dep on `reconcileBulk`. Clusters over the cap skip the judge; members fall through to `novel` (kept distinct — **no drop**) and are surfaced via the new `clusters_skipped_oversize` stat. Found running the real corpus: codex episodic session logs form large topically-similar-but-distinct clusters that produce one costly, unreliable judge call.

### Auth note
The judge runs over **claude-bridge** (OAuth), not a direct anthropic key — the `sonnet-class` alias would pick `anthropic/*` (no working key on this machine), so the runner defaults the model override to `claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-4-6` (still honoring `DREAM_RECONCILE_MODEL`). ADR 0009 D3.

### Proven end-to-end on the live corpus
```
2555 claims → 1465 eligible · 1090 quarantined (codex boilerplate sections + 1 oversized)
exact_dup_groups: 0   clusters_judged: 55   clusters_skipped: 3 (oversize, cap=8)
judge_failures: 0
decisions: merge=16  supersede=29  novel=1404
complete: true   unaccounted=0   over_disposed=0
```
~9 min wall (embed + 55 sequential bridge judge calls).

### Scope
Read-only and **propose-only**: the runner emits a manifest for human sign-off; nothing writes into or deletes from any store. The full-ledger sign-off and the sign-off-gated transactional apply (P2c) follow separately.

### Verification
- `pnpm typecheck` clean; runner script typechecks clean (the 18 pre-existing `scripts/` errors are unrelated and predate this — `scripts/` is excluded from the default tsconfig).
- `pnpm test` — 478 passed / 4 skipped, incl. 2 new tests for the oversize cap (skips above cap, judges at the boundary).

https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED

"@valkyriweb/dream-memory-harness": minor
---

P2c of the cross-harness memory unification (ADR 0009 / #382): the sign-off-gated dry-run apply.

Turns a reconciled ledger into canonical records on disk — but only a *preview* tree, never the live store, until Luke signs off on the diff.

- `canonical/serialize.ts` — frontmatter serializer for the additive `status`/`superseded_by`/`merged_from` fields (round-trips through `parseFrontmatter`).
- `migration/apply/map-claim.ts` — `claimToCanonical`: maps a ledger claim to a `CanonicalRecord` (origin/provenance/capture/confidence by source store, deterministic permalink = slug + `claim_id[:8]`, scope→rootKind/relPath, sensitivity from redaction).
- `migration/apply/plan.ts` — `planApply`: realizes reconciliation decisions as records via the **disposition-vs-edge** model (ADR 0009) — every claim gets one disposition (`novel`/`merge`); `supersede` is an edge layered on top. Hard-gates on the claim-level no-drops accounting (`complete`, `unaccounted`, `over_disposed`).
- `scripts/migrate-apply-dryrun.ts` — reads the manifest + ledger, runs `planApply`, aborts before any write unless the plan accounting closes and matches the manifest stats, renders a preview tree + an `APPLY-DIFF.md` binding artifact (no-drops table + routing + merges/supersedes/novel/quarantine breakdown).

ADR 0009 amended: superseded records are **decay-weighted, not hard-filtered** at recall (ACL is the sole hard gate); deletion of superseded records is allowed via a later human-triggered GC, never during migration. No automated path writes to or deletes from the live store; the transactional apply waits on full-ledger sign-off.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/land

# Land

## Objective

Move approved work from "ready" to landed: run `polish`, babysit checks, merge only with authority, clean docs/notes, and close the session cleanly.

`land` is the OODA **Act** step. Use `deliberate` first when the plan/decision is not approved.

## References

- Post-deploy browser/live smoke check → `references/canary.md`.
- Read-only queue/merge readiness dashboard → `references/landing-report.md`.

## Preconditions

Before acting, confirm:

- scope is clear: changed files, branch/PR, base branch, and owner/repo authority;
- unrelated dirty work is absent or explicitly dispositioned;
- plan/decision is approved, or Luke explicitly asked you to land/merge;
- destructive, public, external, deploy, spend, or data-changing actions have explicit consent.

If approval is missing or the next move is a judgment call, stop and use `deliberate`.

## Workflow

1. **Run `polish` first** — define success criteria, verify artifacts, run selected review lenses (`code-craft`, `autoreview`/`rusty-review`/`codex-review`, `/improve`, optional `/fuse`, adversarial review, `clawpatch`, or domain lenses), track surfaced work, and close local WIP state.
2. **PR/CI babysit** — open/update the PR if needed, push fixes, watch checks, triage failures, and keep looping until green or blocked. Prefer existing repo automation (`/go`, `autofix-pr`, CI links) over hand-rolled polling. Passive waits run in background Bash; fix/triage loops run in a background `Agent(general)`/`autofix-pr`, not foreground `--watch`.
3. **Merge only when authorized** — merge when explicit authority exists and criteria are met. Never merge red, never force-skip required checks, never hide unresolved review threads.
4. **Docs and notes closeout** — after the work lands, revise or delete stale docs/comments/TODOs created or invalidated by the change. Store future work where it belongs: issue, PR follow-up, `plans/`, `docs/`, or project/repo notes — not only chat.
5. **Final work closeout** — run `work-closeout` again after merge: classify remaining dirty files/stashes/branches, preserve WIP with links, clean scratch output where appropriate, and report the final state.

## Success artifact template

Use this in the PR, issue, closeout file, or final reply:

```markdown
## Polish proof
- Success criteria: <pass/fail + proof links>
- Review lenses: <code-craft/autoreview/improve/extra lenses>
- Surfaced work: <durable links or none>

## Landed state
- PR/merge: <link/commit>
- Docs cleaned: <files or n/a>
- Follow-ups: <issue/plan links or none>
- Work closeout: <clean / preserved WIP links>
```

## Stop conditions

Stop and brief Luke when:

- success criteria cannot be measured with available tools;
- CI is red for reasons outside the work or needs credentials/access;
- `polish` finds a ship-blocker that needs scope/priority judgment;
- merge/deploy/release consent is missing;
- future work is real but has nowhere durable to live.

## Final report

Return:

- `Landed` — PR/commit/merge links.
- `Success proof` — criteria + artifacts.
- `Polish proof` — success criteria, artifacts, and review lens results.
- `Docs/follow-ups` — revised docs and durable future-work links.
- `Closeout` — repo cleanliness or preserved WIP.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/go

# /go

Announce at start: **"Using /go. Orchestrating verify → code-review polish → review gate → PR → CI-watch as clean-context subagents."**

You are the **orchestrator**. Phases run as sequential subagents except the review gate, which may fan out into parallel reviewers for non-trivial changes. File-based handoffs live in `./.go-output/`. The arc mirrors a manual ship cycle — clean up the diff, verify it works (surfacing regressions the request didn't ask about), get an independent review, open the PR, then watch CI and fix failures as they land — so the human can hand off the whole loop, not just the build.

`/go` prepares work for PR/CI; it does not merge. Use `land` when the ask is to babysit through merge and close out the session. For read-only merge readiness across a queue after PR prep, use `../land/references/landing-report.md`.

## References

| Phase | Handoff template |
|---|---|
| 1 Verify | `references/phase-1-verify.md` |
| 2 Code Review | `references/phase-2-code-review.md` |
| 3 Review gate | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md`; non-trivial fan-out also uses `references/phase-3-security.md` and `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md`; UI changes also use `references/phase-3-design.md` |
| 4 PR | `references/phase-4-pr.md` |
| 5 CI watch | `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` |

Each handoff is self-contained: the subagent gets the file's contents (with `{{CWD}}` interpolated), reads the artifacts from prior phases, and returns a single-line STATUS.

## File workspace

```
.go-output/
  context.md      # Phase 0 writes — scope, classification, commands
  verify.md       # Phase 1 writes
  slop-scan.md    # Phase 1 writes when slop-scan is available (advisory)
  verify-*.png    # Phase 1 writes (screenshots)
  code-review.md  # Phase 2 writes
  code-craft.md   # Phase 3 writes (## Fixed + ## Follow-ups)
  security.md     # Phase 3 fan-out writes when security review runs
  test-review.md  # Phase 3 fan-out writes when test review runs
  design.md       # Phase 3 fan-out writes when the diff touched UI
  review-gate.md  # Phase 3 synthesis writes
  pr.md           # Phase 4 writes (PR URL + commits)
  ci-watch.md     # Phase 5 writes (CI result + any autofix commits)
```

Create the directory in Phase 0 and add `.go-output/` to `.gitignore` if absent — these are ephemeral.

## Phase 0 — Orchestrator setup

1. Capture scope:
   ```bash
   git status --porcelain
   git diff --stat
   # If tree is clean and commits exist on a branch:
   base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD main)
   git log --oneline "$base"..HEAD
   git diff --stat "$base"..HEAD
   ```
2. **Detect unrelated changes.** Compare the modified files against the user's stated work. Any file that doesn't fit the intent (for example a debug script when the user is shipping CSV export) is unrelated. If unrelated changes exist, halt before writing `context.md` and surface three options to the user: commit them on the current branch, stash them, or move them to a separate branch. Do not dispatch phases until resolved. Phases must never silently sweep unrelated work into the PR.
3. Classify the change as one or more of: `backend-cli`, `web-ui`, `desktop-native`, `refactor`.
   - **Determine `UI-touched`** — the single relevance gate for the Core Web Vitals trace (Phase 1) and the design review (Phase 3). Set `yes` only if the diff changes a rendered UI surface: components/templates/markup (`.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.svelte/.astro/.html/.blade.php`), styles (`.css/.scss/.less`, Tailwind classes), or design tokens. Pure logic, API, config, test, build, or docs changes are `no` — even when the app has a UI. When `no`, Phase 1 skips the CWV trace and Phase 3 skips the design reviewer; never spin up browser/perf tooling for a change that can't move a pixel.
4. Derive project commands from `AGENTS.md` / `README` / `package.json` scripts / nearest config:
   - `TEST_CMD`, `LINT_CMD` (or `none`), `TYPECHECK_CMD` (or `none`), dev-server command if web-ui or backend-cli.
   - `SLOP_SCAN_CMD`: use `npm run review:slop` when present, otherwise `npx slop-scan scan . --lint` for JS/TS repos with `slop-scan` available, otherwise `none`.
5. Scan the user's prompt for context the phases should preserve: flaky-test warnings, known-broken tests on main, infra caveats, reviewer preferences. These go in the `Notes` field of `context.md`.
6. `mkdir -p .go-output` and write `.go-output/context.md`:

   ```markdown
   # /go context
   - Branch: <branch>
   - Base: <base-sha>
   - Classification: <kinds>
   - UI-touched: <yes|no>   # gates CWV trace (Phase 1) + design review (Phase 3)
   - Changed files:
     <list>
   - Test cmd: <cmd>
   - Lint cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Typecheck cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Slop-scan cmd: <cmd-or-none>  # advisory heuristic, not a standalone blocker
   - Dev-server cmd: <cmd-or-na>
   - Summary: <one-line intent suitable for branch slug + PR title>
   - Notes: <anything unusual>
   ```

7. Print: `/go context written: <N> files, classified <kinds>, dispatching verify subagent.`

## Phases 1–4 — Dispatch

For phases 1, 2, 4, and 5, dispatch a subagent with:
- **Prompt** = contents of that phase's reference file with `{{CWD}}` replaced by the absolute working directory.
- **Clean context** — do not carry parent conversation into the subagent.
- **Synchronous** — wait for the subagent to return before dispatching the next phase.

Harness mapping:
- **Claude Code** — `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"`.
- **Pi** — Pi's agent SDK with a fresh context.
- **Codex** — `SendMessage` to a spawned subagent, or Codex's native spawn mechanism.

After each return, read the phase's artifact file and the STATUS line. Apply the early-stop rules below.

### Phase 3 — Review gate with optional fan-out

Before Phase 3, classify whether this is **trivial**. Skip fan-out only if all are true:

- touches 2 files or fewer;
- diff is under 50 changed lines;
- does not touch auth, payments, data access, config, secrets, network boundaries, migrations, CI, deployment, or permissioning;
- Phase 1 found no verification gaps.

If trivial, run only `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` as the code-craft reviewer.

If non-trivial, dispatch these clean-context reviewers in parallel from the orchestrator:

| Reviewer | Prompt |
|---|---|
| Code craft | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` |
| Security | `references/phase-3-security.md` |
| Test engineer | `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md` |

#### Design review step (only when `UI-touched: yes`)

This is a first-class step of the review gate, not an optional extra. The rule is simple: **if `context.md` has `UI-touched: yes`, the design review runs; if `no`, it is skipped entirely.** It is gated on *touching UI*, not on diff size — a change small enough to be "trivial" in code terms (the video's like-button case) can still ship a contrast or layout-shift defect.

When `UI-touched: yes`, dispatch `references/phase-3-design.md` in parallel with the code reviewers above (it runs even when the code change is otherwise trivial). It consumes Phase 1's screenshots + Core Web Vitals and composes the `frontend` skill's `web-design-guidelines` and `taste-skill-anti-slop` references. A `DESIGN-NEEDS-WORK` verdict with unresolved blockers makes the gate `NO-GO`.

When `UI-touched: no`, do not dispatch it and do not load any browser/perf tooling — record `Design review: n/a (no UI surface)` in the synthesis.

Then synthesize their artifacts into `./.go-output/review-gate.md` with:

```markdown
## Decision
GO | NO-GO

## Required fixes before PR
<blockers with source artifact + file:line/evidence>

## Follow-ups
<non-blocking follow-ups>

## Rollback plan
<how to back out safely if this ships badly>
```

If any reviewer reports a blocker, stop before Phase 4 unless the fix is in-scope, applied, and the relevant tests are rerun green.

Before Phase 4 or final handoff, persist non-blocking follow-ups outside `.go-output/`: PR body/comment, GitHub issue, plan doc, repo notes, or the project's existing tracker. `.go-output/` is evidence, not the durable tracking surface.

### Phase 5 — Watch CI and autofix

After Phase 4 opens a PR on GitHub, dispatch `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` as an async CI babysitter and drive the PR to green. Passive CI waits use background Bash; failure interpretation and fix loops use background `Agent(general)` composing `autofix-pr`. Never foreground `gh pr checks --watch` from the orchestrator.

Skip Phase 5 only when:

- Phase 4 returned `PUSHED-NO-PR` (no GitHub PR to watch), or
- the repo has no CI checks (`gh pr checks` reports an empty set after the first poll), or
- the user asked for the PR to stay a draft / explicitly opted out of CI babysitting in their prompt (record in `context.md` Notes).

Phase 5 **never merges**. It stops at green and leaves the merge decision to the human. Unrelated/flaky failures are reported, not force-fixed (see the reference for the prefer-merge-main-over-bloat rule).

## Early-stop rules

- Phase 1 `BLOCKED` → stop. Surface `verify.md` to the user. Do not code-review or PR broken code.
- Phase 2 `BROKE-AND-REVERTED` → continue. The revert restored the green state from Phase 1.
- Phase 3 `NO-GO` or unresolved blocker → stop. Surface `review-gate.md` and the contributing reviewer artifacts.
- Phase 3 `REVIEW-FIXED` with failing tests → the subagent should have reverted; if it didn't, stop before Phase 4 and surface.
- Phase 4 `BLOCKED` → surface the reason (common causes: no `gh` auth, branch protection, dirty tree). Leave retry to the human. Do not run Phase 5 without an open PR.
- Phase 4 `PUSHED-NO-PR` → skip Phase 5 (nothing to watch); surface the remote + branch.
- Phase 5 `CI-RED` after its autofix attempts are exhausted → stop. Surface `ci-watch.md` with the remaining failing checks and their log evidence. Never merge a red PR; never `--no-verify` or force-skip a check to make it look green.

## Orchestrator finish

Print:

```
/go complete.
- Verify: <status>
- Code Review: <status>
- Review gate: <status>
- Design review: <status | n/a (no UI surface)>
- PR: <url>
- CI watch: <status> (green | red — <n> checks | skipped — <reason>)
```

Leave `.go-output/` on disk. The user can delete it when the PR merges. Any follow-ups from `.go-output/` must already be copied to a durable tracker before declaring `/go` complete.

## Guardrails

- If tests are already failing on `main` before /go starts, note it in `context.md`; downstream phases will not claim your change caused or fixed them.
- The human is the final gate. Never auto-merge.

Harness tooling per runtime + rationalizations to resist: `references/harness-notes.md` — read when selecting phase tooling or tempted to shortcut the gate.

Skill history: `references/changelog.md` — read when tracing a design decision.

# Deliberate

## Objective

Run the OODA **Orient → Decide** step: synthesize the current state, identify the real decision, recommend a path, and define exactly what action happens after approval.

This is not the Act step. `deliberate` means: **self-unblock only when the next move is already safe and authorized; otherwise give Luke the relevant information, pros/cons, and recommendation so he can decide.**

## OODA boundary

- **Observe / explore** — gather live evidence: git state, PRs, CI, review output, plans/issues, runtime state, constraints.
- **Orient** — turn evidence into state, target, gap, risk, and blockers.
- **Decide** — present options, pros/cons, recommendation, and the exact next action.
- **Act** — happens only after the plan/decision is completed, reviewed, and approved, or when explicit prior authority already covers the action.

## Workflow

1. **Inventory live state** — check concrete artifacts for the target. Do not rely on memory, stale TODOs, or old plans without verifying them.
2. **Orient the situation**:
   - current state: what is true now;
   - target: what done should look like;
   - gap: what prevents action;
   - constraints: risk, ownership, permissions, timing, cost, taste, business priority.
3. **Classify each item**:
   - `CAN-ACT` — one safe, reversible, clearly correct action exists and is already authorized; do it, verify, and report.
   - `READY-FOR-ACT` — plan/review/approval is complete, but action is external, destructive, public, costly, or merge/deploy shaped; ask or use the explicit approval already given.
   - `DECISION` — multiple valid paths exist and Luke's judgment is needed.
   - `BLOCKED` — missing auth, access, external approval, unavailable service, or unsafe action without consent.
4. **Do not punt fixable work** — if the agent can safely gather missing evidence, fix a local issue, rerun a check, or clarify plan status, do that before asking.
5. **Produce a decision brief** for every remaining `DECISION`/`READY-FOR-ACT` item, ordered by unlock value.

## Action consent

`deliberate` alone is not merge/deploy/destructive consent.

Act only when one of these is true:

- the action is safe, reversible, local, and clearly correct;
- Luke explicitly approved the action in this turn;
- an existing plan/issue/PR says the action is approved, and live gates still match that plan.

For merges, deploys, releases, destructive changes, spend, public replies, or ownership-sensitive calls, treat the result as `READY-FOR-ACT` unless explicit consent is present.

## Decision brief format

Keep it short enough that Luke can answer from a phone:

```markdown
## Decision needed: <one-line question>

State: <what is true now, with artifact links/paths>
Target: <desired end state>
Gap/blocker: <why action should not proceed without a decision>
Plan status: <drafted / reviewed / approved / stale / missing>
Options:
1. <option>
   - Pros: <why choose it>
   - Cons: <risk/cost/tradeoff>
2. <option>
   - Pros: <why choose it>
   - Cons: <risk/cost/tradeoff>
Recommendation: <one option, with why>
If approved: <exact action I will take next>
```

Rules:

- Ask one load-bearing decision at a time unless the choices are independent.
- Provide a recommended default; do not end with "thoughts?".
- Include only evidence that changes the decision.
- Use `bearings` when state itself is unclear.
- Use `polish` when the work needs proof/review, `go` when it needs PR/CI prep, and `land` when it is approved for the Act step.

## Final report

Return four buckets:

- `Acted` — safe/authorized actions completed, with checks.
- `Ready for act` — plan/review/approval state and missing consent, if any.
- `Decision needed` — decision brief(s), ordered by unlock value.
- `Blocked` — exact external ask or missing access.

37	/** Maturity of a fact. Drives whether it may enter the cached core (P5). */
38	export const ConfidenceSchema = z.enum(["extracted", "consolidated", "confirmed"]);
39	
40	/** Lifecycle status (ADR 0009 §4-5). `active` is the only status that enters
41	 * active recall / candidate generation; `superseded` records stay on disk for
42	 * audit/rollback/provenance but are filtered out of the hot path. Default
43	 * `active` so every legacy record and new capture surfaces until something
44	 * explicitly corrects it. No automated path hard-deletes — superseding only
45	 * flips this flag. */
46	export const StatusSchema = z.enum(["active", "superseded"]);
47	
48	export const SourceStoreSchema = z.enum([
49		"pi",
50		"obsidian",
51		"claude-code",
52		"codex-memories",
53		"chronicle",
54	]);
55	
56	export const CaptureMechanismSchema = z.enum(["native", "harvest", "dream", "manual"]);
57	
58	/** Migration/dedup/audit/rollback provenance (spec M2). Content hash + span +
59	 * record id let the claim-level ledger map every source claim exactly once. */
60	export const ProvenanceSchema = z.object({
61		source_store: SourceStoreSchema,
62		source_path: z.string().min(1),
63		// Optional, but when present must be meaningful — an empty hash/span/id would
64		// mislead the P3 dedup ledger.
65		source_span: z.string().min(1).optional(),
66		source_content_hash: z.string().min(1).optional(),
67		source_record_id: z.string().min(1).optional(),
68		migration_batch_id: z.string().min(1).optional(),
69		first_seen: z.string().min(1).optional(),
70		last_seen: z.string().min(1).optional(),
71		capture_mechanism: CaptureMechanismSchema,
72	});
73	export type Provenance = z.infer<typeof ProvenanceSchema>;
74	
75	export const CanonicalFrontmatterSchema = z.object({
76		title: z.string().min(1),
77		permalink: z.string().min(1),
78		origin: OriginSchema,
79		visibility: VisibilitySchema,
80		sensitivity: SensitivitySchema,
81		scope: CanonicalScopeSchema,
82		confidence: ConfidenceSchema,
83		/** Lifecycle (ADR 0009). Defaults to `active`; recall filters on it. */
84		status: StatusSchema.default("active"),
85		provenance: ProvenanceSchema,
86		/** The structured `provenance` above records the *canonical* claim's source.
87		 * When parallel captures are merged, the other members' `claim_id`s are
88		 * recorded here so every source claim stays traceable (ADR 0009 §4 "record
89		 * every source claim_id in provenance") without losing P1's structured shape. */
90		merged_from: z.array(z.string().min(1)).optional(),
91		/** Corrections: permalinks this record supersedes. */
92		supersedes: z.array(z.string().min(1)).optional(),
93		/** Reverse edge: permalink(s) of the record(s) that supersede THIS one. Set on
94		 * the older record at apply; its presence + `status: superseded` is why it
95		 * drops from active recall (ADR 0009 §5). */
96		superseded_by: z.array(z.string().min(1)).optional(),
97		/** Outbound graph edges (the backlink graph). Permalinks this note links to;
98		 * also emitted inline as `[[permalink]]` so Obsidian renders the graph. */
99		links: z.array(z.string().min(1)).optional(),
100		/** Typed soft relations (looser than `links` — "see also"). */
101		relates: z.array(z.string().min(1)).optional(),
102	});
103	export type CanonicalFrontmatter = z.infer<typeof CanonicalFrontmatterSchema>;
